### 1.1  AccountStatements


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Applications:** `AC.STMT.PARAMETER`, `ACCOUNT.STATEMENT`, `ACCT.STMT.PRINT`, `CONDITION.PRIOITY`, `STMT.GEN.CONDITION`, `STMT.PRINTED`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Adv*, *And*, *Fwd*, *Hvt Flag*, *Int*, *Managed by AA*, *Mvmt*, *Print* ... +6 more
> 
> **Sections:** ⚙️ Configuration


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This topic covers the system usage of account statements in Temenos Transact .


##### ConfiguringAC.STMT.PARAMETER

This is a high level parameter application used by the system to create default ACCOUNT.STATEMENT records, when new accounts are opened in the system. Various flags can be set within this record, which is used to determine whether the default ACCOUNT.STATEMENT record is configured to do the following:

- Produce statements when there has been no movement.
- Produce descriptive statements.
- Produce interest and/or charges statements and advices.
- Produce tax advices.
- Calculate the minimum number of months for a statement to be produced if at all.
- Provision to call a local API to populate extra handoff details (mainly to populate sub items in tag 61 and tag 86).

If no record exists, the default value is NO and the minimum frequency is six months. These settings can be overridden in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT record itself.

The Fwd Mvmt Reqd field is used in a value dated account system only. If this field is NO or NULL, then real forward entries with a value date equal or less than the next statement date, which is booked during the statement period alone is reported in the statements. If it is desired that all the real forward entries irrespective of value date booked during the statement period are to be printed in the next statement, then this field has to be set to YES.

- Last statement date is 15/03/2008.
- Next statement date is 31/03/2008.
- Booking date is 15/03/2008 – Value date is 28/03/2008.
- Booking date is 31/03/2008 – Value date is 05/04/2008.

If this field is NO or NULL, then the entry with a value date 28/03/2008 is only reported in the next statement due on the 31/03/2008. However, if this field is set to YES, both the entries are reported in the next statement due on 31/03/2008.

Interest and charges statements can be suppressed through the Int Stmt And Adv field in the AC.STMT.PARAMETER application. The options are YES, NO or NONE.

- YES – Statements are produced regardless of what is input in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT .
- NO and NONE – Statements are not produced in the normal fashion.

> **⚠️ Note:** For any internal account marked with the Hvt Flag as “Yes” during the time of account creation, the system defaults the Stmt Fqu field in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT application to “BSNSS” along with the business date. However, the bank can choose to change the Stmt Fqu field based on their requirement.

The Split Maximum field is used to configure the maximum number of entries after which the record is split and stored in the STMT.PRINTED and ACCT.STMT.PRINT tables. Temenos has released a model record for AC.STMT.PARAMETER with the Split Maximum set as “200”. The bank can either use this configuration from the released record or can choose to define its own configuration.

The screenshot below shows the Split Maximum field configured as 200.


##### ConfiguringSTMT.GEN.CONDITION

When a new ACCOUNT is opened, an ACCOUNT.STATEMENT record specifying the date and frequency for printing account statements is generated automatically by the system. The default frequency is determined by the STMT.GEN.CONDITION application. The STMT.GEN.CONDITION accepts the records with the following frequencies.

- DAILY (every working day)
- WEEKLY
- WEEK2 (will accept two till nine)
- MONTHLY
- TWMTH
- QUARTERLY
- SIX.MONTHLY
- YEARLY

The following screen shot shows the STMT.GEN.CONDITION record for SIX.MONTHLY.

The STMT.GEN.CONDITION application allows the users to define the criteria for which the Print Stmt field is defaulted as NO in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT application. The criteria is defined in the STMT.GEN.CONDITION and it is based on the conditions set in the CONDITION.PRIOITY The Print Stmt field in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT application is set to YES to make any changes in the frequency.


##### ConfiguringACCOUNT.STATEMENT

A record is created automatically in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT application by the system for each new account that is opened. This record controls the date and frequency for printing statements, whether statements are to be printed if there have been no movements and various other statement production options for each account. Defaults are taken from other parameter applications such as the STMT.GEN.CONDITION and AC.STMT.PARAMETER , but these can be overridden by user input in this application. The key to this application is an ACCOUNT number.

Account statements are produced periodically as specified by frequencies in the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT application or online on an ad hoc basis. The following are the SWIFT message types available:

- MT940 – Customer statement
- MT941 – Balance report
- MT942 – Ad hoc statement
- MT950 – Statement

Statements can be produced every working day, for 1-9 weeks, twice a month (on the 15th and the last day of the month) or for 1-12 months (using any day of the month as the anniversary or on the month end date).

Two statement cycles can be specified for each account, for example, weekly and monthly.

These cycles can be independent or combined:

- Separate – Statements for each cycle show the details of all entries since the last statement in the same cycle, regardless of the other cycle.
- Combined – Statements are produced on the dates specified by both cycles, but only contain the details of entries since the last statement from either cycle.

If there have been no entries since the last statement, the statement may be suppressed unless six months have elapsed.

Special interim statements showing the details of all entries since the last regular cycle 1 statement, can be produced any day without affecting the regular statement cycles. When a duplicate or interim statement is produced on request, a charge is applied for the issue of the statement. This charge is usually deferred until the next time the statement is printed in accordance with the statement frequency. The charge is made immediately, together with the production of a debit advice, detailing the charge made when the duplicate statement is produced.

The Managed by AA field specifies whether the ACCOUNT.STATEMENT record belongs to an account created in the legacy AC or AA application. If the defaulted field value is Yes, then the record belongs to an AA account. In such a case, the statement account record cannot be amended manually in ACCOUNT.STATEMENT (for example, frequency cannot be amended manually). However, it can be amended through an OFS string. If the value is blank, the record belongs to an account opened in the AC application and can be amended manually.


> **Related Applications:** `AC.STMT.PARAMETER`, `ACCOUNT.STATEMENT`, `ACCT.STMT.PRINT`, `CONDITION.PRIOITY`, `STMT.GEN.CONDITION`, `STMT.PRINTED`

### 1.2  Daylight Overdraft


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Sections:** 🔧 Working With


#### 🔧 Working With

The following example will be split into 2 days to show how the forecasted exposure is reset with the starting of next business day and how Forecasted Credits are updated with new values.


##### Day 1

In the following scenario, the bank has three TR accounts with a customer. Their opening credit balances and Forecasted Credits on day 1 are listed in the following table:

| Account Reference | Opening Balance | Forecasted Credit (FC) | Sign | Amount |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ac.1 | Cr | 10 | 30 |  |
| Ac.2 | Cr | 30 | 90 |  |
| Ac.3 | Cr | 0 | 100 |  |

Also, overdraft amount (OD), which is the minimum floor amount representing the level of risk exposure the bank accepts regardless of the amount of Forecasted Credits, and the Daylight Overdraft amount (DLOD), which is the maximum ceiling amount representing the maximum level of risk exposure the bank is willing to accept out of the customer’s Forecasted Credits on the SA or TR account level.

| Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 |
|---|---|---|
| Day.1 | OD | 20 |
| DLOD | 50 |  |

When creating the account structure for the customer, the SA is created first, under the designated AA Product for such accounts.

The Act Credit Check field from the BALANCE.AVAILABILITY property must be set to the balance that has been defined for Forecasted Credits in the AC.CREDIT.CHECK application.

The OD and DLOD amounts as well as their currency are defined in the following fields in BALANCE.AVAILABILITY property:

- Cc Com Currency – Represents the currency of both OD and DLOD amounts.
- Cc Com Maximum – Represents the DLOD amount, meaning the maximum ceiling amount consisting the maximum level of risk exposure the bank is willing to accept out of the customer’s Forecasted Credits.
- Cc Com Minimum – Represents the OD amount, meaning the minimum floor amount consisting the level of risk exposure the bank accepts regardless of the amount of Forecasted Credits.

Because the SA is an off-books memo balance account, it has to be marked as such. Therefore, in the ACCOUNT property, the Balance Treatment field must be set to Memo.

The TR accounts can be created under the designated AA Product for such accounts, with the SA set as the parent account. The following screenshot shows a TR1 account:

The BALANCE.AVAILABILITY property is set up similar to the one from the SA account:

Because TRs are on-books balance accounts, in the ACCOUNT property, the Balance Treatment field must be left blank. Also, in the ACCOUNT property, the Parent Link Type field must be set to Exposure. This is done to consolidate the exposure of TR accounts at the SA account level by including the Forecasted Credits in it. The SA maintains total balance of Forecasted Credits as a memo balance in addition to its principal balance.

If the Parent Link Type field is left blank, then only the actual balances of TR accounts is consolidated. The user can set up the Parent Link Type field only when the Parent Account field is also set up, and in the example, this has to hold the reference ID of the SA account.

The Link Type Exception field is associated with the Parent Link Type field and can be set up only if Parent Link Type is set as Exposure. Link Type Exception is a multi-value field which accepts the list of arrangement activities that are exempt from the following Parent Link Type configurations. This means that all the activities mentioned here will follow the default method of aggregating balances to the SA account, by aggregating to it the entire transaction amount.

Accounts TR2 (reference 10014739903) and TR3 (reference 10014739904) are created with the same properties as TR1. Account TR1 (reference 10014739902) opening credit balance is 10, as viewed in the ACCOUNT and ECB applications:

Account TR2 (reference 10014739903) opening credit balance is 30, as viewed in ACCOUNT and ECB applications:

Account TR3 (reference 10014739904) has an opening balance of 0.

Activities are created to update the Forecasted Credit balances of TR accounts:

- Forecasted Credits balance update of 30 on TR1 account:

- ECB record of TR1 account is updated with the new balance:

- ECB record of SA account is also updated:

- Forecasted Credits balance update of 90 on TR2 account:

- ECB record of TR2 account is updated with the new balance:

- ECB record of SA account is also updated (30 from TR1 + 90 from TR2):

- Forecasted Credits balance update of 100 on TR3 account:

- ECB record of TR3 account is updated with the new balance:

- ECB record of SA account is also updated (30 from TR1 + 90 from TR2 + 100 from TR3):

| Transaction Account | Transaction Sign | Transaction Amount | Offset FC | Position Before Transaction | Transaction Status | Account Level | GEMS Level | Impact on GEMS | Account Level | GEMS Level | Account Running Balance | DLOD Vs FC | DLOD Vs OD (IDL Final) | Available Balance + IDL | IDL Utilised | DLOD Vs FC | DLOD VS OD (IDL Final) | IDL Available |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ac.1 | Dr | 30 |  | 10 | 30 | 30 | 40 | 0 | 50 | 50 | 50 | -20 | PASS | PASS |  |  |  |  |
| Ac.2 | Dr | 20 |  | 30 | 50 | 50 | 80 | -20 | 50 | 50 | 30 | 0 | PASS | PASS |  |  |  |  |
| Ac.1 | Dr | 40 |  | -20 | 30 | 30 | 10 | -20 | 50 | 50 | 30 | -40 | DISPO | DISPO |  |  |  |  |
| Ac.2 | Dr | 25 |  | 10 | 50 | 50 | 60 | -60 | 50 | 50 | -10 | -15 | PASS | DISPO |  |  |  |  |


##### Day 2

Considering the same three accounts for the same customer, these are their opening balances for day 2 based on the previous day’s transactions and their new Forecasted Credits based on future known transactions:

| Account Reference | Opening Balance | Forecasted Credit (FC) | Sign | Amount |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ac.1 | Dr | 60 | 100 |  |
| Ac.2 | Cr | 15 | 100 |  |
| Ac.3 | Cr | 0 | 40 |  |

| Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 |
|---|---|---|
| Day.2 | OD | 50 |
| DLOD | 400 |  |

To reflect the Forecasted Credits amounts (mentioned in the table) in the accounts, the user needs to update them by crediting what is missing:

- TR1 account had FC = 30 in day 1. So, in day 2, the user credits another 70 FC to it to reach 100; the user does this by creating an activity to update the Forecasted Credits balance of the account:

- TR2 account had FC = 90 in day 1. So, in day 2, the user credits another 10 FC to it to reach 100; the user does this by creating an activity to update the Forecasted Credits balance of the account:

- TR3 account had FC = 100 in day 1. So, in day 2, the user debits the FC balance for 60 to reach 40; the user does this by creating an activity to update the Forecasted Credits balance of the account:

### 1.3  AA-IF

#### 📖 Introduction

Transact Design Studio can be used for defining the exit points and the associated data flows for integration events for a Temenos Transact application or version.

The fields(Transact core or a local field) from the application can be extracted and the data can be included in the user-defined flow in the integration event. The flow can be made to include additional information from other tables using the integration event synchronous enrichment.

At run time, the system extracts the details pertaining to the business event that has an exit point defined.

Read Integration Framework Designer for more details on the integration framework setup.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

AA is a structured product, each Event (Business flow) is identified based on Activities. Each activity comprises of multiple Properties related with it. Hence the Exit Point has to be configured based on Activity Class or Activity.

As arrangement activity transactions are well-defined business activities which contain multiple properties and linked applications, Integration Framework(IF) supports the events with data from the entire arrangement activity transaction context which include:

- Arrangement Activity
- Child Properties
- Linked Applications

IF can access data definitions at design time and transaction data at runtime from AA.


##### Exit Point Type - AA Activity

The Integration Designer handles the exit point type based on Activity Class/Activity, at the same level as the exit point types for Application, Version, and Component Service, TSA service or Delivery.

The Designer introspects Transact AA and gathers the list of product groups, products, conditions, attributes and activities available from AA. These are displayed as selectable lists in Integration Designer.

In the screenshot below, the exit point is defined for an Activity at the arrangement input stage for a lending product line-Mortgages Product Group.

The user can define the stage where the actual data needs to be extracted since each application has its own flow .This stage is designed using the Event Designer. To define the exit points and the associated data flows, for any application or version in Transact, the Transact Design Studio for integration events is used.

AA is a structured product, each event (business flow) is identified based on activities. Each activity can comprise of multiple properties .Hence the exit point needs to be configured based on activity.

Further, the Activity definition is different for each product and the properties attached to it. Hence while choosing an AA exit point, the product must be selected.

When the Product Group is selected, the list of products available are displayed as a dropdown and can be chosen from the list. Upon selection of a Product, the list of activities corresponding to product get displayed.

In the screenshot below, the AA Flow tab defines the Event input. The product line, product group and product are chosen. Here for the AR.SAVINGS.PARENT, the ACCOUNTS-NEW-ARRANGEMENT Activity Class is selected. The property or application can be further chosen from the list available in the dropdown.

> **⚠️ Note:** When the product is selected, the corresponding Activity class / Activity that belong to this product is listed. Activity Class / Activity is the final list chosen as an exit point . The user has to select either the Activity Class or Activity, not both.

Based on the Activity/Activity class that is selected, the system displays the Properties related to this Activity.

The fields are displayed in a Field selection box and can be added to the Flow Definition list.

A list of applications which can be used for the definition of the exit points is retrieved from the Transact data and is fixed for all activities. They are:

- AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY
- AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS
- AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY
- AA.BILL.DETAILS
- AA.CHARGE.DETAILS
- AA.SCHEDULED.ACTIVITY
- AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS
- AA.OVERDUE.STATS
- AA.CUSTOMER.ARRANGEMENT
- AA.AGENT.COMMISSSION.DETAILS
- AA.AGENT.EVENT
- AA.ARRANGEMENT
- ACCOUNT
- CUSTOMER

At the beginning of the AA activity, the core system requests IF for any exit points defined at the activity level. IF returns the list of exit points and data flows defined.

When the activity is processed, the required data (pre and post) is captured by the core image management system (image here implies a copy of data maintained in core).

At the end of activity, the captured information needs to be handed over to IF. The image should be extracted only if the corresponding details are available in the transaction boundary, that is, though the Property / Application is added at design time, the corresponding Property image has to be extracted if the corresponding property action(I-Input or M-Maintain ) is executed by this activity.

Application images are extracted only if the corresponding application date is updated (a write to data base) by this activity.

> **⚠️ Note:** The CUSTOMER , ACCOUNT , ARRANGEMENT applications are exceptions, as these table images are extracted without having to update (without a write to data base).


##### Condition Data Flow

The data flow may have conditions for data collection. These are defined in a separate tab.

In AA Exit Point, which contains more than one application associated with one exit point, the Condition Data Collection(CDC) is used to filter the unwanted records for an application based on user-defined conditions.

Read about the Event and Flow Designer here as it is similar to the Exit points defined earlier.

The user has to define the stage where the actual data needs to be extracted since each application has its own flow. This stage is designed using the Event Designer. The activity differs for each product based on the property used. Hence while choosing an AA exit point, the product should be selected. Upon selection of a product, the list of activities corresponding to product get displayed.


###### Flow Designer

Based on the Activity/Activity class that is selected, the system displays the Property. The fields to be extracted from the property/applications are also selected.

| Action | Description |
|---|---|
| Ignore Record | If the condition fails the particular record needs to be ignored |
| Ignore Event If Any Fail | For the condition, any one of record fails then no need to emit the message |
| Ignore Event If All Fail | For the condition, all records are failed then no need to emit the message |

During runtime, once all the data is collected the corresponding conditions are executed. Based on the result of the condition, the particular record or entire exit points are ignored.


##### Custom Application

AA Activity Exit point is linked to an Activity Class or Activity. If a user tries to set up the exit point from an Activity / Activity Class, then it only allows restricted applications and Properties, which are related to the Activity or Activity class. Here, core provides an option to add Non-Related (application not updated using this exit point) application or local customized applications into the AA Integration extraction.

| Field Name | Functionality |
|---|---|
| Element Name | Gives meaningful mnemonic which is the primary key of the definition. It has to be a valid alphanumeric. Example: If it is related to Arrangement Property then it is Property Name. During design time, the system displays all this element name with prefix as CUSTOM alone with core derived Properties/Applications in Design Studio Flow Designer tab. |
| Application Name | Indicates a valid Transact application name related to this element. Upon clicking the element in the Design studio the related fields are derived based on this application. |
| Nau Suffix | Indicates unauthorized application suffix for the application. Allowed values are: $NAU, .NAU and .WORK |
| Data Collection Hook | Sets the corresponding element's pre and post image records to be handed over to the integration framework (IF) for processing. During arrangement activity post processing it passes all records modified for the corresponding application within the current transaction. The hook implementer can either select the records applicable to the element from the passed application records or get the element data from a related table. If the record is not passed by this hook, then the corresponding element record is not extracted. This option causes performance issue because mostly it reads data from the database DB. Care should be taken at the implementation stage. |
| Filter | Filters the supplied elements returning only those elements which are required for this arrangement activity integration framework exit point. The incoming elements consist of all those elements defined in the AA.CLASS.APPL.CONDITION record Customer Property Class and the implementer must filter the elements related to the Activity Class, Activity and Property The hook is invoked while designing an arrangement activity exit point, it takes all the elements defined in the AA.CLASS.APPL.CONDITION record and the filtered elements are output to an IF.INTEGRATION.FLOW.CATALOG record. |


##### AA Component Exit Point

The AA Activity Extractor service is used to generate an integration event for any AA transaction. For example, consider TAP with Transact where AA allows TAP to be fed by the TTI B2F interface. IF is used for integrating TAP with Transact. There are several flows and events being monitored by TAP on Transact using IF.

The data records required for TAP cannot be directly obtained from version level while performing the activity (Transaction). In the AA API, the data is assembled as the last part of the routine (simple component routine written using component framework). The data assembled is passed as input parameters to the component routine .An IF event attached to the component routine extracts input parameter as a XML message . In IF Run time, whenever the component routine is called it results in an XML message generated. (It has to be ensured that AA API is linked to activity API).

The flow is as follows:

Consider a user has created a new loan contract.

1. The API routine (AA.TAP.EXTRACT.ARR.DETAILS) attached in the ACTIVITY API runs as an assembly routine which collects the data .
2. Once the data is collected ,it calls the component routine.
3. IF EVENT is called only if design time setup is available .
4. IF XML message is generated with the data that is collected from AA API.
5. The Integration service picks the generated XML message and passes it to TAP system

Click here to see the AA Component Exit Points.

From AA, all the required attribute information are collected by AA.TAP.EXTRACT.ARR.DETAILS method/routine. This routine needs to be attached into the required activities to extract information via IF component exit point. The AA.TAP.EXTRACT.ARR.DETAILS method needs to be attached as post routine and AA.TAP.EXTRACT.PRE.ARR.DETAILS needs to be attached as pre-routine. The Property Class and Action needs to be attached into the last most active property class and action on the corresponding activity class.


###### Exclusion

- AA Extracted service contains only TTI related information. Other than those attribute needs to be added then it should be an enhancement.
- Portfolio should be the pre-requisite to extract the information from AA.
- All the information is extracted during the authroisation stage only.

>

#### 📖 Introduction

Statement Property Class is used to specify the account level statement settings such as Stmt Frequency , Start Date , No Activity Indicator etc. For arrangements without Statement Property Class, the Account Statement functionality continues.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This topic helps the user to configure the Statement property class and the PRINT.STATEMENT application.


##### Account Statement and Passbooks

Banks can choose to generate account statements on a regular basis or can give the customer a choice to have passbook updates. These options are mutually exclusive.

To enable Passbook facility in an Account Product:

- Account Product Category has to be included in the SAVINGS record of the ACCOUNT.CLASS application.
- Passbook field has to be set as Yes in the Arrangement Account.

To generate account statements,

- The fields in ACCOUNT.STATEMENT records are defaulted from the STMT.GEN.CONDITION and AC.STMT.PARAMETER applications. Read Account Statements section in Account user guide for more information.
- Account Statement Conditions can be updated using Statement Property Class in Product.


##### Account Statement Conditions

This topic explains the attributes of Statement Property Class and the configuration options are explained in this topic.


##### Statement preferred date and frequency

Statements can be produced:

- On all working days
- For 1-9 weeks
- Twice a month (on the 15 th and the last day of the month)
- For 1-12 months (using any day of the month as the anniversary or on the month end date)

The Statement - 1 Frequency 1 field specifies the start date and frequency for producing the regular (cycle 1) account statement. Statement of each cycle shows the details of all entries since the last statement in the same cycle regardless of other cycles. This value can be defaulted based on the customer preferences setup in DE.CUSTOMER.PREFERENCES . Customer Preferences also specify customer level delivery preferences like Print, Email, SMS or Secure Message (each of which translates into a Carrier in Temenos Transact Delivery Module) for different types of statements or advices.

In case of Joint owners, the defaulting is based on the values given for the first customer set up as the Beneficial Owner .

The Statement - 1 Frequency 1 field can be sub-valued to give other specific dates in a month for recurring statement generation. In this case, entries from the last statement date in cycle 1 are printed for each sub-valued date.

The Statement - 1 Frequency 2 field specifies the start date and frequency for producing the account statement for additional statement cycles (2 to 9). The field in this cycle can also be sub-valued as mentioned in cycle 1.

Frequency Supported:

- Daily
- Weekly
- Monthly
- Defined


##### Options Available in Account Statement

This section helps the user to configure the fields under Account Stmt tab.

The Detailed Statements include the details of the account movements and generating a detailed statement is optional. When the Detailed Statement field is set to Yes, the Account Statement includes details of the movements, else, the summary information alone is updated.

The If No Movement field in Statement property class specifies whether the Cycle 1 statements should be printed and if there have been no movements over the account since the last statement.

The options in this field are:

- Yes - Statements are produced on the dates specified, regardless of whether or not there have been any movements.
- No - Mentions if there are no movements since last statement and the statement is suppressed.
- No if zero Balance - Mentions if the account has no movements during the statement period and the ledger balance is zero and the statement is suppressed.

Special Statements can be set for multiple dates so the user can specify the unique set of dates upfront in specific frequency.

To have fixed set of unique statement dates instead of the regular frequency, the Follow Spl Stmt field should be set to Yes. The regular statements get discontinued and printed on specified unique dates.

Special Statements can be suppressed if account has zero balance and no movement in statement period.

The Print Attribute Name/Value associated fields given below in Statement Property Class enable the user to print the statements with or without images.

- Printing Option
- Statement Image

The Attribute Name is set at the product condition level and can be made non-negotiable at the arrangement level so the user or the customer can change only the Attribute Value from the options available. These are passed along with the statement output to be sent to a downstream system such as printing solution. These values can be defaulted based on the customer preferences setup in DE.CUSTOMER.PREFERENCES . In case of joint owners, the system defaults based on the values given for the first customer set up as Beneficial Owner .


##### Account Statement Format

Account statement format can vary depending on the product requirement.

- PRINT.STATEMENT holds the definition of the formatting enquiry or API used to produce the statement output.
- The Next Enquiry is a multi-value field used to define a different Account Format Enquiry in Print Statement.
- Besides the main formatting enquiry, additional enquiries can be specified in the Next Enquiry field. This includes additional information such as Rate Change history. This enquiry format is always included in the account statement.
- Different PRINT.STATEMENT definitions can be processed at various instances of the statement service.
- When the Refer to Product field in Print Statement is set to Yes, the statement generation process picks up the appropriate Statement Type and Add-ons from the arrangement or product configuration. For the System record and any default definitions used for Combined Statement process, the Refer to Product field has to be set Yes.
- The Allowed Addon field is used when setting up Statement Types and Statement product condition. Statement Types - This Allowed Addon field can be set with the list of Allowed Add-Ons for that Statement Type. Statement product condition - Once a Statement Type is specified, the user can then specify the Statement Add On . The system validates if Statement Add On specified is actually an Allowed Addon for that Statement Type .
- The Addon New Page field can be set to either Yes or No to indicate if the associated Add on output has to be printed in a new page or as a continuation on the same page.
- The Format field in the PRINT.STATEMENT application is used to attach the AA.NARRATIVE enquiry for a descriptive narrative for the transaction posted in the account statements. Read Configuration for Statement Narrative for more information.


##### Interest Statements

A detailed interest statement (scale) is produced for an arrangement when the Interest Scale field in the statement condition is set to Y. Details such as the interest rate applied for the specified period, along with the accrual information can be obtained from the interest statement generated. On setting Interest Scale as Y, if the same interest properties are defined in the statement condition as well as in the payment schedule condition, then the system produces two statements for these interest properties. The system raises an override to indicate the same : “Statement would get generated both on schedule date and the date defined in statement condition for ”.

The Interest Closing Advice field if set to Y, generates an advice when the interest and charges are applied for an arrangement.

Interest Statements can be produced during COB on the given frequency for the specified properties. The set of associated multi-valued fields such as Stmt Frequecny , Stmt Name and Property indicate the frequency to generate interest statements. The relevant activity has to be generated in the ACCOUNTS-PRODUCE-STATEMENT*AA.PROPERTY format. Activity Messaging completes the setup of mapping the Produce Statement Activity with relevant EB.ADVISE (AA-2022)

Stmt Info Property indicates the Property for which Rate Change has to be recorded. The corresponding enquiry is added in a PRINT.STATEMENT record and linked as Allowed Addon in PRINT.STATEMENT of the account. It is possible to print the Addon in a new page using Addon New Page as Y.

##### Combined Statements

Combined Statement is the consolidation of individual statements supported by a Summary page per account.

- Combined Statements can be set up at the account level based on the customer choice.
- Customers can choose the lead accounts with participant accounts under them. Accounts here refer to financial arrangements including Loans, Deposits, Accounts and AA External Plus Arrangements Every arrangement has an underlying account number. Hence, all the references to account numbers also include the various types of financial arrangements.

The generation of combined statements is applicable only for print carrier.


##### Charges for Statement Generation

Statements can be generated using PRINT.STATEMENT in Temenos Transact . When a statement is generated, it raises a RECORD.EVENT Activity on the arrangement and then the system generates - PRODUCE-STATEMENT.

Charges for account statement are assessed and collected immediately or as a part of the Periodic Charges (frequency is also configured).

Using the Configuration in Charge, Activity Charges and Periodic Charges Property Classes, Charges can be set up on Statements as shown below:

- Statement Charge can be defined either per Statement as a Unit Charge or Free Statements, and as a Charge above a certain number.
- Calculation or Assessment of Charges has to be done either when the Statement is produced or as a part of the Service Charge.
- Posting or Collection of Charges has to be done either when the Statement is produced or as a part of the Service Charge on the Service Charge cycle date It is also possible to calculate the charges when the statement is produced but deferred to be collected as part of the Service Charge.


###### Aligning Interest and Charges on Statement Dates

Relative Date option R_STATEMENT can be used to schedule the interest and charges in line with the statement dates.

- It is a relative date set based on statement date and frequency set for the Statement Cycle 1
- It enables to align payment frequency of interest and charges in-line with statement date.

When the statement condition is defined on the last day of every three months (quarterly) and the Payment Schedule has the start date set to R_STATEMENT without a frequency, the payment schedule is aligned to the statement frequency.

Statement condition: Quarterly

Payment Schedule condition: Aligning to statement

Charge and Interest are scheduled on the same date as account statement is shown below.


##### Multiple Owners

It is possible to set the choice of account statements for multiple owners using AA Customer Role.

When a new arrangement is created, the Delivery Customer attribute in AA.CUSTOMER.ROLE is defaulted into the Delivery Required attribute of Customer Property. Read AA Customer Role for more details.

#### 📖 Introduction

Banks might require a unique identification number for the arrangements across the Product Lines. Alternate ID attribute in arrangement is unique across all Product Lines and across all Temenos Transact Companies. If Alternate ID has been set for an Arrangement, it can then be used in the place of Arrangement reference.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Unlike other Temenos Transact applications where the underlying database table and the application that acts on it are the same (example, CUSTOMER ), it is AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY that is used to act upon AA.ARRANGEMENT .

Set up EB.ALTERNATE.KEY (released by Temenos) as shown below:

- The Alternate ID attribute (which is both in AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY and AA.ARRANGEMENT ) is used to configure the Alternate Key definition.
- The definition for AA.ARRANGEMENT is linked to the Alternate Key definition for AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY .
- It is important to have the uniqueness of this key to be ‘System’ to make sure that the alternate ID is unique not just within the Temenos Transact company but also across the companies in that Temenos Transact installation.
- The alternate ID can be captured during New-Arrangement, TakeOver-Arrangement activities and subsequently maintained using the purpose built Amend.Alt.ID-Arrangement activity.
- The alternate ID becomes effective upon authorisation of the activity.


#### 📋 Tasks

Alternate IDs are typically used for accounts. Each of these account systems are specified in Temenos Transact and for accounts, which are taken over the alternate account ID specific to the previous system will be specified at the arrangement level.

The Alternate ID attribute in arrangement is unique across all product lines and Temenos Transact companies. Any alternate account systems defined in the ACCOUNT.PARAMETER application is defaulted to allow maintenance of the alternate account system.

### 1.6  Archival Process


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Long term arrangements can accumulate and persist large volumes of data in the Online Transactional Processing (OLTP) database until the end of its life cycle. The user can archive both closed and live arrangements. These arrangements are examples in which a subset of the AA tables can be archived e...*
> 
> **Applications:** `.HIST`, `AA.ACTIVE.ARRANGEMENT.CONCAT`, `AA.ACTIVITY`, `AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY`, `AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY.HIST`, `AA.ARR.<PROPERTY>`, `AA.ARRANGEMENT`, `AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY` ... +7 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Act Retain Period*, *Act Threshold Period*, *Activity Type*, *Arc
 Latest Effective Date*, *Arc Filename*, *Arc Last Effective Date*, *Arc Latest Effective
 Date*, *Arc Latest Effective Date* ... +20 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Long term arrangements can accumulate and persist large volumes of data in the Online Transactional Processing (OLTP) database until the end of its life cycle. The user can archive both closed and live arrangements. These arrangements are examples in which a subset of the AA tables can be archived even for live arrangements. Using Data Lifecycle Management (DLM) based archiving, the records in the following applications can be archived:

- AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY
- AA.PROCESS.DETAILS
- AA.ARR.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Data Lifecycle Management (DLM) is a capability that makes use of non-volatile database technology, time-based partitioning, and configurable data transfers to move aged data out of the system’s live database into a non-volatile database before purging it from the live database. It enables the banks to minimise the size of their system’s live database and control its growth while maintaining easy access to data. As a result, scalability is preserved, and the mean-time-to-recover is reduced.

Once the aged data is moved to a read-only database, then the system framework provides the flexibility to access the data either from the live or the read-only database anytime. Read Data Life Cycle Management for more information about the DLM module.

The archiving process examines the files for records to be archived, writes the selected records (and any associated records) to a Read-Only (RO) database, and deletes the records from the live database. The archive parameters like Purge Date , Retention Period , Archive Data , and so on can be configured in the ARCHIVE application.

- Purge Date – Archives the records older than purge date.
- Retention Period - Archives the records older than the retention period. When both Purge Date and Retention Period are set, the system refers only the date specified in Purge Date for archival of records.
- Archive Data – When this field is configured as: Yes – Moves the records from live to read-only database. No – Deletes records from the live database during archival.

Banks can define specific conditions (parameters) for archival processing, that are unique to specific ARCHIVE records only. The Attribute Type and Attribute Value fields in the ARCHIVE application can be configured for this purpose. When these fields are set, the system does not consider the default selection criteria.

- For example, during the archival of closed arrangements, if the number closed arrangements is a huge list, then the bank may choose to drip feed the list of arrangements that must be archived on a given day. This can be achieved by sending the list of closed arrangement records manually using the Attribute Type and Attribute Value fields. The user must create a local file with the list of closed arrangements to be archived on a given day. The name of this local file with the list of closed arrangements must be defined in the Attribute Value field and the Attribute Type field must be set as Alt.sel.file. This file name should be defined in the Archive Id field of the ARC.GENERIC.REQUEST application. When the ARC.GENERIC service is run, the system archives the list of closed arrangements from the file mentioned in the Attribute Value field.

Read ARC.GENERIC.REQUEST section in Full Solution Implementation for more information.


##### Archival of Closed Arrangements

The AA.ARRANGEMENT record in the ARCHIVE application holds the definition for closed arrangement’s archival process. Depending upon the requirement, the bank can specify the Retention Period or Purge Date and Archive Data attributes in this record for archival of closed arrangements. Based on this definition, the system selects the closed arrangements using Arr Status (=CLOSE) attribute, where Closed Date is less than the retention period or the purge date for archival.

The process below is followed for archival of closed arrangements.

1. Closed Date in AA.ARRANGEMENT holds the closure date of the arrangement. The system updates the closure date of the arrangement in Closed Date attribute at the time of closure.
2. The AA Archive Process selects the closed arrangements based on Arr Status (=CLOSE) for which Closed Date is less than the purge date or the retention period for archival. After the upgrade, when the archival process is run, the process verifies the selected closed arrangements for Closed Date . If Closed Date is not found in AA.ARRANGEMENT (for arrangements, which were closed prior to the introduction of the Closed Date attribute), the archival process refers either -CLOSE-ARRANGEMENT or -CLOSE.OFFER-ARRANGEMENT activity’s effective date in AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY and updates the Closed Date field in AA.ARRANGEMENT .
3. Next, the arrangements for which Closed Date is less than the retention period or purge date, are considered for archival.

- The Arc Filename attribute is auto-populated with a list of all files to be archived relevant to the specific implementation and use of AA products. If the attribute is cleared of all current values and the record is committed, then this attribute is automatically populated as explained with relevant AA tables.
- For the archival of closed arrangements, the arrangements should be in CLOSE status.


##### Archival of Live (Open) Arrangements

The AA Archiving process is available for live arrangements and not limited to archiving data of closed arrangements only. This means, long term arrangements like those of Account products continue to accumulate and persist large volumes of aged data in the OLTP database till the end of the lifecycle before they can be archived.

To enable archiving of aged data of open arrangements, the system archives the following subset of AA tables for active open arrangements as well.

- AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY
- AA.PROCESS.DETAILS
- AA.ARR.

The screenshot illustrates the archival process of the live arrangements.

During the lifecycle, every activity is stored in AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY and the references of all such AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY records except the NOLOG and RESTRICTLOG types are maintained in the AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY table. This has the arrangement reference as the key (that is, one record per arrangement) that grows over the lifecycle of the arrangement. To maintain an optimal size, the records of AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY are split and moved to the AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY.HIST table periodically based on the definition of Archive Activities , Retain Activities , Act Threshold Period , and Act Retain Period attributes in AA.PARAMETER . A separate service that continuously runs in the background in AUTO mode manages this split.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Archive Activities | The user can specify threshold value for activities that needs to be moved from AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY to AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY.HIST . When the count of activities reaches the threshold value, the system moves the records to AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY.HIST during close of business (COB) or during online service processing. |
| Retain Activities | The user can specify the count of activities that needs to be retained while moving the records from AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY to AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY.HIST . This is to ensure that the AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY table is not completely empty. |
| Act Threshold Period | The user can specify the threshold period. When the threshold period has reached, the system moves the records from AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY to AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY.HIST during close of business (COB) or during online service processing. |
| Act Retain Period | The user can specify a period in this attribute. While moving the activities from AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY to AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY.HIST , the activities triggered during this period are retained. |

In case both Archive Activities and Act Threshold Period attributes are defined,

- The system refers Act Threshold Period first and if records have breached the definition, these are moved to the .HIST table. If the records have not breached the threshold, based on the Act Threshold Period definition, then the system refers to the Archive Activities attribute, and the records are moved to the .HIST table.

Depending upon the definition in AA.PARAMETER (to archive or retain the activities in AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY ), the system periodically moves the records from AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY to AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY.HIST table when the COB (AA.ARCHIVE.SERVICE) or online (AA.AH.ARCHIVE.SERVICE) service is run. While AA.AH.ARCHIVE.SERVICE archives only the AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY to .HIST , AA.ARCHIVE.SERVICE archives bill details, interest accruals, account details, and activity history records to their corresponding .HIST table.

The AA.ACTIVE.ACTIVITIES record in the ARCHIVE application deals with the archival of the AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY and AA.PROCESS.DETAILS tables for active arrangements.

The Archive Data attribute in AA.ACTIVE.ACTIVITIES record in the ARCHIVE application , must be set to Yes otherwise the archiving process deletes the records instead of archiving them.

AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVTY and AA.PROCESS.DETAILS archival selection is only applicable for records present in the AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY.HIST table.

- The Latest Effective Date attribute in AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY.HIST and AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY tables holds the effective date of the latest activity from the list of activity references in the record.
- This value is updated whenever AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY or AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY.HIST is created or updated.

Depending upon the Purge Date or Retention Period definition of the AA.ACTIVE.ACTIVITIES record in the ARCHIVE application, the AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY and AA.PROCESS.DETAILS records referenced in the AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY.HIST records are archived from the live database and moved to a read-only database if Latest Effective Date in the AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY.HIST table is older than the Purge Date or the Retention Period . Arc Last Effective Date attribute is updated in the records processed in the AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY.HIST table with the oldest activity's effective date and the same is further used as a base for active properties and active concat file archival process.

Consider an active arrangement, where a list of activities trigger dates in a chronological order as below:

- 30-Mar-23
- 31-Dec-22
- 30-Sep-22
- 30-Jun-22
- 31-Mar-22
- 31-Dec-21
- 30-Sep-21
- 30-Jun-21
- 31-Mar-21
- 31-Dec-20
- 30-Sep-20
- 31-Jul-20
- 30-Jun-20
- 10-Jun-20
- 05-Apr-20
- 01-Apr-20
- 31-Mar-20
- 01-Jan-20

The current system date is Apr 1, 2023, and the below records are present in AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY.HIST .

The records in AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY are:

When the archival service is executed on the Apr 1, 2023 with Purge Date defined as Jun 30, 2020, the system refers the AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY.HIST table and selects records, where the latest effective date is less than Jun 30,2020. Thus, the AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY records referenced in #1 are moved to a read-only database and deleted from the live database. Arc Latest Effective Date is updated as Jan 1, 2020 in the #1 record of AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY.HIST . All other # records in AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY.HIST are not considered for archival processing since Latest Effective Date is greater than Purge Date .

Arc Latest Effective Date is updated as Jan 1, 2020 in the AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY.HIST record as part of this archiving. This is further used as a base for property and concat files archival.

> **⚠️ Note:** For an upgrade scenario and in case of older records (activities triggered prior to the introduction of Latest Effective Date ), the system updates the Latest Effective Date field in the AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY.HIST table at the time of archival.

The AA.ACTIVE.PROPERTIES record in the ARCHIVE application deals with the archival of property records. The bank can specify the Retention Period or Purge Date and Archive Data attributes in AA.ACTIVE.PROPERTIES record in the ARCHIVE application, to archive property related records for active arrangements.

The Max Backdated Period attribute controls the maximum days up to which an activity can be back-dated. The user can specify NND or NNM or NNY in the Max Back Dated Activity attribute, where NN is the number of days or months or years. This value is compared against the effective date of a property condition record to identify and archive records that can no longer be modified. Purge Date configured in AA.ACTIVE.PROPERTIES record should be older than the date derived from the configuration in the Max Back Dated Activity attribute.

Consider a AA.ACTIVE.PROPERTIES record

- Purge Date – Mar 31, 2015
- Max Back Dated Activity – Dec 31, 2015

The AA.ACTIVE.PROPERTIES archival process, selects the records from AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY.HIST where Latest Effective Date is less than Purge Date and Arc Last Effective Date is updated. The Activity records referenced in AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY.HIST , with at least one input action is considered and the related AA.ARR. records except the latest before the derived purge date are archived.

> **⚠️ Note:** It is recommended to keep the purge date greater than or equal in the AA.ACTIVE.ACTIVITIES record than the AA.ACTIVE.PROPERTIES record for efficient archival processing. Purge Date defined in the AA.ACTIVE.PROPERTIES record in the ARCHIVE application should be older than the date derived from the configuration in Max Back Dated Activity . The user must set Max Back Dated Activity mandatorily for property records archival and the same is validated during property archival processing. The Arc Filename attribute is auto-populated with list of all files to be archived relevant to the specific implementation and use of AA products. If the attribute is cleared of all current values and the record is committed, then this attribute is automatically populated as explained with the relevant AA tables.

| Purge Date - 30th Apr 2020 | Purge Date - 31st Mar 2020 |
|---|---|
| If Purge Date is defined as Apr 30, 2020 in AA.ACTIVE.ARRANGEMENT.CONCAT , then the system picks up AAA references based on Latest Effective Date and if Arc Latest Effective Date is updated. In this case, all the AAA references in #1 record match the criteria. Hence, the system deletes the linked AAA references from AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY.HIST table for the #1 record and clears the dated references (AA.ARR. records which are not present in live DB) of the eligible records from the AA.ARRANGEMENT.DATED.XREF table. | If Purge Date is defined as Mar 31, 2020 in AA.ACTIVE.ARRANGEMENT.CONCAT , then the system picks up AAA references based on Latest Effective Date and if Arc Latest Effective Date is updated. In this case, only one AAA reference (1-Jan-2020) present in #1 record matches the criteria. Hence, the system deletes the linked AAA references from AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY.HIST table and clears the dated references (AA.ARR. records which are not present in live DB) of eligible records from the AA.ARRANGEMENT.DATED.XREF table. Post deletion, Arc Latest Effective Date is updated as 31-Mar-2020 in #1 record. |


##### Archival of Nolog/Restrict.log Activities

The AAA IDs generated for Nolog or Restrict log activities are not logged into AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY . In the current archival process, the selection is based on AAA with an effective date and activity equal to Nolog or Restrict log activities. As the AAA is a huge file, the selection of Nolog or Restrict log activities for archival consumes more time.

To improve the selection process, Nolog or Restrict log AAA IDs are generated with a prefix 'AAACN' instead of 'AAACT' if the activities are triggered by the system (If Activity Type is set as Nolog or Restrict.Log in AA.ACTIVITY ). In case, the user triggers the activity, 'AAACN' has to be manually forced as the prefix instead of 'AAACT', else AAA IDs are generated with prefix 'AAACT' and the same are not considered for the archival process.

For archival, the AAA records with prefix 'AAACN' and effective date older than the retention period or purge conditions defined in the ARCHIVE application record AA.NOLOG.ACTIVITIES are selected for processing.

> **⚠️ Note:** To archive the older No Log or Restrict.Log activities (with AAACT prefix - prior to DLM changes), the user can specify Attribute Type as Select.attributes and Attribute Value as LEGACY. If specified, the system selects the activities if activity effective date is less than the purge date and verified if the activity is equal to Nolog or Restrict.Log and archives them.


##### Archival of Simulation Records

The AA.SIMULATION.RUNNER record in the ARCHIVE application is used for archival of simulation records.

- The values set in Sim Product Line , Sim Product Group , Sim Product , Sim Retention Period in AA.PARAMETER are referred by the archival process and selection is done on all simulation runner records to identify the applicable records for archival of simulation records. If Retention Period or Purge Date is defined in the AA.SIMULATION.RUNNER record in the ARCHIVE application and Sim Retention Period is defined in AA.PARAMETER , then the period defined in Sim Retention Period is considered for archival of simulation runner records. However, in the above scenario, if Retention Period is defined differently in AA.PARAMETER for different product lines/product groups/products, then the selection process is tedious and it leads to performance issues. To avoid this, the user can specify Attribute Type as Select.attributes and Attribute Value as IGNORE.PRODUCT.RETENTION in the AA.SIMULATION.RUNNER record, then the system refers Purge Date or Retention Period defined in the AA.SIMULATION.RUNNER record for archival processing and ignores the Retention Period defined in AA.PARAMETER . Also, the selection is based on Sim Run Date . If Sim Run Date is less than Purge Date or Retention Period , only those records are considered for archival.

- If the above mentioned attributes are not defined in the AA.PARAMETER table, the selection is based on Sim Run Date for archival. If Sim Run Date is less than the purge date or retention period, only those records are considered for archival process.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Arc Filename attribute is auto-populated with a list of all files to be archived relevant to the specific implementation and use of AA products. If the attribute is cleared of all current values and the record is committed, then this attribute is automatically populated as explained with relevant AA tables.


#### 🔧 Working With

The ARC.GENERIC service archives the AA.ARRANGEMENT tables based on the configurations in the ARCHIVE and ARC.GENERIC.REQUEST applications.

Read Data Life Cycle Management for more information.


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Archival Process feature.

There are no Outputs available for Archival Process feature.

### 1.7  Back Dated Activity Processing


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Temenos Transact allows the user to create a new arrangement, initiate an amendment activity or reverse activity with the effective date that is earlier than the Today’s date. It is possible to apply restriction on what products and activities can be initiated with a back date and the back date can ...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ACTIVITY.CLASS`, `AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY`, `AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY`, `AA.PARAMETER`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Adjustment*, *Child Activity*, *Initiation Type*, *InitiationType*, *Line Attribute*, *Linked Activity*, *Max Back Dated Activity*, *USER*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Temenos Transact allows the user to create a new arrangement, initiate an amendment activity or reverse activity with the effective date that is earlier than the Today’s date. It is possible to apply restriction on what products and activities can be initiated with a back date and the back date can be performed to what extent in the past. For example, an amendment or reverse activity cannot be back dated prior to the arrangement date.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

There is no specific configuration for the Back Dated Activity Processing feature.


#### 🔧 Working With

This section describes the Process Details and Back Dated Activity Processing.


##### Process Details

The AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY table and application records request for activities to be applied to an arrangement. It is updated whenever an Activity is performed for an arrangement.

Activities can be generated in a number of different ways and the initiating source of the activity is identified in the Initiation Type field of the Activity.

A manual request to perform an Activity for an arrangement is initiated directly through AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY (For example, New Deposits, amendments).

The InitiationType field displays the value USER.

Payment in and out of arrangements are initiated using Temenos Transact applications where accounts can be specified (For example, Funds Transfer, Teller, Clearing Interface). When an arrangement account is specified, an Activity is created based on the accounting movement generated by the application.

The Initiation Type field displays the value TRANSACTION.

An Activity can generate additional Activities directly as a result of the initial Activity. For example, a charge for breaking a restriction, applying an Activity based charge or applying an overpayment to a loan. Secondary Activities can be created as a result of any user, transaction or scheduled activity.

These Activities are linked to the initial Activity; if the initiating Activity has reversed, the system reverses the secondary Activities too. Note that secondary Activities can generate further secondary Activities themselves.

The Initiation Type field displays the value SECONDARY.

The Linked Activity field displays the id of the parent AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY , which requests the creation of the secondary Activity. The Child Activity field displays the id of the AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY requests that are created as a result of this Activity.

Activities can be generated as a result of scheduled events in the deposits lifecycle. For example, issue of bills, making amounts due.

The Initiation Type field displays the value of SCHEDULED.

A full history of activities performed for an arrangement is maintained in the AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY table. The table maintains a list of Activities by effective date, Recording Activity id, Activity name, and status and initiation method.

The status indicated whether the associated Arrangement Activity is:

- Unauthorised - UNAUTH
- Authorised – AUTH
- Unauthorised Reversal – UNAUTH-REV
- Authorised Reversal – AUTH-REV
- Deleted when unauthorised – DELETED
- In hold status - HLD

The data maintained in this table is used for Activity based processing including:

- Periodic restrictions on number and value of activities over time.
- Enquiry of Activity history.
- Correction due to back-dated activities.


#### Back Dated Activity Processing

A back-dated activity is recorded in the same way as a standard activity. However, additional processing is required to provide automatic correction.

> **⚠️ Note:** Banks can control the maximum period upto which a back-value dated activity can be triggered in the system. The Max Back Dated Activity attribute in the AA.PARAMETER table defines the specific period (NND or NNM or NNY, NN is the no of days/months/years) and the system controls the user from triggering any back-dated activity prior to this period based on this parameter. Read Configuring Archival Process for more information.


##### Process-Flow Description

When an Activity is processed, the system follows the flow described below:

The Initial Activity request for the arrangement is known as the Master Activity. All correction processing takes place at the same time as the Master Activity. For example, when the Activity is authorised or deleted, the correction Activities are also authorised or deleted.

A correction can be triggered by a new Back-Dated Activity or reversal of an existing Activity.

The system records the master Activity ID in the AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY record fields:

- MASTER.AAA–updated with the Initiating Activity id when a new Activity is created. The initiating new arrangement Activity can be identified where the MASTER.AAA is the same as the activity id itself.
- REV.MASTER.AAA–updated with the Initiating Activity id when an Activity is reversed.

The system checks the following if the correction processing is required:

- Product line require correction processing – the AA.PRODUCT.LINE record displays value REPLAY in the Line Attribute field. (This is released by Temenos). If not set, then no further processing takes place.
- Determine the date that system must replay Activities up to–the REPLAY.TO date. This is determined as the greater of the current system date or the latest Future Dated Activity performed for the arrangement.
- Determine the list of activities that must be reversed and those that must be replayed. The reversal list is obtained from AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY by finding all activities that are processed with an effective date greater than or equal to the effective date of the initiating activity. A list of all live activities is built, those activities that were USER initiated or TRANSACTION initiated are added to a list of activities to be replayed. Reversal of the arrangement creation activity itself does not generate any replay activities. Where the initiating activity effective date is the same as the historic activity effective date the system will only reverse and replay activities that were performed in sequence after the initiating activity, i.e. an activity that was created in the start of day processing would not be reversed or replayed if a back-dated online repayment is made.
- Determine if an accrual adjustment is required. If an interest accrual is made after or on the effective date of the Initiating Activity, then the system must make an accrual adjustment the effective date. Adjustments are made for each type of interest that may have been accrued.

If accrual adjustments are required, the system generates an Accrual Adjustment Activity (AA.ACTIVITY.CLASS DEPOSITS-ADJUST-INTEREST) for each Interest Property identified in the adjustment check.

The Activity backs out interest accruals made from the last date accrued to the initiating Activity effective date.

Activities with effective dates after the initiating effective date identified in the check, adjustment process are then reversed. The sequence of reversal is the most recent effective date through to the oldest effective date.

The system has adjusted interest accruals and backed out any Subsequent Dated Activities, the arrangement contract is reset back to the correct status as at the effective date of the Initiating Activity.

The Back-Dated Activity can be processed and the system generates the same results as if the Activity had not been entered back dated.

| Column 1 | Column 2 |
|---|---|
| Find the Next Activity to Process | Having processed the requested Back-Dated Activity, the system reprocesses the arrangement contract back to the REPLAY.TO date. The next Activity to process must be identified from either: The next scheduled Activity, or The next Activity to be replayed. The system cycles the schedule forwards from the initiating effective date to the REPLAY.TO date to obtain the next Activity to process. |
| Process the Next Activity | The system processes the Activity identified in the previous step. This is performed by creation of a new AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY request. For SCHEDULED Activities, a new request is built for the scheduled Activity. For USER or TRANSACTION Activities, which are being replayed the new request includes any data manually captured by the original request, a reference the original Activity is held in the Adjustment field of AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY. |
| Any More Activities to Process | Once the next Activity is processed, the system repeats the process of finding the next Activity and processing it until the REPLAY.TO date is reached. |
| Amendment or New Activities | Back-dated activities can be processed by the system for an Arrangement. There are no restrictions for adjustments into previous interest periods etc., the only restriction is that the Activity cannot be dated earlier than the Arrangement start date. Activities can be initiated directly through the AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY application (USER activities) or through a payment application (TRANSACTION Activities). |
| Reversal | Any Activity can be reversed unless the AA.ACTIVITY.CLASS is defined as NOREVERSE at any time. The reversal of an Activity also triggers full correction of existing later dated Activities. Payment Activities can be reversed directly from AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY rather than the underlying application (e.g. Funds Transfer or Teller) if required. In many cases, this is the required corrective action to take in the case of a mistake in booking the original payment, as the original transaction may involve a number of parties or may no longer be accessible. In this case a manual adjustment must be made for the other-side of the payment from the AA Suspense account. |
| Automatic Correction | The mechanism used for automatic correction for the contract is to first set the contract state back as though it was back on the effective date of the Activity. This involves the back-out (reversal) of the effect of later dated Activities. The Activity itself is then processed and updates applied accordingly. The system then rolls the contract forward through to the current system date (or forward dated Activity date) by applying scheduled Activities and replaying user and Transaction Activities. The back-dated Activity can result in a different set of scheduled Activities being processed than before due to the impact on the contract state. For example, a contract can be overdue and gone through several stages of the aging cycle. However, due to a back-dated repayment the contract would no longer be overdue so the overdue ageing process now is no longer processed. |
| Back-Out | Back-out processing takes place by reversal of the original Activity. The reversal automatically takes place before the back-dated Activity itself is processed. |
| Accrual Adjustment | An accrual adjustment is made through the LENDING-ADJUST-INTEREST Activity. This Activity reverses the accrual posted between the effective date of the back-dated Activity and the last accrual for that property. |
| Replay | Replay processing takes place by creation of new Arrangement Activities. |
| Accounting | Accounting entries are raised for both reversal of the original Activity and the replay of the Activity. |
| Messaging | No delivery can be generated from the reversal or replay of an Activity. |
| Exceptions and Restrictions | The AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY table and application records requests for activities to be applied to an arrangement. It is updated whenever an Activity is performed for an arrangement. |


#### 📋 Tasks

There are no Tasks available for Back Dated Activity Processing feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Back Dated Activity Processing feature.
