#### 📖 Introduction

The system can be configured to evaluate any restrictions posted on the activities to raise overrides or errors when a payment is made through the payment initiation systems. As the payment initiation system can be different from the payment processing system, the overrides are not raised unless they are configured in the AA.DECISION.PARAMETER table. Hence, the system can be configured to evaluate primary as well as secondary activities that are raised from a payment application to generate the overrides at the time of ordering the payment (for example, the PAYMENT.ORDER application).


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following sections describe configuring the decision parameter and payments initiation systems in detail.


##### Configuring Decision Parameter

AA.DECISION.PARAMETER is a generic parameter table configuration where the user can choose various options or processes based on Product Line, Company, Product, Product group, Activity class, and Activity. When the arrangement matches the conditions set, then the system takes the corresponding decision else the default decision is taken.

The following fields are configured to support the Decision Parameter in AA restrictions and the user can choose between generic or specific decisions.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| Product Line | The product line restriction decisions are more generic. The restriction is validated across all the product groups or products under the product line. For example, Lending, Deposits, Accounts and so on. |
| Product Group | The product group restriction decisions are specific to the product group level ( AA.PRODUCT.GROUP ). The restriction is validated across all the products under the product group for example, CURRENT.ACCOUNTS, MORTGAGES, DEPOSITS and so on. |
| Product | The product restriction decisions are more specific to product level ( AA.PRODUCT ). Only the restricted product is validated and the other products are not validated. For example, DEPOSIT.LONG, MORTGAGE, SAVINGS.ACCOUNT and so on. |
| Activity Class | The restriction decisions can be more specific to activity class ( AA.ACTIVITY.CLASS ). For example, ACCOUNTS-DEBIT-ARRANGEMENT, ACCOUNTS-CREDIT-ARRANGEMENT and so on. |
| Activity | The restriction decision can be taken furthermore specific to a particular activity ( AA.ACTIVITY ). For example, LENDING-APPLYPAYMENT-PO.WITHDRAWAL, LENDING-APPLYPAYMENT-PR.PRINCIPAL.DECREASE and so on. |
| Arrangement Company | The restriction decision depends on the arrangement company. For example, GB0010001, AU0010001, and so on. |
| Decision | When ordering a payment, the user can choose to restrict certain activities from going through the payment or choose not to restrict any activity at all. If there are restrictions applied on such activities, the system checks for the overrides or errors set at product condition level and displays accordingly while validating the payment transaction. The options available are: Primary Restriction - The user can choose a restriction evaluation for a primary activity, that is, only the first activity initiated is evaluated, the associated activities are not evaluated, and any override or error set at the product condition level for that activity is displayed accordingly on validating a payment. Primary and Secondary Restriction - The user can choose a restriction evaluation at both the primary and secondary activities, that is, not only the primary activity, but all the associated secondary activities are checked for any restrictions set. Any override or error set at the product condition level for that activity is displayed accordingly on validating a payment. No Restriction - No activity is evaluated for restrictions set as errors or overrides while ordering the payment. The payment is processed as per the set up. The system processes the decision based on the sequence of the decision parameter. The evaluation check takes place from the initial decision (row) and if no activity qualifies for the restriction, then the next sequence of decisions are picked up, and so on. |
| Default Decision | If the arrangement condition does not match any of the decision parameters sequence, then the default decision is chosen for evaluation. The available options are: Primary Restriction, Primary and Secondary Restriction, and No Restriction. |


##### Configuring Payment Initiation and Payment Systems

When a payment is initiated for an arrangement (debit or credit), it is triggered as an activity through Activity Mapping and the final transaction codes are determined in the allocation rule associated to that specific action.

The system simulates internally and evaluates for activity restrictions if any, for an arrangement, at the time of initiating the transaction. This is checked even before the transaction is completed in the payment system through certain transaction codes. Hence, the same transaction codes should be configured and mapped accordingly in:

- Ordering and Beneficiary code of the PAYMENT.ORDER.PRODUCT
- Debit and credit transaction code used by the Payment System – for example in Product Determination of TPH
- Activity to transaction code mapping in Activity Mapping Condition
- The allocation rule in the accounting generation in an arrangement

> **⚠️ Note:** The Chk Acct Restrict field in the PAYMENT.ORDER.PRODUCT application must be set to Both.

The below screenshots describe the setup required in the Payment Initiation and Payment System to be in line with the AA applications.

The payment initiation setup is as follows:

- Dr Txn Code and the Cr Txn code are updated with the transaction codes to be used in the accounting.
- Ordering Txn Code and Beneficiary Txn Code are updated with the same transaction codes.
- Chk Acct Restrict is set to Both.

The screenshot of the payment initiation setup for a loan disbursement is displayed below.

The below screenshot shows the Payment System setup in the TPH for a loan disbursement. The transaction codes are updated in the corresponding Product Determination application in line with PAYMENT.ORDER.PRODUCT . (Read Payment Hub for more information on product determination).

Activity mapping defines the link between the transaction code raised by the payment system to the corresponding activity in the arrangement. Here, when a debit transaction reaches the arrangement with transaction code 850 (based on the payment system setup – TPH in this case), it is mapped to a default debit for disbursement of the loan.

The Debit Transaction Code, Ordering Transaction Codes in PAYMENT.ORDER.PRODUCT are the same as the Debit Book Code in Product determination, which is the same as the Default Debit Transaction Code used during disbursement.

The AC.ALLOCATION.RULE table defines the transaction codes in soft accounting for generating accounting entries during a disbursement.

The exact transaction codes must be used to evaluate the activity charges or restriction configured in an arrangement. Hence, it is very important to configure the right transaction code in payment initiation systems and Activity Mapping condition, allocation rules for the respective activities. If there are any mismatch of codes and configurations, discrepancies will occur.


##### Illustrations

The AA.DECISION.PARAMETER table for payment is configured for Lending, Deposits and Accounts Product Lines with the following priority:

- The primary and secondary restrictions are evaluated in the Lending product line, for the Personal Loan product, on the LENDING-APPLYPAYMENT-PO.WITHDRAWAL activity.
- Only the primary restrictions are evaluated in Lending product line, for the MORTGAGE.ARM product, on the LENDING-APPLYPAYMENT-PO.WITHDRAWAL activity.
- No restriction is evaluated in Lending Product line, for the Consumer Loan product, on the LENDING-APPLYPAYMENT-PO.WITHDRAWAL activity.
- The primary and secondary restrictions are evaluated across all the Deposits product groups or Deposits products for the Deposits product line.
- The primary and secondary restrictions are evaluated across all the Accounts product group or Accounts products for the Accounts product line.
- The default decision is chosen for evaluation if the arrangement condition does not match any of the decision parameters sequence.

This section describes the configuration of Activity Restriction with illustrations.

In the illustration, a personal, mortgage, and consumer loans have the Activity Restriction condition configured such that, when a disbursement is made on these lending arrangements, against the available commitment amount:

- The payment amount should not be more than USD 100,000.
- If the amount exceeds USD 100,000, then an override message is displayed to restrict the activity.
- If the override is accepted, then a rule break charge (DISBURSEMENTFEE) is applied, and the corresponding override message is displayed to process the activity.
- Hence, the primary activity is the disbursement activity, and the secondary activity is the rule break activity along with the charge.

The screenshots for Activity Restriction configuration for the lending products are shown below. Read Activity Restriction Property Class for more information.

#### 🔧 Working With

When a financial transaction is performed on an arrangement using the payment initiation systems, the user configures the system to evaluate for any credit or debit posting restriction, activity charges in the arrangement or activity restriction configured for that event in that product. The system evaluates and raises any error or override in the Payment Initiation page as applicable for that activity, which is configured at the product-level. It is possible to create the following records in the AA.DECISION.PARAMETER table for regular payments and for clearing.

- PAYMENT
- CLEARING

There are three levels of evaluation of the conditions specified in Decision Parameter.

1. No Restriction
2. Primary Restrictions
3. Primary and Secondary Restrictions

Implementation considerations on Decision Parameter are:

1. For a product where there are no activity restrictions or charges configured or the user does not look forward to evaluate the configured charges or restriction at the time of initiating the transaction, the setup can be No Restriction.
2. For a product where there is a minimal of activity restriction or charges, the setup can be Primary Restriction. The primary restriction is not suitable for a product which has multiple charges, multiple activity restriction, product qualifier along with activity restriction in the same product, a product with a hierarchy structure like a master arrangement link (Facility, Multi Currency and so on). The primary restriction is applicable only for light weight products and can be implemented in products that are simple to improve the performance of the system. For any regular or complex setup like Facility and Drawings, MCY and its sub accounts, multiple instances of Activity Charges or Restriction in the same product, primary and secondary restriction is the suitable setup.
3. For a product where the activity restriction, charges configured must be evaluated at the time of initiating the transaction, the setup can be Primary and Secondary Restriction.

> **⚠️ Note:** The system processes the decision based on the sequence of the decision parameter. The evaluation check takes place from the initial decision (row) and if no activity qualifies for the restriction, then the next sequence of decision is chosen and so on. For the right order of evaluation, the user must ensure to configure the Decision Parameter accordingly.

##### Workflow

8. Click the Commit icon to submit the record.

### 1.18  ProductBuilder


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Arrangement Architecture (AA) module provides a flexible framework that allows to create new Temenos Transact modules. The application provides a business component based architecture for managing products. Arrangements is part of the Retail Banking suite of products.*
>

#### 📖 Introduction

The Arrangement Architecture (AA) module provides a flexible framework that allows to create new Temenos Transact modules. The application provides a business component based architecture for managing products. Arrangements is part of the Retail Banking suite of products.

The main features of the AA module are:

- Ability to build families of products
- Ability to inherit properties from the product family structure
- Ability to determine the properties that a product is comprised of
- Control of default values to be applied for product arrangements
- Dated conditions for products
- Full control of scope of negotiation between product and arrangement conditions
- Control of negotiation of attributes over time
- Design or Proof or Publish life-cycle for product management

Read the Property Classes user guide for more details on individual classes.

#### 📖 Introduction

Simulation is the process of replicating real time scenario for a new or existing arrangement, without updating the actual files in the system. Simulation mirrors a real activity and stores the data in simulated files. Simulation supports execution of transaction with current or future date as effective. Results of the simulation run are stored in special files. Two or more simulations can be compared during the decision process. If approved, a simulated data can be converted to real or live record.

Simulations captured in the past can be executed on the simulation date or any date thereafter.

The Repayment Calculator is a routine-based enquiry to derive repayment amount of a loan along with the associated fees or charges. When the customer specifies the loan amount required and the term for that product in the user interface, the AA framework runs this enquiry and returns the repayment information. The user interface displays the instalment amount along with the total repayment amount, total interest, fees or charges, interest rate, Annual Percentage Rate (APR) type and APR rate.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

There is no special configuration required to run simulations in Arrangements.


##### Information Storage and Retrieval

The details of a simulation are stored in the corresponding $SIM files such as FBNK.AA.BILL.DETAILS$SIM , FBNK.AA.SCHEDULED.ACTIVITY$SIM , and so on. The $SIM files are updated only when the corresponding record in the FILE.CONTROL application has Sim Reqd set as Yes, and Suffix set to $Sim.

The simulation details can be later retrieved from the respective $SIM files using a local enquiry or an API routine.

To improve the response time of the simulation, it is recommended to not update the $SIM files when there is no need to store and retrieve the simulation details. That is, when the simulation is not retrieved at a later stage (through a local enquiry or an API routine), the above-mentioned configuration in the Sim Reqd and Suffix fields can be removed to improve the performance.


##### Suppressing Account Number Generation for Simulation

The system can be configured to assign an account number for the arrangement at the time of simulation or to provide a sample number only for simulation.

In the AA.PARAMETER application, the Sim Account Ref attribute can be updated with a pre-generated account number that can be used temporarily only for new arrangement simulation.

To assign a pre-defined account number for simulation,

- The user has to apply the validation function in the ACCOUNT file to pre-generate the account number (that is, ACCOUNT I F3, but the account should not be created) to be temporarily used for the simulation.
- The existing account numbers from the ACCOUNT application and file suffixes $NAU, $HIS, $SIM cannot be used in the Sim Account Ref attribute.

At the time of simulation, the system checks if the pre-generated account number is configured in the Sim Account Ref attribute and assigns the pre-generated account number to the new arrangement simulation and updates it in the SIM files (such as, AA.ARRANGEMENT$SIM , AA.SIM.ACCOUNT , AA.ARR.ACCOUNT$SIM , ACCOUNT$SIM and so on).

If the financial institution has the multi company setup, the respective company's AA.PARAMETER file needs to be configured with the pre-generated account number from that company in the Sim Account Ref attribute.

Both the actual account number and the IBAN for the arrangement are generated automatically only when the new arrangement simulation is executed.

If the Sim Account Ref attribute is not configured with a pre-generated account number in the AA.PARAMETER file, the system generates the actual account number in the new arrangement simulation process itself and uses it as the account reference for the arrangement when the simulation is executed.


##### Archival of Simulations

The AA.SIMULATION.RUNNER record maintained in the ARCHIVE table holds the default retention period for simulations. The user can modify the retention period, if required.

The retention period for the simulation is calculated based on the Simulation Run Date in the AA.SIMULATION.RUNNER record.

The ARC.AA.SIMULATION.RUNNER routine archives the simulation records. This is triggered during the normal archive process of the AA.SIMULATION.RUNNER archive type, which is added in ARC.GENERIC.REQUEST.


##### Repayment Calculator

An enquiry is released in Temenos Transact that facilitates the calculation of the required values.

1. The Repayment Calculator enquiry uses the AA.PRODUCT.SCHEDULE.PROJECTOR core routine to calculate the loan schedule details without creating a new arrangement.
2. It accepts the Term, Amount and Product.ID as mandatory arguments, uses the Product Catalogue conditions and calls the Schedules enquiry.
3. Then it returns the schedule details such as instalment amounts, total interest, fees or charges, interest rates, APR type and APR rate.
4. Finally, all interest property amounts are accumulated and shown under Total Interest Amount column, all charges are accumulated and shown under Total Fees column and the total interest, total fees and total principal are accumulated and shown under the Total Payment Amount column.
5. The Repayment Calculator returns results for products that have Single or Level configuration in Calc Tier Type field in the Interest property class. Band option is not supported.


##### Synchronous Simulation for API

When a simulation is executed through an API and processed as a service, the response time of the simulation is not predictable.

To improve the response time of the simulation that is consumed through an API, the Synchronous field should be set to Yes in the records in AA.SIMULATION.CAPTURE and AA.SIMULATION.RUNNER applications. When Synchronous is set in AA.SIMULATION.CAPTURE , the system automatically defaults the value for this field in AA.SIMULATION.RUNNER .

> **⚠️ Note:** Synchronous simulation is supported only for IRIS API. It is not supported in the browser.

When Synchronous is set to Yes,

- The system does not handover the simulation to a service. Instead, it is processed online (immediately) using the inline simulation framework.
- The simulation errors are not stored in the simulation runner during synchronous simulation. Instead, the errors are returned as response to the API call.

The Direct Execution option in the Auto Run field in AA.SIMULATION.CAPTURE cannot be configured with synchronous simulation. Therefore, the execution has to be a separate API call after the simulation is completed. For example, in the case of payoff through synchronous simulation, a payoff bill is generated as a $SIM file. If the payoff bill is required in live mode, then the simulation needs to be executed.

It is possible to combine and simulate two or more activities online, that is, without the use of a simulation service. This is achieved by setting the Synchronous field in the AA.SIMULATION.RUNNER record along with the simulation capture references of the respective activities.

The performance of a synchronous simulation can be further improved by defining the Ignore Sim field in AA.PARAMETER application.

- When this field is set as Yes, the AA.SIM. records for the simulation are not created. In this case, If the simulation is amended, then all the fields which were defined during the original simulation creation must be defined again in the payload along with the amended values. During execution of the simulation, If IgnoreReplace tag is set as TRUE in the service.xml of API, then the ProductId , activityId , automaticRun and Synchronous fields must be defined in the payload. If IgnoreReplace tag is set as FALSE, then all the fields of the simulation must be defined in the payload.
- When this field is set as No, the AA.SIM. records for the simulation are created. In this case, when the simulation is amended and/or executed, it is sufficient to define only the required fields in the payload.

> **⚠️ Note:** The Ignore Sim field is applicable only in the case of simulations that are consumed through an API with the Synchronous field set to Yes.

Financial institutions can configure the system to maintain the SIM records for the required properties in the synchronous simulation process.

In the AA.PARAMETER application, the Ignore Sim attribute needs to be set as Yes and the Exclusion Property attribute is set with the required property or properties along with the multi-value attributes, such as Sim Product Line , Sim Product Group , Sim Product to maintain the SIM records in the synchronous simulation process. The SIM records (that is, in SIM files such as AA.SIM.INTEREST , AA.SIM.CHARGE and so on) are maintained for the properties defined in the Exclusion Property attribute in Synchronous Simulations.

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Ignore Sim | Yes |
| Sim Product Line | ACCOUNTS |
| Sim Product Group | SAVINGS.ACCOUNTS |
| Sim Product | SAVINGS.ACCOUNT |
| Exclusion Property | CRINTEREST |

Read API docs to view the sample APIs released for synchronous simulation.

### 1.20  Soft Accounting


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Arrangements module extensively uses the rules based accounting. Arrangements are comprised of a series of balances that can be defined by product type. As a result, the accounting process is flexible to reflect the rules of the underlying products.*

>

> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

The Arrangements module extensively uses the rules based accounting. Arrangements are comprised of a series of balances that can be defined by product type. As a result, the accounting process is flexible to reflect the rules of the underlying products.

The AA modules provide a series of allowed activities that can be performed on a contract. Each activity corresponds to a business action that can take place during the life of the contract.

The methods invoked when an activity is performed on an arrangement don’t generate hard coded accounting movements. Instead, an activity can result in different accounting events being generated. The accounting event reflect the need for an accounting action at that stage of the life of the arrangement and has a context linking it to the business activity such as event amount, currency and so on.

Core accounting system processes the accounting events. A series of accounting rules allow the event processing to be controlled to determine the following:

- Amount to be posted and destination of posting (that is, balance type, P&L, internal account, transaction account)
- Dates to be applied to the movements both value date (used for interest calculation purposes) and exposure date
- Other details of the movements such as transaction codes, system IDs

The accounting rules determine the way a repayment amount for example is allocated against the outstanding balances.

All the AA modules use Soft Accounting for accounting purpose.


#### Soft Accounting

The main components of Soft Accounting comprise of the following:

- AC.BALANCE.TYPE
- AC.EVENT
- AC.ALLOCATION.RULE
- AC.POSTING.DETAILS

On occurrence of an Activity, system triggers soft accounting, only when accounting is required. The corresponding event for this action is defined in Temenos Transact under AC.EVENT . For each Action, the corresponding Allocation Rule can be defined by the user in Accounting Product Condition.

Based on these two inputs, the system generates the accounting entry. The transaction code for the different legs of the accounting entry is available in Allocation Rules, and the Posting Details gives the information that has to be populated in the accounting entry.


#### Key Applications and Tables

The Accounting Property Class is used by all financial products and this controls the link between the accounting events generated by the property actions and the accounting allocation rules to be applied to these events.

Accounting rules can be defined either based on Property, Property Class or combination of them.

- If it is defined based on Property Class, then for all instances of the Property Class the same action and allocations are triggered.
- If accounting is defined based on Property Class and Property, then Property takes precedence.

There are proofing validations in the product that guide the users towards the Balance Types, AC Event configuration in Allocation Rule setup that is missing.

Read Accounting Property Class user guide.

At the Activity Class level, all the actions that are performed on a particular Property Class are defined at AA.ACTIVITY.CLASS level. A corresponding record is available in AA.PROPERTY.CLASS.ACTION , where it is decided if the underlying action raises an accounting entry or otherwise.

The AC.EVENT records are released by core accounting and acts as the link between the Soft Accounting configuration in AA and what is passed to the core accounting to be processed as accounting entries. A combination of these records can be used to create the entries required for any given activity in AA. The description advises the user on the accounting entry generated by the event: CR EXPACCOUNT Balance.

Record ID of AC.EVENT is PROPERTY.CLASS-ACTION.NAME-PAYMENT.METHOD-ADDITIONAL.INFO.

For example, ACCOUNT-DEPOSIT-DUE INTEREST-ACCRUE-DUE-SP.

AC.EVENT records are configured used in AC.ALLOCATION.RULE records, which in turn are linked to AA.PRD.CAT.ACCOUNTING Property Class record.

Read AC.EVENT and corresponding Allocation Rule required for mapping.

| Attribute | Description |
|---|---|
| Description | A meaning full description for the allocation rule. |
| Event Type | An optional identifier to allow the allocation associated only when the event type supplied with the accounting event matches. Null value is assumed to be the default value. No duplicate values allowed. The applications should document the structure of their accounting events to allow this table to be configured correctly. A valid AC.EVENT record is allowed. |
| Entry Print Mask | This attribute indicates if masking is required for the event type. Masking can be applied by setting the value as YES. |
| Mvmt Target | This attribute indicates the target balance associated with the event type. It is sub-valued and can be expanded to allow multiple movements to be raised. Values allowed when Mvmt Detail is set to STMT: BAL*BALANCE.TYPE key - Soft Balance Type (defined in AC.BALANCE.TYPE ) INT*ACCOUNT.CLASS key – Account Class for posting to an internal account of the specified class in event currency INTLCY*ACCOUNT.CLASS key – Account Class for posting to an internal account in local currency of the specified class. AC*ACCOUNT key - Account number for posting to a specific account number. TXN* - Contract ID to be mapped from the supplied event information Values allowed when Mvmt Detail is set to CATEG: PL*CATEGORY key - category code for profit and loss posting Values allowed when Mvmt Detail is set to SPECIAL: CRB - TXN indicating that the contract of the event will be used. No input is allowed if the attribute Mvmt Detail is not populated. |

| Mvmt Dr Txn | Defines the transaction to be used when creating debit STMT.ENTRY or CATEG.ENTRY movement entries. When this attribute is left blank, the value in the Def Dr Txn attribute is used. |

Values allowed when Opp Detail is set to STMT: BAL*BALANCE.TYPE key - Soft Balance Type (defined in AC.BALANCE.TYPE ) INT*ACCOUNT.CLASS key – Account Class for posting to an internal account of the specified class in event currency. INTLCY*ACCOUNT.CLASS key – Account Class for posting to an internal account in local currency of the specified class. AC*ACCOUNT key - Account number for posting to a specific account number. TXN* - Contract ID to be mapped from the supplied event information. Values allowed when Mvmt Detail is set to CATEG: PL*CATEGORY key - category code for profit and loss posting. Values allowed when Opp Detail is set to SPECIAL: CRB - TXN indicating that the contract of the event will be used. No Input allowed if the Opp Detail attribute is not populated. |

The AC.POSTING.DETAIL is used to define the mapping rules of the generation of the entry detailed content. The definition in these records controls how the content of the accounting entries are built.

The movement type can be:

- CATEG – CATEG.ENTRY records
- STMT – STMT.ENTRY records
- SPECIAL – RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY records

For example, in order to map and record the additional fields in STMT.ENTRY , a new set of values are added in the AC.POSTING.DETAILS for storing the additional field and it is modified to allow a new value.

A multi-value field is introduced for storing the additional field name along with its value as an associated field instead of using the Reserved field as and when the requirement rises. Further, it has been restricted that the duplicate occurrence in one of the field is made mutually inclusive with the other field.

The Soft Accounting process looks for the additional fields in the event and populate both the name and its corresponding value from the event information into the new statement entry fields.

| Attribute | Description |
|---|---|
| Description | A meaning full description for the posting. |
| Movement Type | Allows the user to define the entry being generated CATEG SPECIAL STMT |
| Entry Field | Allows the user to designate the name of the Entry Field to be mapped. Must be valid name in the STMT.ENTRY standard selection record, and must be one of the identified attributes that can be mapped. |
| Value Source | Allows the user to define the source of the data to be mapped into the associated Entry Field . Available values are: CONTRACT – data is from the contract TRANSACTION – data is from the transaction EVENT – data is from the event ROUTINE – data is derived by a routine Constant – a constant to be displayed – may be to indicate a standard value. In Temenos Transact AA is the constant used to indicate the entry belongs to Arrangement Architecture. Original Transaction – AA transactions can be reversed and replayed – The value can be picked up from the original transaction Parent Transaction – There can be child activities generated by the system as result of the original activity. System can be indicated to pick up the value source from Parent Transaction. |
| Entry Value | Identifies the item in the Value Source attribute that contains the source data to be mapped. Values should match the allowed list. |


##### Structure Overview

The underlying core applications generate AC.EVENT and AC.BALANCE.TYPE . These are then passed to Soft Accounting. The relevant AC.ALLOCATION.RULE is determined by the system from the Product configuration (accounting condition). Once detected the Allocation Rule to be used, the system uses the setup defined for the specific AC.EVENT and raises accounting.

The detailed flow is also shown below.


##### Accounting Schema Flow

In Temenos Transact , accounting entries are automatically generated for authorised transactions. AA provides a certain amount of flexibility in defining broad rules for a desired accounting set-up. When an Activity involving accounting is processed, that raises an accounting event. Accounting Property Class is used to define Property-wise and Action-wise allocation rules. Further, Properties having a financial implication like Interest, Charge, etc. can have multiple balances which can be defined by users. Allocation Rules define the rules for debit and credit transactions of every accounting event type like which type of entries need to be generated, the balances to be updated, etc. Temenos Transact core accounting raises the necessary accounting entries (Spec Entry, Stmt Entry and Categ Entry) and update the required balances as set in the Allocation Rules. These balances are consolidated and reported in financial reports.

The starting point in the flow should be the Activity Class. All the Property Classes that have balance types defined may generate accounting entries while a particular activity is triggered.

The Property Classes that may generate financial or accounting entries for DEPOSITS-NEW-ARRANGEMENT are Account and Term Amount.

In the example below for DEPOSIT-NEW-ARRANGEMENT we have identified the following actions:

- ACCOUNT-MAINTAIN
- TERM.AMOUNT-UPDATE
- ACCOUNT-DEPOSIT
- TERM.AMOUNT-DEPOSIT

Each of the Actions defined in the Activity Class have an entry in AA.PROPERTY.CLASS.ACTION . When Accounting is set to YES in Action, accounting is triggered for the product.

While looking at these records, notice that only ACCOUNT-DEPOSIT and TERM.AMOUNT-DEPOSIT has the field Accounting set to YES. This means that it is only this one can actually do any accounting and the associated action is DEPOSIT.

When accounting is set to YES for a particular action, to process the transaction, the system looks for the appropriate allocation rule to be used for the PROPERTY. This can be derived from the product condition that is cataloged under AA.PRD.CAT.ACCOUNTING . System locates the most suitable allocation rule by Property and if there is no rule for the property then the system takes Property Class rule.

The accounting definition can be at Property or Property Class level. If it is defined at both level then Property takes precedence. The AC.ALLOCATION.RULE linked to the ACCOUNT Property us DEPOSIT-ACCOUNT and the one to TERM.AMOUNT is DEPOSIT-COMMITMENT.

AA.PRD.CAT.ACCOUNTING

The Action and Allocation Rules for each Property or Property Class pertinent to a specific Product is defined in AA.PRD.CAT.ACCOUNTING . The below screenshot shows the Accounting pertaining to Long Term Deposit to Commitment or Term Amount Deposit.

AA processing generates an AC.EVENT and determines the AC.BALANCE.TYPE that should be updated.

As per core description this event should credit the EXPACCOUNT balance type. The underlying AC.BALANCE.TYPE for this asset type is EXPACCOUNT (contingent, RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY record should be raised).

After event is identified, the system looks at the relevant AC.ALLOCATION.RULE and identifies the transaction codes that are pertinent to the underlying event. In the example, the event is TERM.AMOUNT-DEPOSIT-EXP and the associated transaction codes are NEW indicating that it is a new contract.

Same as above for TERM.AMOUNT-DEPOSIT Action.

It raises contingent entries, RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY.

#### 📖 Introduction

Statement Narrative helps to provide the customers with information about the accounts maintained with the bank along with the periodic statements.

Statement narratives can be parameterised to generate a statement with user-friendly description. This representation of accounting entries as a statement is available as an online enquiry. The functionality also fully supports multi-language definition of narratives.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

For a user-defined activity, it is possible to input a free format and descriptive narrative, which can be utilised to identify the Activity being transacted. Using the AA soft accounting configuration, the narrative can be extracted from AC.POSTING.DETAIL , AA.PROPERTY and AA.ACTIVITY .


##### Posting Detail

In AC.POSTING.DETAIL for the STMT.AA record, the details of the data that has to be mapped into the STMT.ENTRY record are defined as follows.

In the AC.POSTING.DETAIL , three additional narratives have been defined, which appear in Narrative field of the STMT.ENTRY record. The fields are:

1. Multi-value 5 is the Full Description from the AA.PROPERTY record
2. Multi-value 6 is the Full Description from AA.ACTIVITY record
3. Multi-value 7 is a user-defined field. Narrative entered in AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY


##### Event trigger

An event can trigger the mapping of these narratives as per the EVENT value set in Value Source field.


##### Configuring AA Statement Parameter

The AA.STATEMENT.PARAM application is used for defining the AA transaction processing rules and for parameterising the display of the financial properties of an AA arrangement transaction.

The record ID format is: - - , where the variant is optional. Thus, it is possible to configure individually for different AA product lines and different languages, and also to configure variants within the same product line and/or language. This could be useful for defining separate presentations for different product groups, or for back-office user and client correspondence.

The Attributes selection defines the way transactions are presented on a statement.

The list of values that can be defined in the Attributes are:

- Merge Interest Properties – To merge principal or penalty or arrears interest properties into a single financial component
- Net Opposite Entries – To net opposite accounting entries of the same property, with the same balance type and reversal mark, and with opposite amount
- Net Property Balances – To net all balances within the same property balance group (excluding charges)
- Net Reversed Entries – To net opposite accounting entries of the same property, with the same balance type and opposite reversal mark, and with opposite amount
- Properties in Main Narrative – To include description of the financial components in the same line as the lead narrative
- Show Properties – To include description of the financial components in the statement lines
- Show Reversals – To show reversal lines for transactions reversed on the same day
- Skip Adjustment Entries – To skip processing of interest adjustment accounting entries
- Skip Non-Transaction Activities – To skip display of non-transactional activities if they do not affect the statement balance For example, if the Skip Non-Transaction Activities attribute is enabled in the LENDING-GB Statement Parameter record, then a LENDING-MAKEDUE-CHARGE activity does not show in the loan statement (LENDING-MAKEDUE-CHARGE activity is generated based on schedule and not because of some transaction)
- Swap DD and MAKEDUE Activity – To change the order of direct debit or MAKEDUE activities on the statement. For example, show first makedue and then DD, if the make due activity is triggered within the direct debit transaction.

The AA properties, balance types are categorised into the following tabs (the tabs are shown when AA.STATEMENT.PARAM is viewed in the menu) to group the property class and the respective financial components along with the narratives for the statement display. The processing rule for the display can be defined in the processing.

The following are the fields in the Properties tab:

- Property Class – Specifies the property class of the financial component. This is a multi-value field. Financial components on the statement are displayed in the order in which the property classes are defined on this record (using the above example, first ACCOUNT – principal, then INTEREST – interest, then CHARGE – charges).
- Property Name – Specifies the name of the property for the financial component available in the property class. This is a sub-value field under Property Class.
- Property Description – Specifies the property description to be displayed on the statement (as the financial component description).
- Include Balance Type – Specifies the property balance types to be included in the running balance on the statement.

The following are the fields in the Balances tab:

- Property Class - Specifies the property class of the financial component. This is a multi-value field, for display-only (as defined on the previous Properties tab).
- Group Name - Specifies the balance group name. This is a sub-value field under Property Class. A balance group links together different AA balance types in the property class, such as, movement on GRC, DEL, NAB balances is grouped into OVERDUE balance group. This is so that on the statement, movement on any of these balances is described as overdue.
- Group Description - Specifies the description of the above balance group, to be displayed on the statement.
- Balance Type - Specifies the balance type (prefix). This is a sub-value field under Property Class. This field together with Balance Group below allows assigning balance types to balance groups.
- Balance Group - Specifies the balance group the above Balance Type should be assigned to.

The following are the fields in the Narratives tab:

- Property Class - Specifies the property class of the financial component. This is a multi-value field, for display only (as defined on the previous Properties tab).
- Credit Condition - Defines the condition for displaying the credit narrative format given in the Credit Narrative field (on the right). It is a sub-value field under property class, and can be either: - , which means that the respective credit narrative is used if there is a credit movement on the of the . The must be one of the groups defined in the previous page for the respective property class of the property. For example:
- Credit Narrative - Specifies the credit narrative (that is, for credit movement). The narrative can include special keywords: &&PROPNAME&& - Specifies the name of the property on which there is balance movement, as defined in the Properties tab. &&BALGROUP&& - Specifies the name of the balance group in which the movement happened, as defined in the Balances tab. For example: “Repaid &&BALGROUP&& &&PROPNAME&&” could be translated into “Repaid Overdue Capital” for OVERDUE balance group and ACCOUNT property.
- - Indicates that the respective debit narrative is used if there is a debit movement on the of the . The must be one of the groups defined in the previous page for the respective property class of the “DEFAULT” text - Indicates that the respective debit narrative is used if no balance or property specific condition is found. The default condition should be always defined as the first condition.
- Debit Narrative - Specifies the debit narrative (that is, for debit movement). The narrative can include special keywords: &&PROPNAME&& - Specifies the name of the property on which there is balance movement, as defined in the Properties tab. &&BALGROUP&& - Specifies the name of the balance group in which the movement happened, as defined in the Balances tab.
- Reversal Marks - Specifies the two characters to be used for marking reversal statement lines

The following are the fields in the Processing tab:

- Hide Activity - Specifies the multi - value list of AA activities to be hidden from statement display, if the total transaction amount affecting the statement balance is zero.
- Split Activity Class - The multi-value set starting with this field, together with Within Activity Class and Processing Rule fields, defines special processing for arrangement activities. It contains the activity that may be included in the special processing under the conditions defined below.
- Within Activity Class - Indicates the parent activities that qualify the above activity for special processing. It is a sub-value field and if null, then the parent activity is not checked.
- Processing Rule - Defines special processing rules. The rules are executed in top-down order with AND operand. The following rules are available: IF.NOT.FT.TRIGGERED – Continues processing if the activity was not triggered by FUNDS.TRANSFER transaction IF.NOT.DDR.TRIGGERED – Continues processing if the activity was not triggered by the DD.RETURN transaction IF.STANDALONE – Continues processing if the activity is standalone, that is, not executed as a child activity IF.NOT.STANDALONE – Continues processing if the activity is executed as a child activity IF.REV.MASTER.NULL – Continues processing if the activity is not executed as a child of reversal activity IF.NOT.RETROSPECT – Continues processing if the activity is not executed as a child of retrospect activity SEARCH.TOP.LEVEL – Searches for the top-level activity for checking Within Activity Class SEARCH.MASTER – Searches for the master activity for checking Within Activity Class SEARCH.REV.MASTER – Searches for the reversal master activity for checking Within Activity Class ADD.DD.RETURN.REF – Takes reference of the DD.RETURN causing the activity, as the additional &&ADDTNL.TXN.REF&& parameter for Statement Parameter processing ADD.TAX.PROPERTY – Takes the TAX.DATA field value from the accounting entry, as the additional &&ADDTNL.TXN.REF&& parameter for Statement Parameter processing ADD.TXN.REF – Takes the accounting entry transaction code, as the additional &&ADDTNL.TXN.REF&& parameter for Statement Parameter processing (as defined in AA.STATEMENT.NARR.PARAM table)
- Merge Activity - This multi-value field, together with the With Activity field, indicates the arrangement activities that will be merged together when building the statement lines. The activities must have the same value date for the merge to happen.
- With Activity - Indicates the activity to be merged with the one above.


##### Configuring Narrative Parameters

The AA.STATEMENT.NARR.PARAM application links the ACTIVITY.TYPE arrangement to the narrative formats. The ID format is either or - . For example, AA-LENDING-NEW-ARRANGEMENT.

In this parameter record, AA-LENDING-NEW-ARRANGEMENT is used for accounting entries raised by AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY transaction with ACTIVITY = LENDING-NEW-ARRANGEMENT (as Control Field for AA is defined as ACTIVITY).

When the transaction specific parameter is not defined, then the application’s main parameter is used. That is, the transaction specific parameter takes precedence over the application’s main parameter.

The following fields are available on this application and the narrative formats to be defined in the application parameter are categorised into the following tabs (the tabs are shown when AA.STATEMENT.NARR.PARAM is viewed in the menu) to define the selection for display using field operand value.

The following are the fields in the Statement Parameters tab:

- Application – Configures the application for which the narrative formats are defined on the parameter record. This application raises the accounting entry for the arrangement.
- Field - This field, together with Operand or Value, forms a sub-value set for defining conditions for linking the narrative format given in the Statement Format field below. This can be a field name from the above Application , or a special keyword: &&ADDTNL.TXN.REF&& - Indicates the value of the additional parameter defined in the AA activity split rules (in the AA Parameter record) &&DEFAULT&& - Indicates the default narrative format to be used when none of the previously defined conditions are satisfied
- Operand – Checks the condition defined in Field to evaluate Value
- Value – Checks the above condition. This can be either be a constant value or a special keyword: &&CUSTOMER&& - Specifies the customer (number) owning the account for which statement narratives are being built &&ACCOUNT&& - Specifies the account number for which statement narratives are being built. &&ARRANGEMENT&& - Specifies the AA arrangement reference linked to account for which statement narratives are being built.
- Statement Format - The narrative format to be used when the condition specified above is satisfied. The default language format should be linked here. When the narratives are being built for a different language, the system uses the respective language format (if defined) automatically. Only the narrative formats defined for the same application used on the parameter record can be used.

The following are the fields in the Application Parameters tab:

- Application – The field for which narrative formats are defined on this parameter record.
- Control Field - Optional field from the above application, that can be used in the record ID for more specific definition of the parameter records. For example, for a funds transfer(FT), instead of linking all funds transfer narrative formats on single parameter record with ID equal to FT, by setting Control Field to TRANSACTION.TYPE, it is possible to define parameter records per FT transaction type (for example, FT-AC, FTBC ans so on).
- Read from History - Indicates whether the system should read transaction record (for which narrative is being built) from history file. If not set, the transaction record remains as a read from live file only.


##### Configuring Narratives Formats

The AA.STATEMENT.NARR.FORMAT narrative format table is linked to the Narrative Parameter through the Statement Format attribute in the Narrative parameter table.

The following columns are included in this list.

- @id -Specifies the ID of the format record. It is a free text followed by hyphen and language id, and optionally by format variant.
- Description - Specifies the narrative format description.
- Application - Specifies the application for which narrative format is defined.

The following fields are available on this application and the narrative formats defined in the application parameter are categorized into the following tabs (the tabs are shown when AA.STATEMENT.NARR.FORMAT is viewed in the menu) to define the text for display, field level conversion for Narrative format definition and the special processing, to include Balance Types, hide AA PROPERTIES, and so on.

The following are the fields in the Statement Narratives tab:

- Description – Specifies the narrative format description
- Transaction Type - Specifies the user-defined transaction type for this narrative that can be used for filtering account statement enquiry. The transaction types available for selection are defined on EB.LOOKUP table with key AA.STMT.TRANS.TYPE.
- Application - Specifies the Transact application that generates the transaction for which the narrative is being defined.
- Split Same-Day Reversal - Specifies the flag to indicate whether the system should display the original and the reversed transaction line for transactions reversed on the same day. If not set, the reversed transaction is displayed in a single line (assuming that showing of the reversed transactions is marked on the AA parameter file).
- Field or Text - Defines the components of the narrative. It is a multi-value field. In this field either a valid field from the above Application can be defined, or a constant text – enclosed in double quotes.
- field - Returns field from linked application FIELD[x,y] - Returns field number y from array delimited by x CHANGE*x*y Replace value x with value y FMT*x -s Converts value using FMT function and x format TEXT ”x” - Returns text given by x PREFIX ”x” - Prefixes field value with x POSTFIX ”x” - Postfixes field value with x AUDITDATE - Returns year YYYYMMDD of the audit DATE.TIME field value AUDITTIME - Returns time HH:MM of the audit DATE.TIME field value ACCTSAMECUSTOMER - Returns null value if the account with number given by field value does not belong to the customer for whom account statement is being built ACCTOTHERCUSTOMER - Returns null value if the account with number given by field value belongs to the customer for whom account statement is being built. There can be multiple conversions applied on the same field

The following are the fields in the Components tab:

- Hide Line - Indicates that the statement line should be hidden if the total transaction amount (affecting statement balance) is zero.
- Hide Amount - Indicates that the transaction amount should be hidden.
- Hide Components - Indicates that the financial components (AA properties) of the transaction should be hidden, even when the Show Properties attribute on the AA parameter file is set.
- Include Balance (INCL.COMP) – Specifies the AA property balances to be included in the transaction amount. This is a multi-value field. The format is SIGN and PROPERTY. + - Indicates that the property amount should be included if it is positive (credit transaction) - - Indicates that the property amount should be included if it is negative (debit transaction) +PRINCIPALINT - Shows the principal interest amount, if credited -CURACCOUNT - Shows the due principal, if credited -DUENEWARRFEE - Shows the new arrangement fee amount, if raised as a debit charge (due)
- Special Processing (SPEC.PROC.TYPE ) - Specifies the special processing type for the statement line display. Currently two options are available: SEP.MAKEDUE.COMP - Splits lending MAKEDUE activity components (ACCOUNT, PRINCIPALINT, PENALTYINT, ARREARSINT) into separate lines, with additional text given by “capint” or “penarr” after the respective component (property) name. “capint” - specifies the text that follows after CAPITAL and INTEREST components whereas “penarr”- specifies the text that follows after PENALTY INTEREST and ARREARSINT For SEP.MAKEDUE.COMP due charged, the statement lines can be: Capital Due Interest Due Penalty Interest Charged SHOW.TOT.AMOUNT – Uses the amount affecting the statement balance as the transaction amount
- Benefits of Interest - Benefits of Interest is a benefit given to customer when an offset account is linked to a loan account in the system (Bundle functionality). The customer can save on interest by calculating interest only on the outstanding principal after the offset in balance from one of his Retail accounts. The following Narrative Format record is configured to show the Repayment Due transaction along with display of Benefits of Interest in the customer loan statement.

The PRINT.STATEMENT application configures the requests for printing or reprinting of account statements and it can be invoked during COB (end of day) and online processing. The AA.NARRATIVE enquiry can be attached in the Format field in the PRINT.STATEMENT application for a detailed narrative in the statement printing process. The record ID of PRINT.STATEMENT must be attached as a Statement Type in the Statement condition. This enables the printing solution to have a statement similar to AA.STATEMENT enquiry.

It must be ensured that the mandatory selection criteria for this enquiry namely Statement Id , Acct Id , Processing Date , Mask Print , Processing Date , Show Reversal are not changed in the AA.NARRATIVE enquiry.

Read Configuring Account Statements for more information about configuring the PRINT.STATEMENT application.

##### Parameterising Statement Narratives

The statement narratives parameterisation tables provide a flexible way of parameterising transaction narratives for clear and user-friendly presentation of financial activities on an account. The following tables and enquiry are used for this purpose.

- AA.STATEMENT.NARR.PARAM
- AA.STATEMENT.NARR.FORMAT
- AA.STATEMENT.PARAM
- AA.STATEMENT (Enquiry)

| Application | Description |
|---|---|
| AA.STATEMENT.PARAM | Defines how the different financial components (like principal, interest) of an AA transaction are grouped and described under the main transaction narrative. This table enables the user to merge properties, net opposite entries, show or not show property description on statement, show reversal lines, include or exclude specific balance types of properties and so on. Read Configuring Statement Narrative for more information. |
| AA.STATEMENT.NARR.PARAM | Helps to define narratives for AA Events, FT transaction type condition, TT transaction codes, PO (payment initiation) with payment order product. This is further linked to AA.STATMENT.NARR.FORMAT application. Read Configuring Statement Narrative for more information. |
| AA.STATEMENT.NARR.FORMAT | Includes all the narrative format records. A narrative format record defines the narrative format the system should consider when a specific application or activity is triggered against the arrangement. Read Configuring Statement Narrative for more information. |


##### Statement Enquiry

Account Statement .

The enquiry requires one mandatory parameter – account number. If no other parameters are given, then the enquiry uses the default configuration stored on the AA Parameters file for the account’s product line and the default language. The enquiry can be run online for specific dates. The selection below presents the list of available enquiry parameters.

- Account Number - Account for statement preview
- Start Date - Statement opening date
- End Date - Statement closing date
- Transaction Type - Filter to only display transactions of the given type (defined on the statement narrative format record)
- DR / CR Type - Filter to only display debit or credit transactions
- Min Txn Amount - Filter to display transactions with amount greater than or equal the minimum amount specified
- Max Txn Amount - Filter to display transactions with amount less than or equal the maximum amount specified
- Sorting ASC/DESC - Ascending / descending date transaction display order
- Raw Mode - Raw statement display without any additional processing, useful for analysing the statement content
- Language - Use specific language AA parameter record

> **⚠️ Note:** The remaining enquiry parameters mirror the AA Parameter processing attributes and overwrite them if specified in the enquiry.

The below example statement is generated for Account 50007278 through the enquiry.


###### Prerequisite

The Update Entries field should be configured as ALL in ACCOUNT.PARAMETER , else some online entries may not be captured in EB.CONTRACT.BALANCES (ECB).

The PRINT.STATEMENT application configures the requests for printing or reprinting of account statements and it can be invoked during online processing and at the end of day. The AA.NARRATIVE enquiry can be attached in the Format field in the PRINT.STATEMENT application for a detailed narrative in the statement printing process. The record ID of this PRINT.STATEMENT record must be attached as a Statement Type in the Statement condition. This enables the printing solution to have a statement similar to AA.STATEMENT enquiry.

The AA.NARRATIVE enquiry is only for the purpose of COB statement printing using AC.STMT.HANDOFF. It returns the same information as the AA.STATEMENT enquiry when generated using the Statement Printing service. It is released with the standard selection criteria required for the Print Statement service. Hence it is not recommended to launch this enquiry as an individual enquiry. It must be used only during COB statement printing as a service.

Two special keywords (&&ACCOUNT&& and &&ARRANGEMENT&&) are used for discerning the debit or credit side of a transaction or an arrangement activity, to link specific narrative depending on whether the account was debited or credited.

- &&ACCOUNT&& For a PO transaction, if the narrative is built for the account that appears in the Credit Main Account field of the transaction, the PO.LOAN.REPAYMENT-GB format is used (resulting in “"Loan Payment from… " narrative).
- &&ARRANGEMENT&& In this example, For an AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY transaction with activity equal to LENDING-NEWARRANGEMENT, if the narrative is built for the arrangement (account) not equal to the arrangement on which the activity was executed (so not for the loan account) then, the ACCT.NEW.ARRANGEMENT-GB format is used (resulting in “Disbursed loan …” narrative). Otherwise the default LOAN.NEW.ARRANGEMENT-GB narrative format marked by the &&DEFAULT&& keyword is applied (resulting in “New loan contract” narrative).

There can be multiple conversions applied on the same field. In the example below:

The following can take place:

- If the account number given by Credit Acct No (on the FT transaction) does not belong to the customer for whom the statement is built, this narrative part is set to null and the conversion process stops.
- Return the category of the account given in Credit Acct No – read ACCOUNT and return value of Category field.
- Return short name of the category extracted above – read CATEGORY and return value of Short Name field.
- Return first value of the Short Name field.
- Prefix the above value (short name) with “your “.
- Postfix the above value (your short name) with “ “(space).

To edit an existing Statement Narrative record perform the following steps:

1. Soft Accounting .

3. Click the Edit option assigned to target record.
4. Amend the record based on expected narrative configuration.
5. Click the Validate Icon and check for any errors and overrides.
6. Click the Commit icon to submit the record.

### 1.22  Charges and Commissions


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Sections:** 🔧 Working With


#### 🔧 Working With

The users can configure the charges to be due on the first, next, or last payment. The charges are triggered on occurrence of a specific activity and it is due to the customer as per the configuration.

If a user has set the charge collection on the next payment, but the system levies the charge on creation of the contract, it is still due only on the next payment date, that is, it is not due immediately. It is scheduled to be collected on the first payment date as per the schedule configuration.

Alternatively, if a user configures the collection of charge on the first payment, but the first payment date lapses when the customer triggers an activity, the system raises an override and schedules the charge along with the next upcoming payment.


##### Collecting Fee for External Event

The Record Event activity class registers an external event manually in the system. In asset financing, the financial institution can collect a delivery fee when the asset is delivered to the lessee or customer. This is an external event and not connected to the system. The user can manually register the event in the system using ASSET.FINANCE-RECORD.EVENT-ARRANGEMENT. Similarly, below activities are used for collecting charges for external events:

- Failed collection of the asset: At the end of the term, if the lessor is unable to collect the asset, the financial institution levies a charge for the failure of collection of assets. The activity can be registered in the system using ASSET.FINANCE-RECORD.FAILED.COLLECTION-ARRANGEMENT activity. A failed collection fee is levied on the arrangement when the user triggers this activity manually.
- Payment return fee: Lease payments scheduled for collection from an external system might fail due to various reasons like account unavailability or insufficient funds. System triggers ASSET.FINANCE-RECORD.DD.RETURN-ARRANGEMENT activity to register the payment failure. The user can configure a payment return fee on occurrence of this activity.

User creates an arrangement with the condition that the system collects the delivery fee when the ASSET.FINANCE-RECORD.EVENT-ARRANGEMENT activity is triggered.

Delivering the asset to the lessee is an external event. The user triggers ASSET.FINANCE-RECORD.EVENT-ARRANGEMENT in the system to register this external event. System prompts an alert message that a fee is levied for the activity.

System schedules the delivery fee to be collected along with the first payment.

### 1.23  Hybrid Pooling


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Key Fields:** *AA Bundle ID*, *Align Dates*, *Alt Acct Id*, *Alt Acct Type*, *Alt Id Type*, *Alternate Id*, *Alternate Id Type*, *Back-to-Back FX* ... +27 more
>

#### 🔧 Working With

The below are the different process to create a hybrid cash pool:

| Process | Activity | System/User |
|---|---|---|
| Create pool in pending live | BUNDLE-NEW.OFFER-ARRANGEMENT | Orchestration service |
| Create accounts in pending live | ACCOUNTS-NEW.OFFER-ARRANGEMENT | Orchestration service |
| Set go live date for pool | BUNDLE-UPDATE.LIVE.DATE-PRODUCT.BUNDLE | User |
| Set go live date for accounts in pool (be spoke) | BUNDLE-RESTRUCTURE-BUNDLE.HIERARCHY | User |
| Bring accounts to Live | ACCOUNTS-NEW-ARRANGEMENT | Scheduled by orchestration service and processed by COB orchestration process |
| Bring pool to live | BUNDLE-NEW-ARRANGEMENT | User/CB Orchestration process |
| Add standalone account | ACCOUNTS-TRANSFORM-ARRANGEMENT | Scheduled by orchestration service and processed by COB orchestration process |
| Remove pool account | ACCOUNTS-TRANSFORM-ARRANGEMENT | Scheduled by orchestration service and processed by COB orchestration process |
| Close pool account | ACCOUNTS-SETTLE-PAYOFF | Scheduled by orchestration service and processed by COB orchestration process |

This section describes the steps and sequences to be followed, to manually create the various account part of a BN pool structure.

The navigation is as follows,

- Product Catalog.
- Select Product Catalog from the User Menu

> **⚠️ Note:** These accounts (including the master account bundle arrangement) can be created forward dated. They are activated by the system at SOD on that date.

Create CT accounts in the desired currencies.

- Switch off settlement instructions on pay-in and pay-out sides.

Create a new bundle arrangement under the master account product.

- Attach the CTs to the product bundle.
- Identify the currency of the master account and choose the corresponding CT account to be the recipient of the bundle.

Create summary or transaction account in the order of the hierarchy.

- The parent must be created first before creating the child.
- If TR1 has its parent as CS1, which has its parent as SA1, then SA1 is created, followed by CS1 and then TR1.
- Once an account is created, its parent can only be set or changed through the purpose built internal restructuring activity.
- Normal Update-Account activity cannot be used.
- Similarly, once an account is created, the bundle arrangement (master account) and link account number (CT account) can be updated through the purpose built External Restructuring Activity.
- Switch off settlement instructions on pay-in and pay-out sides.
- Once the accounts are created, the normal workflow on updating their conditions are to be followed through the arrangement overview. The new activity drilldown links to setup, Bank interest or fees or schedule and settlement Internal interest or fees or schedule and settlement conditions.


###### Generating IBAN

When the Bundle for the master account product is created in Draft status and when it is subsequently moved to the New Offer status, the IBAN is generated based on the values defined for Generate Iban and Alt Id Type . The IBAN can be seen in the AA.ARRANGEMENT record of the underlying contract.

As displaying the entire IBAN Value on the card is not feasible, it displays few characters of IBAN and appends it with three dots , for example, GB12DEMO60161300087537 is displayed as GB12DEMO6061…; on hovering over the text it displays the full string value.

The Alternate Id Type and Alternate Id of the Alt Id Types can be viewed in the expand header of each card. For the accounts other than master, T24.IBAN value gets displayed on the card instead of Account ID. If T24.IBAN value is available, the Alt Acct Type and Alt Acct Id get displayed on the expand card header.

When creating the CT accounts except for Limit (in case of MCCFor SCCF or MCF or SCF) is updated, no other special attribute needs to be specified to attach it to a master account, since it is done through the UPDATE-PRODUCT.BUNDLE activity. The user does this activity directly on the bundle arrangement (master account).

Once the CTs and MAs are created, when creating SA or CS or TR or MTR, it is important to capture the pool and hierarchy details via the purpose built attributes in Account property.

The following is a screenshot of a TR being created new, attached to an existing Pool under SA1 as its parent. The navigation for this could either be from the Product Catalog or the Master Account Overview.

The Master account is the bundle arrangement.

- If the account added or created is in a different Temenos Transact company than the master account, then the master account reference must be captured suffixed with its company mnemonic. In the example above, since the master account is in Temenos Transact Company BNK, it must be captured as AA1710732QS1/BNK for the system to recognise it.
- Linked Account number is the CT Account. If left blank and if a valid CT in this currency exists, then the system would default it. If a value is entered, the system validates that it is a valid participant in this Bundle Arrangement and that its currency matches this account’s currency.

- Parent account is used to capture the parent in the hierarchy. It is an optional field and when left blank, it mean the account being created would be added to the pool directly under the master account level.
- If a value is entered, the system would validate that it is, A valid member of the Bundle Hierarchy An allowed parent of this account Enabled for multi-currency if its currency is different from that of this account’s currency

In case of opening CS or SA, the above rules hold true except for the Linked Account Number (for which input is allowed).

The accounts in the BN pool can be internally moved (at any point). To facilitate this, the ACCOUNTS-CHANGE.PARENT-ARRANGEMENT activity is initiated from the New Activity menu.

During this process happens, the balances from the previously linked parent account is also transferred.

The above screenshot shows a TR account linked to SA account 2000003347. The SA and linked TR account’s balances are the same.

From the New Activity menu in the TR account, the User activity ACCOUNTS-CHANGE.PARENT-ARRANGEMENT is initiated.

For a restructuring, this activity runs at COB, hence, the Effective Date needs to be day + 1. The new parent account is changed to 2000003355, which is the new SA account. After authorisation and a COB is run, the restructure process is initiated.

The above screenshot shows that the balance (USD 88,592.08) is moved from (2000003347) to (2000003355) account.

This section enables the user to understand creation of BN pool.

BN structure creation process starts from creating a master arrangement in a draft status. The user can provide the necessary details to create the master arrangement by selecting the NEW STRUCTURE tab in Graphical User Interface (GUI). Mandatory information is Product Name, Country (on which the Master arrangement is created), Currency (master account) and Structure Name (optional).

To create a new BN structure, from the GENERAL TRADING screen,

1. Click NEW STRUCTURE .
2. Enter the mandatory information and then click CREATE . The master arrangement is created in view mode.
3. Click to add new accounts to BN structure. The symbol is enabled.
4. Click to add new accounts to the BN structure. The Add Account to Structure pop-up window opens.
5. Select the respective account type to add a new accounts to the pool. Standalone accounts can be selected and added to the BN structure by filtering the accounts by Currency.
6. Click to add multiple accounts to the pool. Example: To add two SA accounts, select the currency and company from the drop-down list. Once the account placed holder is created, click OK to create the placeholder card in GUI.
7. Click Save to save the BN pool structure in GUI. GUI passes the information to Temenos Transact to store the placeholder details. The user can save the changes in GUI after the BN pool structure is approved by corporate. When the user saves the Master arrangement in GUI, Temenos Transact does not any validation.

The BN structure can be edited and updated with new accounts and removal account by selecting the edit options. The Draft BN structure can be edited with the following details.

- Adding new placeholders
- Removing placeholder accounts
- Changing Parent details
- Adding Standalone accounts
- Adding a new parent placeholder for child accounts

Click Validate and Commit . The CT placeholders are created automatically. CT account is opened in Master account company for each currency of TR accounts.

To disconnect account placeholder, Click on each cards. The account card is removed immediately from the BN pool structure. When the Summary Account (SA) or Currency Summary (CS) placeholders are removed from BN pool, the child accounts are linked to the immediate parent. The parent accounts can be removed along with the child accounts from BN pool.

> **⚠️ Note:** Account number is not generated in Temenos Transact, hence the conversion of TR account to standalone is not possible.

To add standalone accounts to BN pool, click on the respective cards.

> **⚠️ Note:** This icon is enabled only for Master or SA or CS accounts.

Standalone accounts can be added under SA and CS account or directly under the master arrangement without any parent. Until the BN pool becomes live, the standalone account terms and conditions remains the same. Once the live date reaches, the account is converted to TR and the new product conditions applies. The account number remains the same as standalone account and only the change product activity is triggered.

Export. The BN structure can be exported as PDF, HTML, Excel, Power Point and Word. The exported BN structure is produced with the corporate customer for any modifications or changes in the structure. BN structure can be exported during Draft, Preliminary and Live status.

Go Preliminary to move the pool to preliminary. To move the pool to Preliminary status, the Pool Orchestration Service is run after committing the Activity. Once the Go Preliminary is triggered on a particular BN pool, the user can click on top-left and GUI displays the GUI landing page.

This section enables maintenance of cover control

This option is available in Tools menu. Click Edit to update the cover control setup. Accounts part of BN pool are listed as tree view and the changes can be updated in each account. Cover control on CT accounts are not applicable and hence the options are not enabled. Enable Apply settings to sub-structure to copy the cover control setup to child accounts.

Credit check is set for internal or external transactions or both. When the options is Null, the credit is applied during the transaction processing. Click Save to update the changes in Temenos Transact.

Click Edit to add new SA,CS,TR or MTR accounts in preliminary BN structure. The similar process is followed in Draft to add new accounts in preliminary. The user can commit the changes once the placeholders are created. Once the BN pool is committed in GUI, account number is generated immediately in Temenos Transact and appears on each card. The user can update the terms and conditions for the new account created in BN Pool.

To sets the Global Go Live Date from CARD VIEW Click Go Live on top-right of the BN Pool structure in GUI.

In the below screen, the Global Go Live is set for Bundle arrangements and the custom Go Live date option is for individual accounts part of BN Pool structure. Set the Global Go Live Date first and then the customer go live date, else an error message is displayed. Custom Go Live date is an optional input, participant accounts in BN pool goes live with the same date as Master or Bundle go live. When the go live date is set for individual accounts, then the accounts are live only on that particular date. Transactions are not allowed until the accounts are moved to LIVE.

The Custom go live date can be the same as Master live date as or later than Master live date. Temenos Transact displays an error message when the customer go live date is before Master live date.

This section enables maintenance of CT Accounts

CT Account

CT accounts provides static information of accounts such as CUSTOMER NAME, CUSTOMER ID, ACCOUNT NUMBER, STATUS and SCHEDULED CHANGES. CT expand card also has an option to setup or amend the interest conditions. When the limit is available for the CT account, GUI allows editing of limit on CT accounts.

CT Account Transactions

CT Account balances

Limit Conditions

To update or amend the limit records, click Edit. Once the changes and amendments are done, click Commit to submit the changes in Temenos transact.

Interest Conditions

Click Interest conditions on CT account in expand view, the version of Interest calculations are launched. The interest activity can be set with immediate effort or for a future effective date. On committing the changes, GUI passes the information to Temeons Transact to update interest details.

Summary Account/Currency Summary

SA account provides the static information of accounts such as CUSTOMER NAME , CUSTOMER ID , ACCOUNT NUMBER , STATUS and SCHEDULE CHANGES . It provides the combined balances of all the child accounts linked under the SA accounts. It is multi-currency accounts; hence, any allowed currencies can be linked to SA. When the SA account is having a multi-currency child accounts, then the balance is combined to SA account currency. SA expand card can setup or amend interest conditions and internal cover control.

When the user clicks on Interest condition, the respective version is launched to update the internal interest conditions. Manage Limit option allows the user to setup the internal and external cover control. Manage limit version is launched and the GUI allows to update and commit the changes.

TR Account

Expanded view of TR account provides the static information of accounts such as CUSTOMER NAME , CUSTOMER ID , ACCOUNT NUMBER , STATUS and Schedule Changes. TR account provides the balances and transactions of the respective TR accounts. The user can view the transactions by providing the start and end date. TR expand card can setup or amend interest conditions and internal cover control.

When the user clicks on Interest condition, the respective version is launched to update the internal interest conditions. Manage Limit option allows the user to setup the internal and external cover control. Manage limit version is launched and the GUI allows to update and commit the changes.

TR Account Transfer Services

Setting Future Internal STO/Sweeps

Linked Account Number is the CT account. If this field is left blank and when a valid CT in this currency exists, then the system defaults it.

- When a value is entered in this field, the system checks if it is a valid participant in the bundle arrangement and currency matches the account’s currency.

Parent Account is used to capture the parent in the hierarchy. It is an optional field and when left blank, the account created is added to the pool directly under the master account level. When a value is entered in this field, the system validates if it is,

- A valid member of the bundle hierarchy
- An allowed parent of this account
- Enabled for multi-currency (if the currency is different from that of the account’s currency)

> **⚠️ Note:** The above rules hold true when opening CS or SA, (except for the Linked Account Number for which input is not allowed).
