#### 📖 Introduction

Product bundles are defined using the Product Bundle Property Class. The Product Bundle Property Class is used to store the arrangements that form a part of a Bundle. It stores the Recipient arrangement, which is marked with the INTEREST.COMPENSATION Property name in the Master Type attribute and the Donor Product Groups, with the Mandatory attribute set to either Yes or No. The Product Bundle Property Class also provides the option to delegate the Bundle constitution rules to the Product Qualifier when the RULE BASED tab is selected in the Bundle Constitution attribute.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The AA.PRODUCT.LINE table provides a high level definition of the business components (Property Classes) that may be required to construct a product belonging to that line. For example, the Bundle Product Line enables the users to design and service Bundle products such as:

- Offset Mortgage
- Interest Compensation
- Interest upgrade
- Bonus Interest

The Product Lines are defined by Temenos and cannot be created by the user.

A Product Line is described by the Property Classes which constitute it. A financial institution may then use these building blocks of functionality to construct the individual products which are available for sale to its customers.

The Bundle Product Line has the Replay line attribute indicating Reverse Replay functionality is available for this Product Line. Bundle being a non-financial Product Line does not have the Currency line attribute.

The Property Classes available for Bundle Product Line are:

| Property Class | Mandatory |
|---|---|
| Customer | Yes |
| Product Bundle | Yes |
| Interest Compensation | No |
| Constraint | No |
| Activity Api | No |
| Activity Messaging | No |
| Activity Presentation | No |
| Alerts | No |
| Eligibility | No |
| Bundle Hierarchy | No |
| Settlement | No |
| Pricing Rules | No |
| Charge | No |
| Payment Schedule | No |
| Activity Charges | No |
| Tax | No |
| Periodic Charges | No |
| Charge Override | No |
| Limit | No |
| Interest | No |
| Inheritance | No |
| Property Control | No |
| Activity Restriction | No |
| Activity Mapping | No |

In the above example shown for Bundle, it can be seen in total the AA.PROPERTY.CLASS records that constitute a Bundle Product. The minimum required classes are marked as mandatory YES and the optional ones are marked as NO.

The mandatory classes govern the minimum required components when creating a new product in the subsequent AA.PRODUCT.GROUP and AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER records. However, although a particular class may not be mandatory at a Product Line level, the option is available to further define mandatory classes at the AA.PRODUCT.GROUP stage, which further controls the overall consolidated mandatory classes per Product defined.

Banks can confine certain products to be only part of a Bundle. The Bundle Only attribute in Product Designer is used for this purpose. For example, if a Savings Account Product is offered only as part of a Bundle, then the Bundle Only attribute should be set to Yes for this savings account.


##### IBAN in Bundles

The Bundle Product is a non-financial Product Line as a result of which there is no system-driven option to generate an IBAN for the master arrangement. Hence to generate an IBAN, a customised routine has to be attached in the Alt Acct Gen Api field of ALT.ACCOUNT.PARAMETER .

Read Product Bundle Property Class user guide for more information.


##### Activity Mapping in Bundle

The Event Ref and Event Activity attributes are used to map the Participant Events (TEC.ITEMS) to the relevant Bundle Activity. The event mapping is done only for the online events in the Bundle Product Line.

> **⚠️ Note:** Activity Mapping in Bundle Product Line does not allow input for TRANSACTION, TXN.ACTIVITY, DEF.CR.ACTIVITY and DEF.DB.ACTIVITY.


##### AA.ACTIVITY.CLASS

Each record in AA.ACTIVITY.CLASS defines the list of actions to be applied on the given list of Property Classes for a given process in the Activity.

Temenos releases AA.ACTIVITY.CLASS records for Product Lines and its Property Classes or the arrangement.

When the properties are linked to AA.PRODUCT.GROUP , the system generates records in AA.ACTIVITY which are property-specific named instances of AA.ACTIVITY.CLASS .

An activity definition is linked to the AA.ACTIVITY.CLASS . When the activity is triggered, the actions to process are determined by referring to the Activity class.

The following records in AA.ACTIVITY.CLASS are released for the Bundle Product Line: BUNDLE-NEW-ARRANGEMENT BUNDLE-RENEGOTIATE-ARRANGEMENT BUNDLE-UPDATE-INTEREST.COMPENSATION BUNDLE-UPDATE-PRODUCT.BUNDLE


##### Triggering Activities on Bundle

Using TEC, the user can trigger an activity on a Bundle based on an event happening on its Participant arrangement (Closing the Participant Account). To make this possible, additional configuration is required to map the events on the participants to the Bundle Activities.


##### Preconfigured Events (TEC Items)

The following events come pre-configured in the system. These are used in the Activity Mapping so that whenever an account that is part of a Bundle is closed or has its product changed, it can result in the appropriate Activity on the Bundle.


##### TEC Items

- In the below screenshot, when a qualified event (for example, CLOSE-ARRANGEMENT-ACTIVITY) is raised in an (Bundle participant) arrangement ‘A’, TEC publishes the event.
- The published event is consumed by AA Linked Arrangement subscriber to do the following: Finds if there are any linked arrangements to arrangement ‘A’ Finds if the linked arrangement (if any) is impacted by the event Raises the mapped AA Activity on the linked arrangement if the arrangement is interested with the event Hands off the Activities to AA Process Activities
- The AA Process Activity runs the Activity, which in turn triggers the Product Qualifier Rules.
- The Product Qualifier rule evaluation may result in the following outcomes: Change Product Close Arrangement Log/Event


##### Retail Bundle Services

The following services are associated with Retail Bundle.

| Service Name | What the service does | COB Stage / Online | Trigger | Dependent / Related Processes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| AA.SERVICE.PROCESS | Performs the processing of all scheduled activities. The process checks all current arrangement contracts to see if there a scheduled Activity due to be processed as part of the Close of Business. | S022 |  |  |
| AA.COB.PAY.IN.OUT | This job submits and completes processing of AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY requests generated by non-AA transactions during Close of Business. | D250 |  |  |


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic helps the user to open a bundle arrangement and understand its features.


##### Opening a Bundle Arrangement

To open a Bundle arrangement,

1. Using the menu, select Product Catalog from the list of options available. The following page appears.
2. Expand the Bundle Product Line drop-down and then Retail Accounts Bundle . The products available under the Retail Accounts Bundle appear.
3. Select the relevant product using the icon and enter the required details such as Customer and Effective Date .
4. Validate the contract.
5. Add the additional requirements to the relevant conditions tabs as required and commit the contract. In the example above, two current accounts are added to the Bundle. The bundle details are updated after running the AA.PROCESS.ACTIVITY service or after COB.


##### Other Features

The following are some additional features to be noted:

- Interest Compensation is the amount calculated based on the combined balance (credit and debit) of donors. Donors can mention both credit balance and debit balance.
- All the donors contribute their credit and debit balances to a pool, combine all their balances and then one interest is calculated that can be used for donation.
- The participation of recipient and donors is for processing interest. Depending on the need, the donors can be removed or replaced and Bundle can be closed.

Read Interest Compensation for more information.


##### Donor

Donor participants donate their balances to the recipient. In a Product Bundle, the donors should provide the information as highlighted in the below screenshot.

The attributes and their activities in the Donor section are as follows:

Balance for Compensation

Each donor can specify both the credit balance and debit balance; the donor can also specify multiple balances to be donated.

For compensation purpose, the donor can mention the balance type. If the balance type is not specified, then it means that the donor is not going to donate any balance to the recipient.

This feature is also useful when a donor is needed to suppress their interest which would otherwise accrue based on unauthorised overdraft balances.

Donate

It is important to mention the balance type from which the balance should be used for offset.

There is an allowance to specify the Donate attribute only when the Balance for Compensation attribute is specified (without leaving blank) since the donor balance type can have credit balance or debit balance in a given day. For example, offset only the Credit Balance of the Current Account for an Offset Mortgage.

Interest Property

It is recommended to mention which Interest Property will be affected in the Bundle arrangement. The affected Interest Property should be mentioned and all other properties continue normal processing.

Accrual Type

Until now, the accrual type is used either for calculation purpose or suppress purpose. Donors can now continue maintaining accrual details for only information purpose by setting the Accrual Property as INFO ONLY. These accrual details are maintained in separate set of attributes ( a copy of current interest accrual attributes) in AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS .

Recipient

Recipient participants receive donation from the donors. In a Product Bundle, the recipients should provide the information as highlighted in the below screenshot:

Recipient Property

For a recipient, there is a facility to mention multiple recipient properties which can include credit interest properties as well as debit interest properties.

On a given day, if the consolidated balance is credited, then both the CRINTEREST and CR2INTEREST are accrued on the balance (highlighted in the screenshot) on the same day.

Max Offset %

It is the maximum percentage of the recipient balance that can be offset by the donation. In case of interest compensation, leaving the attribute empty indicates that there is no offset but only consolidation of donor and recipient balances to calculate interest.

In an offset mortgage, let the principal is -85,000. If the donor balances amount to credit +100,000, then specifying Max Offset % as 100 would mean that only 85,000 of the credit balances are offset against the Recipient’s debit balance.


##### Bundle Closure

A Product Bundle can be closed when needed. Before closing a Product Bundle, all the participants can be de-linked instead of being closed. Then the de-linked participants behave as independent participants.

When closing a donor participant, stop the closure, force the user to change or close the Bundle, and then close the donor participant.

Follow the same procedure in case of recipient participate also. While closing a donor or recipient, the validation should be done at preliminary stages of closure process. For example, in case of AR, validation should be done at REQUEST.CLOSURE stage.

A forward-dated Bundle closure is also possible which allows closing the Bundle on the scheduled date. During SOD of scheduled date, the system automatically executes Bundle Closure Activity.


##### Amend Bundle Participants

Amending Bundle participants includes adding a new donor, removing an existing donor and changing an existing recipient.

- A donor can be added by setting a right interest Property (suppress or info only or calculate). A donor can be removed by de-linking from the Product Bundle.
- An existing recipient cannot be removed but there is an option to change the existing recipient. To change the recipient, the existing recipient needs to be de-linked first and the new recipient should be uploaded.


##### Back Dated Transactions

There is a possibility of backdated transactions on donors and recipient for recalculation or adjustment of accrual interest (for current period), or capitalised interest and accrual interest (for previous period).

When an event notification or activity is run on the Bundle arrangement to indicate the interest needs to be recalculated, the effective date of this activity would be the same as the originating back dated activity or transaction.

This activity should trigger reverse and replay on the Bundle arrangement and interest recalculation on the recipient arrangement.


##### Interim Capitalisation

There is possibility for the user to capitalise the interest on any Interest Property without allowing scheduled capitalisation dates being cycled. For example, if the scheduled capitalisation is 31st of every month. Even if the interim capitalisation was done on the 16th of the same month, the next capitalisation should still be 31st of that month.

Back-dated interim capitalisation (the accrued interest gets capitalised as of the back valued date) is allowed and forward dated capitalisation is not allowed.


##### Bundle Definition by Product

The following section describes the specification of participants at the product level:

- Banks can restrict the type of products in a Product Bundle so that the participants belonging to the restricted product are also restricted in the Product Bundle.
- The definition of a Product Bundle is enhanced to allow specification of participants at the product level. To be a part in Bundle, a participant should belong to an eligible product (or change to eligible product).
- For example, if a Notional Pooling allows a checking account product to be a participant, then an existing normal current account needs to be changed to a checking account product before it can be added to a Bundle.
- It is possible to specify the Product Group of the participating arrangement as part of the Bundle Product condition.
- So, as in the above example, both the checking account and normal current account are in the same group and the Bundle definition cannot be made specific to restrict the normal current account from being added to a Bundle.
- In the above example (screenshot), both GROUP.CHECKING and GROUP.SUBSIDIARY are part of the CURRENT.ACCOUNT Product group. By specifying the Product, it is possible to restrict which Products under the given Product group are allowed to be part of this Bundle.
- After the arrangement is added to a Bundle, it is possible for a user to change the product on that participating arrangement to another product, which is not eligible in the Bundle.
- While changing the product (Loan/Deposit/Account), the system checks if the product is part of any Bundle. If so, it checks if the arrangement has been specified at Product level or Product Group level.
- If the specification is at the Product level, then it raises an error to stop the Change Product Activity and force the user to remove the arrangement from the Bundle before proceeding with the Change Product.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Create Product Bundle

There are no Tasks available for Bundle Definition feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

Bundle arrangement is not a financial arrangement. It establishes the link between the Recipient and Donor arrangements. The user can create bundle arrangements for card package, loan offset, master account, account bundles and retail packages.


##### Enquiries and Reports

In Bundle Definition, the user can view the following enquiries and reports:

Overview Icon

Bundle overview gives an overview of the entire bundle arrangement and its critical properties like arrangement part of bundles, interest compensation, balances, activity log and so on.

Bundle Participants

This enquiry displays the list of various arrangements and its type of linkage to the bundle like recipients and donors. Click the View icon corresponding to a record to view the financial arrangement overview.

Balances/Accruals

This enquiry displays details about the combined balances or accruals of all the financial arrangements linked to the bundle.

Activity Log

This enquiry displays the various activities triggered in the bundle along with the date.


##### SWIFT Messages

NA


##### Alerts

NA


##### Advices

### 2.9  BundleOnly


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Bundle Only option allows the user to keep the arrangements in restricted mode until the arrangement is bundled with other products. In order to make the Bundle Only arrangement live, the user must tie the arrangement with other arrangements as a Bundled Product.*

#### 📖 Introduction

The Bundle Only option allows the user to keep the arrangements in restricted mode until the arrangement is bundled with other products. In order to make the Bundle Only arrangement live, the user must tie the arrangement with other arrangements as a Bundled Product.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Product Designer ( AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER ) allows the user to define if the Product created has to be part of a Bundle – Bundle Only attribute helps to define the status.


#### 🔧 Working With

Arrangements created with Bundle Only Products are kept in Restricted Mode until the arrangement is bundled with other Product(s).

- Any transactions initiated while the arrangement is in Restriction Mode leads to an override.
- The below overrides can be converted as errors, if required. Override while creating new arrangement is shown below. Override in FUNDS.TRANSFER application is shown below.
- The arrangements become live once they are attached to an active Bundled Product.
- Upon attaching the arrangements with Bundled Products, the restrictions on the arrangement are withdrawn.
- The restrictions are reinstated on the arrangement based on eligibility rules when the Bundled Product is amended, settled, or dissolved.
- On the other hand, closing this Bundle Only Product generates an Activity on the Bundle. This event could then be configured to run the qualifier rules on the Bundle and result in automatic dissolution of the Bundle.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Create Product Bundle

There are no Tasks available for Bundle Only feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Bundle Only feature.


> **Related Applications:** `AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER`, `FUNDS.TRANSFER`

### 2.10  ChargesInBundles


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Bundle Product Line and Bundle Arrangements if configured have the ability to generate charges. Arrangements still function like a Non-Financial (NF) arrangement but a financial settlement account can be linked which is used to process the charges.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ACTIVITY.CLASS`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Amortisation TermResidual AmountProg Pay PercPercentageActual AmtAuto SettleOn ActivityRecalculateRecalc FrequencyApply PaymentInclude Prin PaymentBills CombinedGroup Bill TypeGroup Min Amount*, *Auto Settle*, *Charge Auto Settle*, *Comparison Type*, *Default Finan Com*, *Default Settlement Account*, *Handoff Charge*, *Payment Method* ... +2 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

The Bundle Product Line and Bundle Arrangements if configured have the ability to generate charges. Arrangements still function like a Non-Financial (NF) arrangement but a financial settlement account can be linked which is used to process the charges.

The Property Class available in the Bundle Product Line are shown below:

- Activity Charges
- Charge
- Payment Schedule
- Periodic Charges
- Charge Override
- Tax
- Settlement

The AA framework and its usual configuration can be used in building the Bundle Products and each one of the above Property Class acts as the building blocks to generate the appropriate Charge.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

This topic helps the user to configure the various charges in Bundles.


##### Charges in Bundles

By adding charge to the Bundle Product Line, both the debit and credit charge type can be configured. Since this is on a non-financial arrangement, there are no balances and transactions processed on the arrangement.

Charges defined can either be fixed charge and a calculated charge based upon Activity Count or a routine based calculated charge. Product designer of Bundle Product allows Calculation Sources to be defined only for the routine based calculations.

To map the charge created to a Non-Financial Arrangement and collect or pay it to a financial arrangement, Handoff Charge in Charge should be set as Yes.


##### Activity Charges

Activity Charges allows charges to be triggered on an event, that is, an Activity. It also offers a feature to settle some charges with funds from UNC (Un-specified Credit). As there is no UNC balance on the non-financial (NF) arrangement like Bundle, the following validation is added.

| Attribute | Validation |
|---|---|
| Charge Auto Settle | Only NULL or NO is valid |
| Settle Activity | No input allowed |
| Auto Settle | Only NULL or NO is valid |


##### Periodic Charges

Periodic Charges can be added to a schedule of a non-financial arrangement to both cater for deferred charges (from Activity Charges) and cater for calculated charges based on number of activities over a period of time.


##### Payment Schedule

Payment Schedule is designed to handle both incoming and outgoing payments and calculations for all of the financial Product Lines. For non-financial products, the use of this Property Class will be restricted to the scheduling of Charge properties or Periodic Charge properties.

For the Bundle Product alone, Payment schedule condition will be allowed to be defined without a currency, since the amount is going to defined / calculated from the currency specific definition in charge or periodic charge Property condition.

This validation will be relaxed only for the Bundle Product Line and still insist on currency specific definition for any other financial Products.

Definition of payment method ‘Maintain’ would be restricted as it can be only used for account Property Class.

| Attribute | Validation |
|---|---|
| Payment Type | Only AA.PAYMENT.TYPE records with CALC.TYPE equal to ACTUAL and TYPE equal to calculated are allowed. Additionally MAND.PROP.CLASS can either be null or only contain CHARGE or PERIODIC.CHARGE. |
| Payment Method | Pay and Due values are allowed but Maintain and Capitalize are not allowed. |
| Amortisation Term Residual Amount Prog Pay Perc Percentage Actual Amt Auto Settle On Activity Recalculate Recalc Frequency Apply Payment Include Prin Payment Bills Combined Group Bill Type Group Min Amount | These are no-input fields. |


##### Settlement

To settle a charge, the user has to specify the settlement account arrangement using Settlement Property Class. For charge processing and generation of the bill, the Settlement Property Class and the Default Settlement Account attribute are used to link the actual AR account.

> **⚠️ Note:** Linked settlement arrangement cannot be closed until the Arrangement is delinked. Ensure to add the Charge Property in the Bundle to the AR Account that is set as Settlement Account.


##### Charge Override

Besides negotiating a charge at the Arrangement level, the user may wish to change or waive a charge at the time it is assessed (For example, Activity Charge or Activity Restriction Charge). In order to accommodate this, the Charge Override Property Class is added to the Bundle Product Line.

> **⚠️ Note:** Once a charge has been raised and passed onto the settlement account if the user then wants to change or waive the charge, it has to be done on the settlement account itself.

Bills enquiry in the Bundle Arrangement lists all the bills, which was raised by it in the settlement arrangement. Each bill can trigger ACCOUNTS-ADJUST.BILL-BALANCE.MAINTENANCE on the settle account arrangement.


##### Tax

In certain circumstances, there may be a requirement to deduct tax from any generated charges. Using the Tax Property Class in the system, AA and its Products can be configured to calculate and raise any such taxes on any defined Charges (Fees).

The Tax Property Class is included in the non-financial (Bundle) Product Line.


##### Currency impact for Bundle Arrangements

- For a financial Product, the financial Property Classes must have Product Conditions in the Available Currency.
- For a non-financial Product like Bundle Product Line, the financial Property Classes must have Product Conditions in the Currency of the financial table file (FTD) – the Local Currency of the Company in the Default Finan Com attribute.
- Proofing errors are raised in the absence of the Product Conditions in this currency.
- For instance, when a Bundle Product is released in EU1 Company, the Product Condition for these financial Property Classes will be validated against Default Finan Com Company’s Local Currency.


##### Charge Setup on Bundle Arrangement

In a Bundle Arrangement (a non-financial Arrangement), it is possible to specify Charges at the bundle arrangement level with its own schedule (or event based) and have it settled against a designated account (using the Settlement Property Class).


##### Periodic Attributes in Bundle

The Periodic Attribute Class namely Bundle Participant Count can be used to calculate the participant count and compare it with arrangement values.

In this illustration, Comparison Type is set as MINIMUM . The system can evaluate the minimum number of participant arrangements and use it for evaluating the rules specified in Product Bundle.


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic helps the user to understand the processing after configuring the charges in Bundles.


##### Charge Processing in Bundle

Defining a charge on a Bundle product results in the charge being raised on the settlement account.

- There are three main components in the processing: Non-Financial Arrangement (NF) – This is where the charge is raised (Bundle) Event Processing Framework – A mechanism to communicate between arrangements Financial Arrangement (F) – This is where the charge is settled, an AR account.
- The Non-financial (Bundle) arrangement is where the charge is defined and raised.
- The Make Due and Capitalise activities do three main tasks: Calculate the Charge Create the Bill Raise Accounting
- The DEFER Activities eventually trigger their corresponding Make Due or Capitalise Activity on the deferred to date.
- The non-financial arrangement is only responsible for the first task and raises an event; the financial arrangement does the second and the third tasks.
- As such the non-financial arrangement uses these three Activity Classes: -RAISE.CHARGE-CHARGE -RAISE.CHARGE-PAYMENT.SCHEDULE -RAISE.CHARGE-PERIODIC.CHARGE
- These Activity Classes are responsible for calculating and populating AA.CHARGE.DETAILS and raising a charge event with the details necessary for the Financial Arrangement.

Charge Details

The RAISE.CHARGE Activity determines the charge and creates records in AA.CHARGE.DETAILS .

This contains all of the standard details on how a charge was calculated. Details of any adjustments or waiving of the charge are also included.


##### Charge Event

Once the charge has been calculated and the charge details record is populated, the Activity must then raise an AA event (for example, Charge Raised). The event must contain:

- Details about the arrangement and activity that raised the charge
- Details about how the charge will be settled (for example, the ID of the financial arrangement, Due vs. Cap, and so on.)
- Dates (both the date of the charge and a deferral date if the charge is configured for deferral)


##### Event Processing Framework

A generic arrangement to arrangement Event Messaging framework communicates between the non-financial and financial arrangements.


##### Financial Arrangement

To settle a charge raised on non-financial arrangement, the AA event processing raises an Activity on the financial arrangement. The financial arrangement does the further processing using below Activity Classes:

- -MAKEDUE.CHARGE-
- -CAPITALISE.CHARGE-
- -DEFER.MAKEDUE.CHARGE-
- -DEFER.CAPITALISE.CHARGE-

These Activity classes are used for both CHARGE and PERIODIC.CHARGE Property charges. They are responsible for creating records in AA.BILL.DETAILS and all the accounting.

Bill Details

Non-financial arrangement does not create bills, but the financial arrangement, which completes the settlement of the charge. The user has an option to modify or waive the charge (for DUE or PAY) before it is settled.


##### Accounting and Balances

All accounting and charge balances are handled at the financial arrangement level. Accounting rule definition for all the charges in non-financial arrangement (Bundle) are taken from the financial arrangement, which is linked as the settlement account.

- The system validates if the Accounting condition defined has at least one Charge or Periodic Charge Property Class.
- The Charge Property or Periodic Charge Property used in the Bundle arrangement should also be part of the Settlement Account arrangement.
- The Product Condition attached for the Charge/Periodic Charge Property does not affect the Bundle Charge/Periodic Charge Property (a null charge can be attached in the Settlement Account arrangement).

It is possible to define the Accounting Rules for the Charge or Periodic Charge in the Account arrangement.


##### Reverse and Replay

Once a charge is raised and handed off to the event service for processing, any reversed activities or backdated activities on the non-financial arrangement does not impact the charge raised. Also, the Activity raised on the financial arrangement cannot be reversed.


##### Ad-hoc Charges

To collect adhoc charges AA.ACTIVITY.CLASS namely BUNDLE-CHARGE.ADHOC-ARRANGEMENT. This is a user-initiated activity. When configured, this can be linked as an Activity Charge and with usual configuration, the required charges are generated.


#### 📋 Tasks

Related topics:

- Create Product Bundle

There are no Tasks available for Charges in Bundles feature.


#### 📊 Outputs

There are no Outputs available for Charges in Bundles feature.


> **Related Applications:** `AA.ACTIVITY.CLASS`

### 2.11  InterestCompensation


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Interest Compensation Property is used to store the source and target Interest properties such as Recipient Product Group and its Property, the Donor Product Group and its Property, and so on. It also stores whether interest calculation of the Donor arrangements at their arrangement level have to be...*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS`, `AA.SOURCE.CALC.TYPE`, `The AA.ARR.INTEREST`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Arrangement*, *Arrangement Type*, *Balance for Compensation*, *Book Date*, *Calc Type*, *Customer*, *Donate*, *Link Arrange* ... +8 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Interest Compensation Property is used to store the source and target Interest properties such as Recipient Product Group and its Property, the Donor Product Group and its Property, and so on. It also stores whether interest calculation of the Donor arrangements at their arrangement level have to be calculated or suppressed even when the Recipient arrangement does the interest calculation with the Recipient Property.

Notional Pooling in a Bundle can be enabled by configuring the Interest Compensation Property Class and its associated attributes.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Interest Compensation feature is used in a Bundle Product, where the user can define the Product Groups, that can form the Donor and Recipient Product Groups.

Refer Interest Compensation Property Class for further details.

The user is allowed to configure the attributes at the product or arrangement level.

The Donor Product Group as per the Balance for Compensation and Donate attributes, contributes the balances to the recipient product, on which the Recipient Property calculates and stores interest as per the product condition attached at the recipient level.

Sample Product Conditions for Interest Compensation are shown below.

When a customer has multiple accounts in savings / current account product groups, a bonus interest can be paid on one of the accounts. All credit balances are netted for a composite balance.

Interest is calculated on this balance on the recipient product as an additional bonus interest. It maybe also be noted that Interest calculation continues on the donor products.

In the above example, while the interest on savings account (donor) continues to get posted, current (donor) account interest is suppressed and posted on the consolidated balance of all the accounts in the interest compensation current account.

When a customer has four different accounts, the interest can be credited in one of the accounts, which is the recipient account (Interest Compensation Account). Other accounts are the donor accounts. Calculation of interest is based on the combined balance of all the accounts. The interest rate applied is the credit interest rate as applicable to the recipient account. Interest calculation is switched off on the donor arrangements.

It may be noted that the recipient current account group has both credit interest and debit interest properties.

The donor is the CURBALANCE and donates both credit and debit balances towards DRINTEREST and CRINTEREST.

- The savings accounts interest credit interest is calculated for information purpose.
- The current account credit and debit interest calculations are suppressed.

When a customer has a loan and other accounts arrangements, it is possible to have interest accrual for the loan on the net balance of all the arrangements put together. The interest on associated savings or current arrangement is suppressed.

In the above example, the mortgage arrangement is the interest compensation account. The net balances of the savings account and the loan arrangement are combined to calculate the interest for the loan arrangement.

Here, Max Offset % gives the maximum percentage of the recipient balance that can be offset by the donation. Consider the principal is 85000 Dr in the mortgage loan, 80 percent in Max Offset% implies only 68,000 (80 percentage of 85,000) of the credit balance can be offset against the recipient’s debit balance. This field can be left blank to indicate 100 percentage offset.


##### Interest Calculation on Notional Pool

Notional Pooling is a mechanism for calculating interest on the combined credit and debit balances of accounts that a corporate parent chooses to cluster together, without actually transferring any funds. Banks can have regulations on the number of accounts to be held under a specific product group or a specific product to enable the notional pooling feature. In most cases, banks prefer to restrict the type of products that can be participants in a Bundle. A normal arrangement might need to be changed to an eligible product, for it to be part of a Bundle.

For example, if notional pooling allows only a certain type of checking account to be participants, then an existing normal current account might need to be changed to checking account product before it can be added to a Bundle.

In an Interest Compensation condition with Offset Type as Blank/Recipient:

Banks can have a group accounts concept intended for companies and organisations. The operative accounts can form part of the donor accounts and the recipient can be the actual checking accounts in the bank. In this case,

- Balances of the donors contribute to the recipient arrangement and adjust the recipient balance for interest calculation.
- Offset percentage input in Max Offset% is applied only on the recipient account balance.
- The default option is blank.

Consider a scenario, where the recipient or master account has only -100 balance, the sub-account A has -300 balance and sub-account B has +200 balance. Here the sub-accounts are the donors. Max Offset% is set as 50. Sum of interest cap amount on the originally charged is -10.

When Offset Type – Recipient or Blank

Only -50 (50 percentage of master account balance of -100) can be offset by credit balances in the donor. Hence, interest calculation applicable on the notional aggregate balance after offset correction is applied on (-50) = -50.

- 0.0833.

In an Interest Compensation condition with Offset Type as Pool:

The master account of the pool is the recipient accounts, and the sub account of the pool are the donor accounts. The balances are grouped as credit and debit balances and offset against each other subject to a Max Offset % . This feature is currently available only for Accounts Product Groups. This means the accounts can be notionally pooled to have a pool debit balance which can be offset with a pool debit balance (subject to a Max Offset % ) and the interest is calculated on the balance/s after the offset. The system allows the following:

- Maximum of two recipient properties.
- Recipient properties can be memo or real interest property.
- Max Offset % is allowed for only one of the recipient property for the other recipient property the Max Offset% should be entered as 100 or left blank (which defaults the same to 100). The bank can configure the debit balance to be offset with certain percentage, for which the Max Offset % can be indicated against the debit interest property. To fully offset with the debit balance with the credit balance Max Offset % can be left blank, indicating 100 percentage offset.

- The participants of the pool should have the same schedule frequency for Charge and Interest properties.
- For Memo Interest, in the Recipient Property, ensure the schedule for the memo interest property at the Product Condition Level or Arrangement Level is set to either Due or Pay.

Consider a scenario where the recipient or master account has only -100 balance, the sub-account A has -300 balance and sub-account B has +200 balance. Here sub-accounts are the donors. Max Offset% is set as 50 percentage. The sum of interest cap amount on the originally charged was -10.

When Offset Type – Pool

50 percentage offset is applied on (-100-300), then -200 is offset by the credit balance of the pool (since +200 is available in sub-account B). Hence, interest calculation applicable on the notional aggregate balance after offset correction gets applied on -200.

- 0.33.


##### Interest for Notional Pool Bundles

The system allows calculating an actual or real interest on the pool balance, that is, the interest on the total debit balance and credit balance of the pool, after considering the Max Offset % .

It is possible to suppress for the interest component at the donor product level (if the interest component is not suppressed at the Donor Product Level, interest gets calculated for the donor arrangement as well as the pool).

In the above scenario, the interest on the recipient current account, considering the pool balance, is made due, capitalised or paid to the master current account (as per the schedule configured for interest) and interest accruals at the individual donor current account are suppressed (irrespective of the schedule configured for the interest).

Thus, the system is configured for interest to be paid to the customer only on the pool balance and avoid any interest payment in the individual donor current account product.


##### Memo Interest for Notional Pool Bundles

The user can define memo type interest property on real account for which the interest property type should be Memo Only.

The system allows to calculate memo interest on the pool balance, that is, memo interest on the total debit and credit balances of the pool after considering the Max Offset% . The memo interest properties at the product condition level or arrangement level has to be configured to pay or due, depending on the Debit or Credit Interest.

In the above scenario, the memo interest on the recipient current account, considering the pool balance, is made due or paid to the master current account (as per the schedule configured for Memo interest) and all other memo interest accruals at the individual donor current account are suppressed (irrespective of the schedule configured for the interest).

However, the non contingent interest accruals at the individual donor current accounts are allowed, thereby the non-contingent interest based on the individual donor current account balance are accrued at the individual donor product level.

Thus allowing memo interest to be paid or made due to the customer on the pool balance and allow non contingent interest to be paid or collected at the individual donor current account product.

This is only an illustrative configuration. The bank can configure to pay or suppress the interest at the donor level and raise an interest entry only at the recipient level.

- The memo interest property cannot be set to Capitalise.
- For Offset Type set as Pool, the system allows a maximum of two recipient interest properties and Max Offset% can be set for only one of the recipient property.


#### 🔧 Working With

The Arrangement Overview pages of the Interest Compensation and Offset Mortgage Products are shown below respectively.


##### Interest Calculation on Notional Pool

Notional cash pooling offers offset based interest calculation for Account products based on combined balances of the participants in the pool. Additionally, an offset can be applied on the overall credit and debit balances of the pool. Banks can minimise the interest expense by offsetting debit and credit positions on the overall balance of the pool, after considering the Max Offset % value. Customers also will have the advantage of interest getting calculated on the entire pooled balances.

> **⚠️ Note:** To enable interest calculation on the pool and suppress the same in the donors, the user has to ensure that the BNK/AA.PROCESS.ACTIVITIES service is running and COB is completed.

##### Workflow

Interest Compensation related activities are listed below:

Bonus interest product bundle is opted when a customer has more than one current and one savings account. On opting to this bundle customer can enjoy interest on sum of credit balances of all accounts in a nominated current account.

To create bundle bonus arrangement, perform the following steps:

1. Account Bundles/Loan Offset .
2. Click the New Arrangement icon for the Bundle Bonus activity.
3. Enter a value in the Customer field.
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
5. Click the Bundle Participants option to expand.
6. Enter a value in the Arrangement field.
7. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
8. Click the Commit icon to submit the record.

Interest Compensation bundle is created when a customer holds more than one current and one savings bank account. By opting for this bundle product, customer can receive interest on sum of all account balances in a single nominated account.

To create an interest compensation arrangement, perform the following steps:

1. Account Bundles/Loan Offset .
2. Click the New Arrangement icon for the Interest Compensation activity.
3. Enter a value in the Customer field.
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors.
5. Click the Bundle Participants option to expand.
6. Enter a value in the Arrangement field.
7. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
8. Click the Commit icon to submit the record.

Interest Upgrade product bundle is created when a customer has a premium current account and a savings account in the bank. On opting to this bundle product, customer can enjoy a higher rate of Interest on credit balances in Premium current account.

To create an interest upgrade arrangement, perform the following steps:

1. Account Bundles/Loan Offset .
2. Click the New Arrangement icon for the Interest Upgrade activity.
3. Enter a value in the Customer field.
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors.
5. Click the Bundle Participants option to expand.
6. Enter a value in the Arrangement field.
7. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
8. Click the Commit icon to submit the record.

Mortgage Offset product Bundle is created when a customer holds a Mortgage loan and a Savings or Current Account with the Bank. By opting for a Bundle, the customer gets an advantage to setoff credit interest of the account against debit interest of the loan. Thus, customer enjoys paying the net interest.

To create a mortgage offset arrangement, perform the following steps:

1. Account Bundles/Loan Offset .
2. Click the New Arrangement icon for the mortgage offset.
3. Enter a value in the Customer field.
4. Click the Validate icon to check for errors.
5. Click the Bundle Participants option to expand.
6. Enter a value in the Arrangement field.
7. Click the Validate icon to check for errors and overrides.
8. Click the Commit icon to submit the record.

### 2.12  Misc


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Arrangement Bundle module (AB) provides Product bundling functionality for Temenos Transact . The module allows retail products to be bundled with the following features:*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.PAYMENT.TYPE`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Auto Settle*, *Type*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- APIs
- Temenos Transact Services

The Arrangement Bundle module (AB) provides Product bundling functionality for Temenos Transact . The module allows retail products to be bundled with the following features:

- Consolidated interest calculation by taking set of arrangements either within the same Product Line or across Product Lines including the netting of credit balances against debit balance.
- One of the arrangements in the Bundle arrangement is the master arrangement (called the Recipient arrangement) and the balances of the Donor arrangements will be taken for the interest calculation along with the balance of the Recipient arrangement, with or without interest calculation of the Donor arrangements at their level.
- Bundle arrangement is not a financial arrangement and it only establishes the link between the Recipient and Donor arrangements.
- Adding new arrangements to the Bundle and removal of the existing arrangements from the Bundle is possible.


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

Product Conditions of a Property Class are evaluated to bring out the features of the Property Class. The values in the Product Condition are defaulted in an arrangement during its creation. The negotiability, default values and other restrictions are also defined in the Product Condition. These Product Conditions along with the Properties derived from the Property Classes are grouped together to build products.

Product Conditions are dated and some of them have currency as part of their ID. When currency forms part of the Product Condition ID, then the user has to create different conditions for each currency in which the product is available. When a new condition is created or an existing condition is amended, the product to which the condition is linked has to be proofed and published.

Model parameters consists of

The Activity Charges Property Class defines the charges that has to be applied when a particular activity is triggered on an arrangement. These charges can be made due, capitalised or deferred. The user can enable auto settle the charges made due from unallocated credit balance by setting the Auto Settle field to Yes.

In accounts, charges are enabled for Dormancy, Settle Payoff and Ageing. This Property Class is also used for all AA related modules. Charges are set for various other activities.

The Activity Restriction Property Class is used to specify the restriction on a particular transaction. The user can define the restriction rules including the relevant periodic attributes and activities in the Product Condition. These rules are then used to define activity-based or property-based restrictions. A rule, if broken, can be set to result in an override or error.

A charge can be attached for this Product Condition and set to be made due , capitalised or deferred.

For Retail Accounts (AR) module, activity restriction is used for restricting transactions by number, type and so on. This is also used in other modules to restrict the user from performing various user activity based on life cycle status of contracts.

The Activity Messaging Property Class links the soft delivery module to Arrangement Architecture. Messages are sent based on the role and activity performed on an arrangement. This record allows either specific Activities or Activity Classes to be defined and linked to the EB.ADVICES records.

The Activity Presentation is a non-mandatory Property Class, that allows the user to define versions used for various Properties during arrangement activities. The versions used can be defined at Property Class, Property and Activity levels.

The Interest Property Class is used for all interest definition and processing in AA. A Temenos Transact product defined and processed in AA can have multiple Interest Properties defined (for example, principal interest, penalty interest, commission, and so on). Interest rates can be defined as fixed rate, floating rate, periodic rate, linked rate (referring an interest property from other arrangement), routine based calculation and tiered interest.

Further, it is possible to define a negative rate, minimum interest amount and waive the interest.

Interest adjustment can be done in runtime, and adjustment related details or values can be captured in adjustment related fields.

The Interest Compensation Property Class is used by a Bundle product. This is used to store the source and target Interest Properties, Recipient and Donor Product Groups, and the Properties. Interest can either be calculated or suppressed as defined in this Product Condition.

The Payment Schedule Property Class is used by all the products, which have amounts billed (that is, made due), capitalised or pay. A Payment Schedule can be comprised of one or more payment definitions with conditions, such as payment type and method, arrangement properties, dates and amount. The AA.PAYMENT.TYPE application is used to define the standard payment types such as Constant, Linear, Actual and Fixed Equal and so on that can be used by a product. This payment type is then attached to each payment schedule definition. The user can specify start and end dates, and the repayment of arrangement to commence after ‘n’ months from the arrangement date or ‘n’ months before the maturity or ‘n’ months after the change product or reset and rollover has happened.

The Periodic charges Property Class acts as a container to group different Charge Properties and calculates a periodic charge amount. The Payment Schedule Property Class drives this Property Class. A periodic charge property can be attached in payment schedule and periodic charge amount is calculated on schedule date.

At arrangement level, the user can adjust entire periodic charge.

The Inheritance Property Class is used for BN Pool structure for inheriting the Product Conditions set at parent level arrangement to the child level arrangement accounts. The Product Conditions that are set for inheritance are attached to Property records with type as ‘Inheritance Only’. The Properties to be inherited can be controlled at both Source and Target levels.

The Limit Property Class primarily controls the use of LIMIT module by the product. The user can set up a single or shared limit. The user can define the LIMIT.REFERENCE applicable for a specific product such that the same would be defaulted in an arrangement. For a new limit, at the arrangement level, the LIMIT.SERIAL has to be given as NEW. The AR module can have a self-contained secondary limit without having actual limit attached to it. Overdraft status\Notice for AR module is handled inside Limit Property Class.

The Product Bundle Property Class is used to store the arrangements that form part of a bundle. It stores the Recipient arrangement, which is marked with the INTEREST.COMPENSATION Property name in the Type field and the DONOR Product Groups, with the field min and max values of arrangement required under each Product or Product Group, and currency, which each arrangement can belong to.

The Bundle Hierarchy Property Class is used to define the allowed products and relations between products that are part of a Bundle. It is used in BUNDLE Product Line and is a product definition (product only). Accounts arrangement when linked to a Bundle that has bundle hierarchy definition is validated against the condition specified and only when the conditions are satisfied.

Accounts arrangement can become part of the bundle. Linking of an accounts arrangement with a Bundle is done by specifying Bundle arrangement reference through BUNDLE.ARRANGEMENT attribute in the Account Property Condition.


##### Illustrating Model Products

Retail Bundle (AB) Product Line provides various bundle account and package functionality for Temenos Transact . The module allows the user to create Account Bundles, Card Packages, Loan Offsets, Master Account and Retail Packages using the AA framework under the BUNDLE Product Line.

| S.No | Product Name | Product Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Account Bundles | Account Bundle as Bundle Bonus Account Bundle as Group Account Account Bundle as Interest Compensation Account Bundle as Interest Upgrade |
| 2 | Card Packages | Card Package |
| 3 | Loan Offsets | Loan Offsets as Offset Mortgage |
| 4 | Master Account | Bundle product for Master Account |
| 5 | Retail Packages | Retail Package for Current Account package Retail Package for Loan Package Retail Package for Saving Package |

### 2.13  ProductQualifierRules


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Product Qualifier rules are used to define a rule in an arrangement to arrive at a result, and the result of the rule triggers another Activity on the same arrangement or a linked arrangement.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ARRANGEMENT`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Online Closure*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Product Qualifier rules are used to define a rule in an arrangement to arrive at a result, and the result of the rule triggers another Activity on the same arrangement or a linked arrangement.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

Product Qualifier rules set in a Bundle are aimed at assessing the validity of a Bundle arrangement against the pre-requisites of the Bundle. Failure to meet the rules could result in dissolving the Bundle (BUNDLE-CLOSE-ARRANGEMENT).

Read Activity Restriction User Guide - Product Qualifier for more information.


##### Activity Based

In the Activity Based tab, the user can define Participant Closed Activity (BUNDLE-RECORD.EVENT-PARTICIPANT.CLOSURE) and Participant Product Changed Activity (BUNDLE-RECORD.EVENT-PARTICIPANT.CHANGE.PRODUCT) as the trigger for running both these Rule Sets.


##### Rule Set

For Rule.Set.1, the system evaluates the Rule Expression 1.Payroll.Current.AC and for Rule.Set.2, the system evaluates the Rule Expression 1.Preferred.Welcome.AC. When either of the Rule Set fails, that results in Decision.1 to dissolve the Bundle (BUNDLE-CLOSE-ARRANGEMENT).


##### Rules

There are two rule names defined:

- 1.Payroll.Current.AC and
- 1.Preferred.Welcome.AC

These rules use the Bundle Participant Periodic Attribute to evaluate the number of participants in the Bundle. The Payroll.Current.AC rule evaluates if the Bundle has at least one account belonging to Current Account Product or Payroll Account Product. Likewise, Preferred.Welcome.AC evaluates if the Bundle has at least one account belonging to Preferred Savings Account or Welcome Savings Account.


#### 🔧 Working With

This topic explains the user, the procedure of closing a Bundle participant.


##### Closure of Bundle Participant

The work flow of closing a Bundle participant is described below.

The above flow can be described with an example.

| Arrangement 1 | Preferred Savings Account |
|---|---|
| Activity A1 | Close Arrangement Activity on Preferred Savings Account |
| Arrangement 2 | Bundle Arrangement |
| Activity A2 | Participant Closed Activity on Arrangement 2 |

- When the Close Arrangement is triggered on Arrangement 1, it triggers an event.
- This event is subscribed by the Linked Arrangement Subscriber. The linked arrangement subscriber finds the Bundle arrangement from AA.ARRANGEMENT of Arrangement 1. It uses the Non-financial Activity mapping on the Bundle arrangement to determine the Activity to be raised. This activity is handed off to the AA Process Activities service. When the service runs that activity, the Life Cycle management rules kick in on the Bundle Arrangement. The resulting action is done.
- Depending upon the Action context setup, the resultant activity can be raised inline or passed to AA Process Activities service.
- In case the Change Product Activity is triggered on Arrangement 1, then it is possible that the Change Product on the Arrangement 1 is reversed. In that case, it should not automatically result in reversal of the activity done on the linked Arrangement.
- Instead that can result in a different TEC Item being raised, which can then have its own resulting actions based on configuration.
- In the example above, if the result of evaluation on the Bundle resulted in ‘Bundle-Close’ arrangement, then in subsequent Reversal of the activity on the Arrangement 1, there is no longer a Bundle Arrangement to listen to that event.

Read Activity Restriction User guide – Deal Processing, Product Qualifier Rules, Activity Based Rules, Example for more illustrations.

When the Rule.Set.2 - 1.Preferred.Welcome.AC fails, the system records the closure of Bundle Participant in the Bundle using the TEC.ITEM AA.PARTICIPANT.CLOSURE.

The item pending for processing in F.EVENT.LOG is seen here.

When the XXX/AA.PROCESS.ACTIVITIES and XXX/EVENTS services are run, the system triggers the Close Arrangement Activity.

> **⚠️ Note:** The TEC Event is configured based on ACCOUNTS-CLOSE-ARRANGEMENT Activity. So, the Preferred Savings Account must have its Online Closure set to Yes to trigger this event immediately and result in Participant Closed Activity on the Bundle.

### 2.14  ProductVariationInBundles

#### 📖 Introduction

Product Variations allows the users to create variations of the same product but with different conditions. Depending on the customer eligibility rules, the system would then automatically default the right variation conditions onto the arrangement.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

In the following example, a subscription fee is defined for different customer segments through the Platinum, Gold and Silver variations.

The Product Condition for Gold where Fixed Amount is set as 8 USD is shown in the below screenshot.

The Product Condition for Silver where Fixed Amount is set as 10 USD is shown in the below screenshot.

The Product Conditions are associated with the Bundle Product in the Product Designer.

Variation Priority is defined as Platinum, Gold and Silver as shown below.


#### 🔧 Working With

Scheduled Charges and Activity Charges can be applied on Bundle products.

- These charges can be flat charge, banded/tiered charge.
- For a calculated it is possible to have a routine based calculation source.

- Bundle Setup Fee - Onetime Fee during Bundle setup.
- Bundle Subscription Fee - Periodic Charge, on frequency basis.
- Bundle Amendment Fee - Adhoc charge upon Bundle amendment.

Product Variations in Bundles for Charges can be based on the customer segment.

| Customer Segment | Platinum (USD) | Gold (USD) | Silver (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Setup Fee | 5 | 8 | 10 |
| Subscription Fee | 0 | 3 | 5 |

The following screenshots show how the subscription fee is assessed based on the customer segment.

Subscription fee assessed for a Gold customer is shown below.

Subscription fee assessed for a Silver customer is shown below.


##### Arrangement Info Only

The system defaults Arr Info Only based on the value in Default Info Only at Product condition level and can then be overridden by the user as necessary.

The Arr Info (Information only) attribute indicates the arrangement is added to the Bundle Product just for an information purpose and does not benefit from the Bundle.

When a Product Group is designated as Arr Info Only in the Product Bundle Property Class, the system by default marks the Bundle participant arrangement of the Product Group as Arr Info with an option to edit the flag.

- An arrangement designated, as Arr Info can be associated with multiple Bundle Products.
- When an arrangement is already part of Bundle Product (other than Arr Info), the system restricts the arrangement from being designated as Arr Info .
- When an INFO ONLY arrangement is set to be an operational arrangement (Info Only = No), the system validates if that arrangement is already an operational arrangement in another Bundle. If so, raise a validation Error.

A sample screenshot of override message for ARRANGEMENT INFO ONLY is given below.


##### Arrangement Role

The relationship between the Bundle arrangement owner and the participant arrangements are defined in the Product Bundle Property Class.

During a Bundle arrangement creation, the system validates the relationship between the Bundle arrangement owner and the participant arrangement. The system restricts the participant arrangement being part of the Bundle product if the relationship does not exist.

### 2.15  Chargeoff


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS`, `AA.ACTIVITY.HISTORY`, `AA.BILL.DETAILS`, `AA.INTEREST.ACCRUALS`, `CATEG.ENTRY`, `RE.CONSOL.SPEC.ENTRY`
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Bill Type*, *Charge Off Amount*, *Charge Off Percentage*, *Charge off Amount*, *Charge off Percentage*, *Full Chargeoff*, *New Property Amount*, *Or Prop Amt* ... +8 more
> 
> **Sections:** 🔧 Working With


#### 🔧 Working With

Working with Loan Charge-off Key Features Charge-off is different from writing off the arrangement. The key features of charge-off are: A full or multiple partial charge-off transaction is possible. The interest on the charge-off balance should accrue, but is not passed to income. Reversal of charge-off transactions is possible Removal from charge-off or partial removal from charge-off (that is, a lessening of the charge-off amount) is possible as well. Dual accounting –that is, having two sets of books, the customer record vs. the bank record and applying payments independently to the two records. The charge-off feature is available for the Lending Product Line. The Charge-off Property has to be included in the product for charging off an account. Activity Class - Charge-off Full/Complete Charge-off The LENDING-CHARGEOFF-ARRANGEMENT Activity Class is used for charge-off of an arrangement. The complete outstanding in the loan is charged off. Partial Charge-off or Charge-off in Parts It is possible to charge off a loan, in parts. The LENDING-CHARGE-OFF-ACCOUNT Activity Class is used to charge-off the Account Property balance, based on the charge-off order. This is used to both charge-off an amount of principal (that is, increase charge-off amount) and to reduce the charge-off (that is, decrease the charge-off amount) if required. If a loan is being charged-off for the first time, this Activity is responsible for creating the charge-off balances as well as the customer’s shadow balances. Handling Charge-off under FASB Regulations For handling charge-off under certain specific regulations (FASB), the bank user uses the CHARGEOFF-REPORTING activity. Dual Accounting For loan contracts, apart from the customer balances, it is possible to store two separate balances, the bank balances along with the charge-off balances. When a Lending Product with Charge-off Property is proofed and published, the system automatically creates the balance type records to maintain charge-off balances along with the customer and bank balances. For a loan that is charged off, for CUR , the balances prior to the Charge-off Activity is stored as a shadow CUR CUST. The charge-off amount is stored in CUR CO and the amount under banks book is stored as CUR . The CUR CO charge-off balance, is the contingent balance and CUR CUST is a balance used for internal purpose and CUR is only non-contingent in nature. When the LENDING-CREDIT-ARRANGEMENT activity is processed, the amount credited to UNC is also credited to UNC CUST. When the LENDING-DEBIT-ARRANGEMENT activity is processed, the amount debited from UNC is also be debited from UNC CUST. Shadow Balances When a loan is charged-off, the borrower is unaware of this action, and continues to receive regular billing notices. As a result, when a loan is fully or partially charged off there is a situation to maintain two sets of books: A customer record (that is, the customer’s view of the balances and bills) A bank record (that is, the bank’s view of the balances). Prior to the charge-off, the customer and the bank records are the same (and therefore there is only one set of books). However once a loan is partially or fully charged off, the views are different. Customer Record Banks generally don’t communicate charge-off decision to the customers. So, a customer is unaware of a charge-off. Copying the balances prior to the Charge-off Activity creates a shadow record. This now becomes the customer record and does not include any of the effects of the charge-off. The bills and payments continue to be processed normally against this customer record. The payments received have to be apportioned as per the Payment Rules according to the customer. The customer balances are apportioned in this repayment order. Bank Record Full/Complete Charge-off For a full or complete charge-off using the LENDING-CHARGEOFF-ARRANGEMENT activity, there are no bank balances. The BNK balances are zero in this case. Charge-off in Parts/Partial Charge-off A charge-off creates the shadow balances for the customer record that do not include the effects of the charge-off (that is, the customer is completely unaware). As a result, the existing balances (customer balance less charge-off amount) continue to be referred to as the bank record and includes the effects of the charge-off (for example, the charged-off balance). As the arrangement advances, it also contains the interest accrual on the bank balance and charged-off balance separately. Additionally payments to the loan are allocated in a different manner on the bank record than on the customer record. This is based upon the value of the book balances and the status of the loan (for example, partially charged-off, fully charged-off or non-accrual). Internal inquiry screens display both the customer and the bank record, once a loan is partially or fully charged off. Reports breakdown the information this way as well – including both the bank balances and the customer balances. Charge-Off Balances The CUR CO and each ACC CO balance corresponds to the charge-off balance for the principal and the interest respectively. The system creates these balances by appending a CO at the end of each balance type. Multiple Interest Accruals For a full charge-off, the system accrues interest for charge-off and the customer balances namely CO and CUST balances. There is no bank balance to accrue interest for the BNK balances. For a partial charge-off (charge-off in parts), the system accrues interest for bank balance (for example, CUR ), charge-off and the customer balances. The system also accrues interest for the chargeoff and customer balances namely CO and CUST balances. It is necessary to accrue both charge-off and customer interest on the corresponding balances separately. Full/Complete Charge-off During a full charge-off, the arrangement balances are moved to the Chargeoff PL. As part of shadow accounting, CUR CUST and CUR CO balances are maintained during a full Chargeoff. This results in the accrual of balances per Interest Property for each of this principal balance. Each of them accrues interest at the same rate but based upon their balance. ACC CUST is accrued on CUR CUST and ACC CO is accrued on CUR CO. Though multiple interest accruals are done based on different balances, definition of source balance for each type of accrual is not required. Product configuration contains: Property Source INTEREST CURACCOUNT Corresponding Accruals in a full charge-off loan are: Balance Source ACCINTERESTCO CURACCOUNTCO ACCINTERESTCUST CURACCOUNTCUST Partial Charge-off or Charge-off in Parts In a partial charge-off, there are three balances: CUR , CUR CUST, CUR CO. Hence, there are three accrual balances per Interest Property and each accrues interest at the same rate but based upon their balance. ACC is accrued on CUR then ACC CUST is accrued on CUR CUST. Though multiple interest accruals are done based on different balances, definition of source balance for each type of accrual is not required. The interest is calculated on: Property Source INTEREST CURACCOUNT Corresponding accruals in a partial charge-off loan are: Balance Source ACCINTEREST CURACCOUNT ACCINTERESTCO CURACCOUNTCO ACCINTERESTCUST CURACCOUNTCUST Product Setup and Charge-off Balances When a Lending Product with Charge-off Property is proofed and published, the system automatically creates the below balance type records to maintain customer, bank and charge-off balances. Except bank balances, other balance type records which are created by system are contingent in nature. Bank Balances Charge-off Balances Customer Balances CUR CUR CO CUR CUST DUE DUE CUST CUST UNC UNC CUST ACC ACC CO ACC CUST DUE DUE CUST CUST CUR CO balance type holds the cumulative amount that’s been charged-off against an account. ACC CO balance type is used for posting the accrued interest on charged-off balances namely CUR CO. Dual Billing In the case where a loan is in Charge-Off status, AA.BILL.DETAILS is updated with both the customer and the bank due amounts. For a complete charge-off, the reflection of the charge-off billing is found in the billed balances. The bank amount is zero For a partial charge-off, two sets of figures (the customer and bank amounts) are calculated and stored on the bill. The customer and the bank amounts differ due to the effect of the charged-off principal as well as the alternate way of applying credits to the arrangement. Illustration of Partial Charge-off The changes that happen in an arrangement when a charge-off is performed is illustrated with the help of the below example. The arrangement is in delinquent status and is being charged off using the LENDING-CHARGEOFF-ACCOUNT Activity giving the transaction amount as 80,000 USD. This means 80,000 USD of principal is charged off. The Loan Arrangement Overview is displayed below. The Charge-off Activity is shown below. The Loan Arrangement Overview After Charge-off is shown below. Comparison of Arrangement Balances Before And After Charge-off The ECB balances before charge-off of 80,000 is shown below. The ECB balances after charge-off of 80,000 is shown below. Note that the arrangement balances have changed as a result of the charge-off. Bill Generated Before/After Charge-off On bill generation, AA.BILL.DETAILS is updated with both the customer and the bank due amounts for each of these accruals. AA.BILL.DETAILS stores the bank related fields that get updated on and after the charge-off of an arrangement. Once the charge-off is done, then the customer balances are stored in existing amount related fields and bank balances are stored in the BNK (bank) fields. Overdue processing is triggered based on the bills getting aged. The Os Prop Amt and Or Prop Amt fields of the bill are based on the customer balances(original amount) and regular overdue processing is triggered for the same. Balance type AA.BILL.DETAILS CUR Os Prop Amt Bnk Or Prop Amt Bnk CUR CUST Os Prop Amt Or Prop Amt Key Features of Full/Complete Charge-off A complete charge-off is done using the LENDING-CHARGEOFF-ARRANGEMENT activity. After a complete charge-off is made in the arrangement, the Full Chargeoff field in the AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS application displays Yes. During charge-off, the loan principal is charged off to the PL Category assigned to the Account property class. The interest is charged off to the PL Category assigned to the Interest property class. Any tax is charged-off to the PL Category assigned to the Tax property class. Validations During a Complete Charge-off When this activity is executed, the system performs the below validations and results in error in below scenarios: The bank performs the charge off after clearing any outstanding credit balances of the loan (like UNC/INV/AVL). Hence if there are any credit balances available during a charge-off, the system raises the following error. When there is a charge with outstanding pay balance, the arrangement cannot be charged off. The pay balance must be cleared and then charge-off should be triggered in the system. Post charge-off, the banks do not prefer to disburse any further loans or increase the loan commitment further. Hence, the disbursement activity is not allowed after the charge off. During the cooling and cancel period, the loan charge-off is not allowed. Any income to the arrangement is booked to the Chargeoff PL of that Property An arrangement that has undergone partial charge-off can undergo full charge-off, but an arrangement that is completely charged off cannot be charged off further. Loans cannot go to negative rate when loan is in charge-off. Dormant loans cannot be charged off. When an arrangement has a charge set to amortise, the charge cannot be charged off. The system raises an error when the user tries to do a full charge-off when there is a charge amortisation in progress. During charge-off, the system calculates the penalty interest if this has been configured and this helps the bank to access the real charge-off amount for all the property. Illustration of Charge-off Consider a loan that has few bills outstanding and is delinquent. Perform a charge-off. The charged-off arrangement is shown below. The charge-off information in AA.ACCOUNT.DETAILS is as shown below. Arrangement Balances Movement The loan principal balances and billed interest balances are moved to Chargeoff PL and are stored in CO and CUST balances as off-balance sheet items. Here, the sum is: ACCPRINCIPALINTCO=ACCPRINCIPALINTCUST+DELPRINCIPALINTCUST CURACCOUNTCO=DELACCOUNTCUST+CURACCOUNTCUST Bills A bill that was already generated is also updated with the charge-off information. In a full charge-off, the BNK balances for the Property after charge-off is zero. The billed amount and outstanding balance here represents the CUST balance, as shown below Interest Accruals After a charge-off, the interest accruals are under CUST and CO balances. Charge Bills Charge-Off An arrangement with interest and charge bills is being fully charged off, including all interest and charges in the bills along with outstanding principal. Any Activity Charge, Periodic Charge and Rule break charge are also charged off. This is subject to certain evaluation: The system evaluates if there are any pay charges outstanding and raises an error to indicate that the same must be settled. The system evaluates if there is charge collected that is undergoing amortisation, then the system doesn’t allow to charge off that arrangement. Consider an arrangement that has been charged off. During a charge-off, charge bills are also charged off. A rule break that is being charged off is shown below. The balances after the charge-off, also reflects the charges being charged off. For customer books it is as shown below. Activity Charge for charge-off books is shown below.
