### 4.7  Household Pricing


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *Customer Relationship Pricing can be enabled by grouping the related and unrelated arrangement of the customers.*
> 
> **Applications:** `AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY`, `AA.CRA.PARAMETER`, `AA.CUSTOMER.RELATED.ARRANGEMENTS`, `AA.CUSTOMER.ROLE`, `AA.EVALUATION.DETAILS`, `AA.PERIODIC.ATTRIBUTE`, `AA.PERIODIC.ATTRIBUTE.CLASS`, `AA.PRD.DES.PRICING.RULES` ... +3 more
> 
> **Key Fields:** *Absolute Value*, *CRA Customer*, *CRA Method*, *Cra Customer*, *Cra Method*, *End Date*, *End date*, *Exclude* ... +12 more
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction | ⚙️ Configuration | 🔧 Working With | 📋 Tasks | 📊 Outputs


#### 📖 Introduction

Customer Relationship Pricing can be enabled by grouping the related and unrelated arrangement of the customers.

Aggregate balance, number of arrangements owned in specified products or services subscribed for the household determine the pricing and other benefits for the customer relationship group.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following section describes the parameter settings required for Household Pricing.


##### Defining Customer Relationship Parameter

The following section describes the Customer Relationship Parameter in detail.

- AA.CRA.PARAMETER defines the rules for indicating customer relationship definition.
- This table specifies which customer relation codes are eligible for grouping into the related customer’s CRA (Customer Related Arrangements) and if it has to be automatic or manual inclusion to the group.
- When a customer opens a new arrangement, the arrangement gets added to the Household Relationship definition, thereby contributes and avails the Customer Relationship Pricing (Household Pricing).
- AA.CRA.PARAMETER has system level records in which Relation Code is assigned with CRA Method as Automatic or Manual.
- The rules are defined by Relation Code , that is, relationship of the account owner with the related customer.
- The rules defined in this table are applicable only for the related customers of the arrangement’s beneficial owner.
- For beneficial owners, the addition of new arrangements into the customer’s CRA is Automatic.
- For related customers, the option defined in the relation CRA Method determines whether the addition of the customer’s new arrangement into the related customer’s CRA is either automatic or manual.
- For Automatic option, the CRA Customer is set by default; for Manual option, the CRA Customer has to be input manually.

Periodic Classes such as Product, Product Count, Service, Service Count, and Product and Service count are used to support the balance type rules defined, based on products. The periodic class is used in the Pricing Rules Property Class.

The Multiple Arrangements and Satisfied by attributes in AA.PERIODIC.ATTRIBUTE decide if the pricing rules defined in AA.PRD.DES.PRICING.RULES should consider multiple arrangements or bundle or single arrangement while executing the pricing rules.

USD 5,000, then the sum of all arrangement balances of the CRA family group can cumulatively satisfy the rule of minimum balance.

CRA balance components are defined through AC.BALANCE.TYPE with Reporting Type as Cra.

The user can indicate the Product Line, Product Group, Product for Cra balance type to be applied. For instance, if the Product is defined as Savings account and Balance Type is defined as Current Balance, then CRA balance is calculated only by summing up the current balance of the Savings account pertaining to the family group.

Any Product Line, Product Group, Product or Balance Type that is marked as Exclude or left undefined is not considered for CRA balance calculation.

The Absolute Value attribute is meant for handling negative balances in lending and account arrangements with negative balance and the balance is transposed as an absolute value.

The Pricing Rules Property Class is used to define the preferential pricing and service charge waive off. In the example shown below, the management fee is waived off if the minimum balance of the Loans and deposits is greater than USD 40,000. The AC.BALANCE.TYPE and AA.PERIODIC.ATTRIBUTE are used to define the rule.

The owner of an arrangement is the customer whose role is defined as Beneficial Owner in the AA.CUSTOMER.ROLE table. It is possible to relate other customers in an arrangement with a relation code.

- An example of a child relation defined in the customer ID 100336 is shown below.
- The system automatically updates the related customer record with the Reverse Relationship code.
- Reverse Relationship parent that is updated automatically in the customer ID 100802 is shown below.

The related arrangements of a customer are stored in the AA.CUSTOMER.RELATED.ARRANGEMENTS table for relationship pricing purposes. This table records both the customer’s own arrangements and the arrangements of related customers based on certain defined rules. This is a system maintained table and any updates to the table is only through:

- An Activity New Arrangement Creation Change Customer Change CRA Customers
- A Service
- Customer Static Change - that is change of relationship in the customer record.

All the related arrangements cannot be added to the customer’s CRA. This addition is based on certain defined rules. These rules are defined in the AA.CRA.PARAMETER parameter table.

- This table specifies the customer relation codes that are eligible for grouping into the related customer’s CRA and the method (automatic or manual) used to group, whenever the customer opens new arrangements.
- The rules are defined by Relation code , that is, relationship of the account owner with the related customer.
- The rules defined in this table are applicable only for the related customers of the arrangement’s beneficial owner.
- For beneficial owners, the addition of new arrangements into the customer’s CRA is by default, with an option to opt out.
- For related customers, the option defined in the Relation Cra Method determines whether the addition of the customer’s new arrangement into the related customer’s CRA, is Automatic or Manual.
- This is a system level record and must exist for CRAs to be maintained.
- In the absence of this record, CRA table is not updated even for the owners of the arrangement.
- To explain the rules, consider that the customer (beneficial owner) opens a new account.
- System adds the account to the customer’s CRA.
- In order to add the account to the CRA of related customers, system checks if the Relation code is found in AA CRA Parameter table. If the code is available and the Relation Cra Method is Automatic, then the system adds this account to the related customer’s CRA. If the code is found and Relation Cra Method is Manual, the customer has to manually add this account to the related customer’s CRA. If the code is not found, then this account cannot be added to the related customer’s CRA.

The Cra Customer attribute in the Customer Property Class displays the list of customers whose CRA records are updated automatically based on the AA.CRA.PARAMETER table. It indicates the customer ID whose CRA is updated to include the account being created.

The following section describes the process of defining pricing benefits for non-related customers.

- In the AA.CRA.PARAMETER table, the user can configure the Non-Relation CRA Method field to include non-related customers in the arrangement.
- For non-related customers, setting the Non-Relation CRA Method field as Manual allows an unrelated customer to be added in the arrangement of the beneficial owners. When the Non-Relation CRA Method field is set as Restricted, the user is not allowed to add an unrelated customer as a CRA customer in an arrangement.
- When a non-related customer inclusion is chosen, then the related customers can only be added automatically. An error is raised if manual option is used.

> **⚠️ Note:** Only one time switching of the Non Relation CRA Method field from Restricted to Manual is permitted. Further switching is restricted.

The CRA parameter is configured as shown in the below screenshot.


#### 🔧 Working With

The following section describes about the AA Customer Related Arrangements, addition and removal of CRA customers, household pricing and pricing benefits for unrelated customers.


##### AA Customer Related Arrangements

The list of arrangements in the AA.CUSTOMER.RELATED.ARRANGEMENTS table (defined per customer) allow the user to avail pricing benefits, charge waiver, and so on based on the relationship of the family group or household, with the bank. AA.CUSTOMER.RELATED.ARRANGEMENTS is a system maintained table. For any changes in the CRA relationship arrangement, a set of associated multi-value attributes are available (except for changes or updates triggered on the same day where the same set of attributes is updated)

A customer can be part of multiple relationship groups.

- If Update Method is designated as Automatic, Cra Customer is populated in the arrangement and the arrangement ID gets updated in the AA.CUSTOMER.RELATED.ARRANGEMENTS table upon authorisation of the arrangement.
- If Update Method is designated as Manual, user includes the Cra Customer in the arrangement, after which system updates the information in AA.CUSTOMER.RELATED.ARRANGEMENTS table of the related customer.
- AA.CUSTOMER.RELATED.ARRANGEMENTS is updated only for the relationships mentioned in the table (either automatic or manual) and not updated for the other relationship codes (even for the owners of the arrangement). In all these cases, the relationship code has to be available in the CUSTOMER record.
- In the absence of AA.CRA.PARAMETER record, AA.CUSTOMER.RELATED.ARRANGEMENTS is not updated even for the owners of the arrangement.
- When a relation code is removed in AA.CRA.PARAMETER , related customer(s) pertaining to the relationship are removed from all the existing arrangements. This activity is performed using the AA.CRA.SERVICE job. If the parent relationship is removed from AA.CRA.PARAMETER , then all the CRA relations at the arrangement level associated with the Parent Relation Code are delinked. This action impacts the aggregate relationship size of the family group.
- The End date attribute in AA.CUSTOMER.RELATED.ARRANGEMENTS records the end of the contribution of the arrangement in the household relationship. This attribute is updated during :
- Expiry, redemption or closure of the arrangement.
- The customer disassociates from the arrangement due to other activity.
- Due to update or change customer or when relationship code is removed from AA.CRA.PARAMETER .
- During the archival process, the expired relationship arrangements are removed from the AA.CUSTOMER.RELATED.ARRANGEMENTS
- During arrangement creation, the customers who are related to the beneficial owner are added in the system based on the following condition
- The customer ID of the relative is mapped with the beneficial owner in the CUSTOMER application.
- The relationship code has to be defined in AA.CRA.PARAMETER if it is stated as Automatic.
- Upon authorisation of the arrangement, the relations (automatically or manually based on AA.CRA.PARAMETER definition) that are added to the arrangement gets updated in the AA.CUSTOMER.RELATED.ARRANGEMENTS .
- The AA.CUSTOMER.RELATED.ARRANGEMENTS is a system maintained table. Whenever a CRA record is updated, a new dated record is created automatically in the table. If a record already exists for the day, the record is overridden. A customer can be part of multiple relationship groups.

When a customer opens a new arrangement, system performs the following during the AA.ARRANGEMENT.ACTIVITY validation.

- Populates all the beneficial owners in Cra Customer attribute.
- For each beneficial owner, finds all the related customer IDs and their relation code from the RELATION.CUSTOMER record.
- For each related customer, looks up their relation code in AA.CRA.PARAMETER .
- If the code is found and method is Automatic, appends it to Cra Customer attribute.

The user can do the following:

- Modify the customer IDs that are automatically populated by the system.
- Opt out of adding the account to a CRA by manually removing the customer ID.
- Add a new customer ID in whose CRA the account has to be updated. These customers are validated against: The RELATION.CUSTOMER table that is, whether the customer is related to any of the beneficial owner or not. The AA.CRA.PARAMETER table to determine if the relationship is eligible for CRAs, that is, whether the relation code is defined and method is set to Automatic or Manual.

When the below activities are authorised, the AA.CUSTOMER.RELATED.ARRANGEMENTS record of each customer captured in Cra Customer attribute is updated.

- New Arrangement Activity
- Take Over Activity
- Change Customer Activity
- Update CRA Customer Activity (New Activity Class)

In addition to New Arrangement and Takeover Activities, the Change Customer and Update CRA Customer Activity allows the user to modify the Cra Customer attribute in an existing arrangement.

During charge assessment or interest definition, the CRA balance is compared against the pricing rules to serve the customer with preferential pricing.

- 50,000 USD, to avail a credit interest rate benefit, say 25 basis points higher than the base rate. In this case the system evaluates the total deposits maintained in all the arrangement of the CRA, family group and the rule is compared against the aggregate total balance.

It is also possible to make multiple pricing rules to co-exist to satisfy a rule.

- 50,000 USD – in such a case if either or both conditions are satisfied the special rate is given to the new arrangement.

- The start of day balance of all products are considered to arrive at the CRA balance.
- CRA balances are calculated dynamically during evaluation, a virtual balance basically.
- When a new relation code is included in AA.CRA.PARAMETER or CUSTOMER application, the system does not automatically add the related customer to existing arrangements. The reason is that it is not always required that a customer includes all related customer(s) in an arrangement.

The following are the basic checks to be done when the household pricing benefit is not available for an arrangement

- Check AA.CRA.PARAMETER if the relationship code is updated as Manual or Automatic.
- Check if the customers record is updated for the relationship code.
- Check if the customers are added as Cra Customer in the arrangement created.
- If AA.CRA.PARAMETER has relationship code has the Cra Method as manual, then user must manually include the customer ID as Cra Customer . This ensures that AA.CUSTOMER.RELATED.ARRANGEMENTS updated.
- AA.CUSTOMER.RELATED.ARRANGEMENTS are generated or updated by the system only when arrangements are created or updated for Cra Customer
- Finally also check if the pricing rule setup is qualified for the Household pricing in AA.EVALUATION.DETAILS .

The following scenario explains how to include an unrelated customer manually and a related customer automatically.

An arrangement is created for customer A, who is the primary customer .

Customer A has a related customer B (relation code 14) and based on the CRA parameter setup, the customer B is automatically added as the CRA customer of A.

Customer C, is the business partner of the customer A. However, the customer C is unrelated to customer A. The bank user adds the customer C as the CRA customer of A, manually. Subsequently, when the business agreement expires, the user removes customer C from the CRA of customer A. This is explained in detail in the following sequence of steps.

1. Creating an arrangement - The user creates a new arrangement for customer A on April 1, 2019.
2. Updating CRA for parent child relationship automatically - Customer B, is automatically added to CRA of customer A on the same day of the arrangement creation. The child parent relationship is established when the Relationship Code field is set as 14.
3. Adding an unrelated customer - Customer C is added manually by the user through Update Customer activity since he doesn’t possess any direct relationship with the customer A. The user adds customer C as CRA customer in the arrangement on April 5, 2019. The Unrelated field in the CRA record is set to Yes subsequently.
4. Removing the unrelated customer - The user removes the customer C as a CRA customer from the arrangement on April 12, 2019 and subsequently the End Date field for the relationship is populated in the CRA record.
5. Removing the related customer - The user removes customer B as a CRA customer from the arrangement on April 17, 2019 and subsequently the End Date field for the relationship is populated in the CRA record.

#### 📖 Introduction

Related topics:

- Temenos Transact Services

Pricing is part of the Retail Banking suite of products.

AA provides various pricing methods for financial institutions to attract and retain customers. It offers Preferential Pricing based on the relationship a customer maintains with the bank or the channels through which the customer accesses and transacts on their accounts.

Preferential Pricing comes in various formats. These can be condensed into six main pricing strategies:

- Regional Pricing
- Channel Pricing
- Household Pricing
- Relationship Pricing
- Package Pricing
- Promotional Pricing

These strategies can be used independently of each other or in combination, depending on each use case.


##### Illustrating Model Parameters

The model parameter for Pricing in AA is explained below.

The Product Conditions of a Property Class are evaluated to bring out the features of the Property Class. The values in the Product Condition are made default in an arrangement during its creation. The negotiability or default values and other restrictions are also defined in the Product Condition. These Product Conditions along with the properties derived from the Property Classes are grouped together to build the products.

The Product Conditions are dated and some of them have currency as part of their ID. When the currency forms part of the Product Condition ID, then the user has to create different conditions for each currency in which the product is available. When a new condition is created or an existing condition is amended, the user has to proof and publish the product to which the condition is linked

Model parameters consists of:

This Property Class is used to define properties having more than one routine that has to be merged from different product levels. If three levels of products are defined, this condition can be used to take all relevant routines from all the three levels so that all conditions and calculations are taken into account.

This Property Class links the soft delivery module to the arrangement architecture. Messages are sent based on the role and activity performed on an arrangement. This record allows either specific activities or activity classes to be defined and linked to the records in EB.ADVICES .

This is a non-mandatory Property Class, that allows to define versions used for various properties during arrangement activities. The versions used can be defined at Property Class, Property and Activity levels.

This Property Class is used to evaluate the eligibility of a customer for a specific product based on a set of rules. In Temenos Transact , the EB.CONTEXT has to be created first. Based on this, the rules are defined using the rules engine. Once these rules are validated, the EB.RULES.VERSION and EB.RULES are created in Temenos Transact .

This Property Class allows the user to configure the preferential pricing adjustments that have to be made to financial arrangement for customers who have a certain relationship with the bank.

This Property Class allows the user to to hold information about required exchange rates and settlement accounts.


##### Illustrating Model Products

The module allows the user to create Loyalty Products, Valued Customer and Internal FX using the AA framework under the Relationship Pricing Product Line

|---|---|---|
| 1 | Loyalty Products | Loyalty Pricing Product |

#### 📖 Introduction

Package Pricing provides special pricing benefits in interest and charges for customers based on the package the customer is using. This package can be any combination of customer service like the number of arrangements in different products or different services opted by the customer.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following section describes the Bundle product line used for Package Pricing.


##### Bundle Product Line for Package Pricing

Interest Compensation is a non-mandatory Property Class. This enables users to exclude Interest Compensation Property Class during the definition of normal packages that does not involve Notional Pooling.

The Property Control Property Class controls the behaviour of Bundle properties and its impact on the participant arrangements.


##### Property Classes

This section explains the Property Classes used in configuring package pricing for bundled products.

| Attribute | Description |
|---|---|
| Master Product | Used to specify the product of the master arrangement. It must be one of the products defined as constituent product. |
| Master Type | Accepts both Interest Compensation (for Pooling) and Property Control properties (for Package Pricing) |
| Master Arrangement | Accepts valid Internal arrangement that belong to Master Product |

| Property Class | Mandatory | Relevance w.r.t BUNDLE Product Line (Package Pricing) |
|---|---|---|
| Property Control | No | This is used to control how the Bundle properties affect the participant Arrangements. |

| Attribute | Description |
|---|---|
| Package Product | It specifies the Package Pricing Plan, that is, Bundle product name. This is a no-input attribute and is used only for reference purpose. |
| Package Property Control | It specifies whetherthe arrangement condition is suppressed, referred from the Bundle or mergedwith the Bundle condition. Has three options: Merge with Package Suppress Refer Package Thisis a no-input attribute and is used only for reference purpose. |

In the AC.BALANCE.TYPE application, Reporting Type is set as Bundle, and is used to define the rules based on combined bundle balances. During charge assessment, the balances of the arrangements are fetched from the records that are part of the bundle when reporting type is set as Bundle.

The periodic attribute framework is capable to run rule against the count or number of products held by the client in a bundle and then run the pricing rule for using the pricing rules framework at bundle level. The pricing rules are passed on the individual arrangement(s) based on the Property control setup.

The Periodic Attribute framework is capable to run a rule against the products and/or services availed by the client in a bundle and then run the pricing rule for using the pricing rules framework at bundle level. The pricing rules are passed on the individual arrangement(s) based on the Property control setup.


#### 🔧 Working With

During bundle creation, multiple arrangements are packed together under the bundle page in the arrangement creation Activity. The bundled products are validated against the pricing rules and charge waiver or discounts are applied according to the setup. Few examples of such benefits are discussed below.


##### Discounts Based on Number of Products or Services

The following section describes how to setup discounts based on number of products.

Banks choose to offer service charge discount based on the number of products.

Banks offer a discount on the primary arrangement (that is, the anchor account), when a certain number of additional products or services are purchased. This discount has to be evaluated by the primary arrangement at the time of the service charge assessment.

Banks offer discounts based on number of products that are tiered. More the products that a customer holds, larger is the discount. This can be achieved by defining more than one rule for the same Pricing Name and Property combination. The rules are evaluated one by one and discount pricing corresponding to whichever rule passes first is applied.

This pricing rule definition at bundle level is propagated to the individual arrangement(s) based on the definition in Property Control Property Class.

The Pricing Rules condition at the bundle level (that is, Package Pricing Rules) is merged with the condition of the primary arrangement. During rule evaluation, in addition to evaluating the rules of primary arrangement the rules defined at bundle are evaluated and the details stored in the AA.EVALUATION.DETAILS table.


##### Rules Based On Enrolment in Specific Products or Services

The following section how to define rules based on the customer’s enrolment in specific products or services.

Banks define a fee in an account that can be waived or reduced based on customer’s enrolment in specific products or service.

Periodic Attributes are available Pricing Rules based on Products and/or Services which are part of the bundle. With these periodic attributes, rules can be defined in Pricing Rules and merged with the primary arrangement’s condition.

With this number of products setup, the Pricing Rules condition at the bundle level is merged with the primary arrangement condition. During rule evaluation, in addition to evaluating the rules of primary arrangement the rules defined at bundle are also evaluated and the details are stored in the AA.EVALUATION.DETAILS table.


##### Pool Transactions at Bundle Level

The following section describes how to pool transactions at Bundle level.

Bank defines a transaction charge used in the Charge Condition. Here the transaction fee is unit charge of USD 0.5 with 200 free items. The transactions rules have to be evaluated at primary arrangement at the time of the service charge assessment. In order to achieve this transactions are pooled at the bundle level and process any excess fees at the primary arrangement level.

- Suppress the Transaction Fee Charge Property on the secondary arrangements. This prevents their service charge processing from calculating any transaction fee.
- Define conditions for transaction fees (charge) and service charges (periodic charges) which are specified at the bundle level and used by the primary arrangement.
- Replace the Transaction Fee Charge Condition on the primary arrangement with the one specified in Property Control. This can include a different number of free items and different fees for additional transactions.
- Merge the Service Charge Periodic Charges Condition specified in Property Control with the one on the primary arrangement. This provides the primary arrangement service charges with the correct transaction activities from all of the various product types in the bundle.

Here transaction fee is replaced for primary account with Package Transaction Fees and for the secondary accounts it is suppressed.

- The Periodic Charges for account are as shown below.
- The Periodic Charges for bundle are as shown below.
- Effect of Property Control to merge condition for service fee.
- Statement Fee and Cheque Fee are merged as seen below.
- Based upon the above configuration, the primary arrangement calculates a transaction fee on the cheque withdrawals from all the constituent arrangements of all three Product Lines. The first 200 are free and any check withdrawals above 200 are charged at USD 0.50 per item

For example, a bank can offer higher deposit rates or lower interest rate on loans as part of promotional pricing when initially launching a particular product to its ...*

#### 📖 Introduction

Promotional Pricing offers lower price temporarily to enhance the effectiveness of product sales effort to cost sensitive customers. For example, a bank can offer higher deposit rates or lower interest rate on loans as part of promotional pricing when initially launching a particular product to its potential customers.

The AA hierarchical Product Builder allows a bank to define a standard product (for example, current account) and a child product that offers promotional pricing and is made available for a limited period of time. The child product displays the ability to switch to the standard product (that is, the parent) after a predetermined time.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following section describes the promotional pricing configuration in detail.


##### Product Availability

A product can be available for sale only for a specific period. Similarly, the product can be made available in specific channels or line of business or organisation level . For these products, it is possible to define special pricing and discounts.

In the below screenshot, a child account product available only in the mobile banking channel is displayed.


##### Product Inheritance

Product inheritance allows the user to create a product hierarchy where the child product can be created by inheriting the parent product’s properties and having its own pricing for promotional purpose.

Read Product Inheritance for more information.

The user can define a special pricing in the child product and the subject product’s available and expiry dates can be specified while publishing the product to promote the subject child product for specific period.

As an illustration, consider a child product is promoted with special pricing and the product is only available between Dec 20 and Jan 31. The arrangements cannot be created under the child product post expiry date (Jan 31).

Read Product Catalogue - Proofing and Publishing for more information.


##### Relationship Pricing

The pricing strategy is based on classifying customers into groups and determining the profitability of the customer. Based on that profitability banks set their prices for services. It is an effort to reward loyalty and build long-term relationships in an increasingly competitive market

Read Configuring Relationship Pricing for more information.


##### Regional Variation

Regional pricing helps to specify a pricing plan for a particular branch in the state of a region. This hierarchy is pre-defined in the organisation hierarchy setup. It is not customer or channel specific and it allows a bank to modify their products pricing based upon the branch location.

Regional availability helps restricting a product availability at any level of the organisation and line of business.

Read Configuring Regional Pricing for more information.


##### Bundle Only Products

Read Introduction to Bundle Only for more information.


#### 🔧 Working With

The following section describes the product availability, product inheritance and promotional pricing based on customer and region with illustrations.


##### Product Availability and Product Inheritance

Products can be made available for sale only in specific channels, line of business, organisation, or region. For these products it is possible to define special pricing and discounts.

Read Introduction to Product Availability for illustrations on product availability.

Product inheritance allows the user to create a product hierarchy where the child product can be created by inheriting the parent product’s properties and its own pricing definitions for promotional purpose.

Consider the Standard Current Account product offers credit interest as below,

Consider the current system date as Apr 1, 202 2. The available and expiry dates are defined as Apr 1, 2022 and May 1, 2022 respectively in AA.PRODUCT.MANAGER to make the Special Current Account product available only for the period between Apr 1, 2022 and May 1, 2022.

Consider an instance where a Welcome Savings Account product is defined as the Bundle Only product using the Bundle Only attribute in AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER .

#### 📖 Introduction

The Regional Variation Product Line is defined with the following Property Classes to achieve regional pricing variation.

- Preferential Pricing
- Property Control

Regional pricing helps to specify a pricing plan for a particular branch in state of a region. This hierarchy is pre-defined in the organisation hierarchy setup. It is not customer or channel specific and it allows a bank to modify their products pricing based upon branch location.

Regional availability helps restricting a product availability at any level of the organisation and line of business.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The following section describes defining the organisational hierarchy and the property classes used for regional pricing.


##### Defining Organisational Hierarchy

Branch. The user creates hierarchical order of organisation levels that they prefer to use for operational benefit and profit business.

The organisation is defined by the user with the help of the ST.ORGANISATION.STRUCTURE virtual table. In this example the Division, Region, State and Branch records are user-defined.


##### Product Line

The Regional Variation Product Line is defined with the following Property Classes. Preferential Pricing Property Control

The Regional Variation Product Line is defined with the following Line Attributes: Single Group No Arrangements

This Product Line has the following unique features.

- Arrangement creation is restricted.
- The Product Line is not displayed as part of the Product Catalog.
- Only one Product Group can be created under Regional Variation.
- The IDs of the products are restricted to the IDs of records defined under ST.ORGANIZATION.CODE table.
- Parent Product is a no-input attribute and the parent is derived from the setup defined under ST.ORGANIZATION.CODE .
- The functionalities of Inheritance Only and Default Product attributes are suppressed.
- The ST.ORGANIZATION.CODE table relationship is used to proof and publish the child (until the last level) products.


##### Property Class

The following Property Classes are used to define Regional Pricing. Read Property Control Property Class for more information.

This Property Class allows replacement or merger of arrangement condition with a new condition specified. The Secondary attribute in Property Control allows no-input.

- It controls Interest, Charge, Periodic Charges and Pricing Rules Property Classes.
- Control Master has Suppress, Merge, and Replace options. Suppress – The associated Property or Property Class is suppressed at arrangement level. For Example: If Charge definition is to collect a charge of USD100 but in Property control, there is a choice as SUPPRESS at Property or Property Class level, then this charge at arrangement level is not collected. Merge - The associated Property or Property Class is merged with the condition given in Property Control. Merge functionality is similar to Merge option Property Class type. Replace - The associated Property or Property Class condition in the master arrangement is updated with the condition defined in the property condition attribute while retaining the existing arrangement's pricing rules in place.

> **⚠️ Note:** Suppress functionality is not supported by Regional Pricing. The Secondary attribute in Property Control is a no-input field for Regional Pricing Product Line.

- If the currency is not specified for a Property or a Property Class, but that Property Class is currency specific then the system creates CAT records for the currency which is specified in PRODUCT for that Property.
- If the Product attribute is blank, then the system creates a condition which is defined in Current Product Currency attribute.
- If Product is not specified, then the system creates records without currency for optional Currency Property Classes.
- CAT records are created as a part of proof and publish process, for conditions given in Property control.
- PRODUCT.NAME-PRODUCT.GROUP/PRODUCT*PROPERTY.CLASS/PROPERTY-CURRENCY-DATE is the ID of the CAT records.

#### 📖 Introduction

The Relationship Pricing Product Line allows for opening and closing of relationship pricing plan arrangements automatically or manually.

Preferential Pricing is used primarily by financial institutions, such as banks and credit unions, Relationship-Based Pricing is a competitive pricing model. The pricing strategy is based on segmenting customers into groups and determining the profitability of the customer. Based on that profitability, banks set their prices for services. It is an effort to reward loyalty and build long-term relationships in an increasingly competitive market.


#### ⚙️ Configuration

The Relationship Pricing Product Line allows for opening and closing of relationship pricing plan arrangements automatically or manually.

The main difference between Relationship arrangements (Preferential Pricing) and other types of financial arrangements is that, before opening a financial arrangement for the customer, the relationship arrangement needs to be created.

This can be automatic based on the eligibility rules or it can be created manually specifically for the customer. Therefore, when a customer opens a financial arrangement based on his eligibility and the variation and the channel is identified (for example, Variation is kept as Internet and if the customer opens a deposit product through Internet banking and eligible for HNI product), a relationship plan is already created automatically for HNI - Internet Variation. In this case the Internet Variation is selected and the preferential pricing for Interest, Charge and Bonus is given to this financial arrangement.


##### Product Line

The AA.PRODUCT.LINE table provides a high level definition of the business components (Property Classes) that may be required to construct a product belonging to that line.

- For example the RELATIONSHIP.PRICING Product Line enables the users to design and service term pricing plan products such as: HNI (High net worth individuals) Senior citizen
- The Product Lines are defined by Temenos and cannot be created by the user. A Product Line is described by the Property Classes which constitute it. A financial institution may then use these building blocks of functionality to construct the individual products which are available for sale to its customers.
- In the above example shown for relationship pricing, it is seen in total what AA.PROPERTY.CLASS records constitute a relationship pricing product. The minimum required classes are marked as mandatory Yes and optional others are marked as No.
- The mandatory classes govern the minimum required components when creating a new product in the subsequent AA.PRODUCT.GROUP and AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER records. A particular Property Class may not be mandatory at a Product Line level the option is available to further define mandatory classes at the AA.PRODUCT.GROUP stage which further controls the overall consolidated mandatory classes per product defined.


##### Property Classes Supported By Variation

The following records in AA.PROPERTY.CLASS are defined by Temenos and can be Variation applicable.

- Account
- Activity Charges
- Activity Restriction
- Charge
- Eligibility
- Interest
- Officers
- Periodic Charges
- Preferential Pricing
- Term Amount

As seen below in the Account and Eligibility examples , the Type attribute controls this with the value of Variation.


##### Properties Supported By Variation

The following section describes the properties supported by variation,

- Although Temenos defines the AA.PROPERTY.CLASS records that can be used as a Variation, another step to configure, is to set the AA.PROPERTY record also to be a Variation.
- As seen above, this Interest Property can be used as a Variation. The user may decide another version of Interest isn’t allowed to be a variation so this gives the user some level of flexibility. At the proofing and publishing stage if a Property isn’t set as a Variation, an error is shown.
- If the AA.PROPERTY.CLASS type is defined as Variation then the ID structure of the product condition has one additional component, which can accept any value defined in the EB.LOOKUP table or AA.PRODUCT.VARIATION virtual table.
- For example, the Eligibility Property type is set as Variation, then the product condition DEPOSITS.SHORT--20110414 (Default condition) should have product conditions for Branch, Internet and Mobile variations (defined in AA.PRODUCT.VARIATION virtual table).
- As shown below, the product condition ID structure is created as DEPOSIT.SHORT-BRANCH-20110414 for branch variation.
- Variation position in product condition is optional. It is allowed only when the Property Class has the Variation type.
- When a key is defined in AA.PRD.DES.XXX of a Property Class which supports variation, a validation is done to check the third position in the ID structure, whether it is a valid Variation defined in AA.PRODUCT.VARIATION virtual table.
- As shown below if the validation fails it produces an error message.

AA.PRODUCT.DESIGNER – Variations is shown below

If a product has more than one variation, the user can specify the variations and their priority order to be taken through this attribute. The available values are from the AA.PRODUCT.VARIATION virtual table as previously defined. The order in which the user specifies the variations is from top to bottom. In other words, when determining the variation to use, the system starts from the first multi-value attribute and stops when the customer is eligible.

If the customer is not eligible for a variation, then this attribute determines if there is a non-variation (Default) product. If this is checked then the default configuration cannot have eligibility, as all the customers are eligible.

Definition is allowed only for the Properties of a Property Class for which variations are defined. If the product supports multiple variations, then product conditions needs to be created for each variation. In the Property Variation attribute of the product designer, the user can select the variation it should support. Additionally, if a customer is eligible for more than one variation, then the variation to be used is determined based on the priority defined in the variation tab.

Consider a product has Internet, Branch and Mobile variations; it is possible that for one Property (for example, Principal Interest) the user can provide all three variations Internet, Branch and Mobile. But for another Property (for example, Penalty Interest) only the Internet variation is specified.

When the product with various properties (with variations against them) is proofed, the following conditions are checked:

- If a Variation is stated, then one condition has to exist for all currencies from the date on which the product is available.
- If a Variation is stated and the condition does not exist, an error is thrown during proofing stage.
- Even if Variation is stated and all variations for the product condition exist, system checks for a default condition for all of these properties. If a default condition is missing, system throws an error.
- When effective condition is stated (say FLOATING.INTEREST condition after 1Y), then variation has to exist for those conditions as well.
- If a product supports multiple currencies, then the variation condition has to be available for all currencies.
- Eligibility condition needs to have all variation conditions, stated in the Variation attribute, since this is the key Property which determines the variation itself.


##### Defining Eligibility Conditions at Product Level

The Eligibility Property holds the settings to determine whether a customer is eligible for a particular product of not. As stated before the Eligibility Property Class supports Variation type. Therefore, eligibility condition (rules) must be defined for each variation if defined in the product. If default product has been selected, the user needs to create one default eligibility product condition.

- The Eligibility conditions are defined at the product level and cannot be changed at the arrangement level as the Property Class type is set as Tracking Only.
- General or currency specific rules can be defined with their corresponding Failure Type and Failure Action.
- If either Periodic Review or Customer Static Review is checked, then a default product has to be entered to which the current eligible product moves to if the eligibility condition(s) fail while evaluation during COB. A frequency needs to be defined if Periodic Review is opted.
- Customer Static Review is triggered during COB only when there is any static change to the customer record.
- Any rule failure while customer review or periodic review during COB is updated in the ARR ELIGIBILITY record.
- A Close option is available as part of Review Failure attribute (along with Ignore and Change Product). This is applicable only for relationship pricing products and is not allowed for any other Product Line.
- When a rule is evaluated and system has Close defined, then that relationship pricing arrangement is automatically closed (using RELATIONSHIP.PRICING-CLOSE-ARRANGEMENT).
- If the user has manually created the plan, it updates in the Eligibility Review attribute in AA.ARRANGEMENT with manual. If the option is Manual, then the arrangement is not picked up for any review processing.

- Product Catalog or New Arrangement Creation
- AA evaluates eligibility criteria of each variation (For example, Internet, Branch and Mobile) in the priority order specified and it uses the first variation for which the customer is eligible.
- If the customer is not eligible for any of the variations or the default (if specified) then the Product does not appear in the customer specific version of the Product Catalog.
- The user however can open a variation manually if the eligibility rule is set to raise an override as against an error.
- When triggered by either a static change or on a period (depending on the eligibility condition) the system again checks the eligibility of each variation in order to determine which one the customer is best suited for.
- If they are eligible for a higher priority variation (that is, an upgrade) then AA triggers a Change Variation Activity and the conditions change based upon the Reset setting of each Property.
- If they are not eligible for an upgrade but they are still eligible for the current variation then no further action is performed.
- If the customer needs to be downgraded then AA triggers a Change Variation Activity to downgrade their conditions based upon the “reset” settings.
- If the customer is not eligible for any variation or the default one also, then for financial arrangements AA follows the existing rules that change the product itself to a specified product specified in Change to product without eligibility rules. In the case of a relationship pricing arrangement, if close option is selected, it automatically closes the arrangement.

Existing pricing arrangements can be reviewed to determine whether the customer is still eligible for the relationship pricing:

- Static Change – When a static change occurs (for example, a customer is no longer a staff member), the customer is no longer eligible for the preferential pricing.
- Periodically – Banks may prefer to review a customer’s relationship pricing on a periodic basis. For example, for pricing based upon a customer’s assets or salary, the bank may prefer to review the customer’s pricing on a monthly basis.
- Updated Pricing Product – As Eligibility Property is set as Tracking, and if a pricing product is re-proofed and published, the system reviews all existing pricing arrangements as the eligibility conditions might have changed (that is, rules added or removed). Based on the eligibility conditions, the customers who initially were eligible for Senior citizen plan may now be eligible for HNI product.

The list of variations supported by the product is stated in the Variation attribute (multi-valued). The order in which the values are stated, indicate the priority of eligibility as well. Therefore, the top most definition has the highest offer so that the customer gets maximum benefit.

- When the Eligibility Property type is set as Variation, and included in a product, the following is checked: When Property level variation is stated, proofing checks only for the existence of such variation as stated in the product. If nothing is stated, system does not insist on any variations for this Property.
- For a product that supports variations, bank has to define the variations that are required and whether a default condition is required, if a customer does not qualify for any variation.
- If a product is defined with three variations; Internet, Branch and Mobile, then there has to be eligibility conditions for all three variations Internet, Branch and Mobile. Default eligibility conditions should also be configured for a default product if required. Additionally, if a customer is eligible for more than one variation, a priority system is required to determine the variation that is to be used.
- For example, if two products HNI and SENIOR.CITIZEN are available in relationship pricing, then eligibility conditions with rules should be opened for all the variations that the products support.
- HNI and SENIOR.CITIZEN products support three variations that is, Internet, Branch and Mobile. Eligibility product conditions needs to be created for each variant and default Eligibility conditions should also be configured for a default product.

During Periodic Eligibility review, the system checks for eligibility again and the following events can take place as a result:

- No change in customer data, arrangement stays in the same variation.
- If any changes occur to the customer record, based on the eligibility rules the system upgrades the customer to new variation or downgrades.
- If the customer is not eligible for any variations or default condition also, then the customer arrangement changes to the product specified in Change product in Eligibility Product Condition.
- If the customer fails the eligibility rules and Eligibility Failure is set as close, then the arrangement is closed.
- When a new arrangement is created by entering the customer number and validating, the system automatically chooses the correct variation based upon the defined eligibility rules and priority specified. If at this stage the variation is manually specified for the customer, eligibility is still checked and if the customer is not eligible and the rule is configured to raise an override; the user can choose to accept it with an override message.


##### Preferential Pricing Class

The Preferential Pricing Property Class allows configuration of the preferential pricing adjustments that are available for the financial arrangement of customers who have a certain relationship with the bank.

With regards to Interest payable and due charges it defines the rules for benefits that the customer gets for his relationship with the bank

For example, if the customer qualifies for a SENIOR.CITIZEN plan, he can get a 0.50 percent enhanced interest rate on deposits.

The Charge Pricing attributes allow a bank to specify preferential pricing for debit charges. For pricing the user can specify one of the following three options:

- Discount Percentage (CHG.DISCOUNT)
- Discounted Flat Amount (CHG.CURRENCY and CHG.AMOUNT)
- Exclude from Preferential Pricing. In the case of a flat amount, the Currency attribute refers to both the currency of the arrangement as well as the currency of the charge amount.
- Product Line – It is the Product Line for which charge pricing is valid. If left blank, it indicates the definition is applicable for all Product Lines.
- Product Group – It is the Product group for which the charge pricing is valid. If left blank, it is applicable for all product groups.
- Product – It is the Product for which charge pricing is valid. If left blank, the definition is applicable for all products.
- Variation – It is the Product variation for which this charge pricing is valid. If left blank, definition is applicable for all variations of that product.
- Property – It is a debit Charge Property. If left blank the definition is applicable for all charge properties of this Product Line. The charge Property has to be a valid record in AA.PROPERTY and should not be a CREDIT Property type.
- Currency – It is the currency of the arrangement and amount.
- Percentage – If specified as 2.50 the calculated charge is reduced by 2.5% (mutually exclusive with CHG.AMOUNT). Rate attribute has to indicate the percentage value. If stated, it could not exceed 100 and could be less than 0.
- Amount – If an amount is specified it replaces the amount calculated/specified in the arrangement.
- Exclude – It allows the user to mark a Property or Currency combination to be excluded from Preferential Pricing. This can be used in the case where there is a generic setting for preferential pricing (For example, 20% for all charges) and if the user wants to exclude a specific NEWARRFEE charge from the preferential pricing then if the user selects Exclude option for NEWARRFEE charge, and it is excluded from the preferential pricing.

The Bonus Charge Pricing attributes allow the bank to specify preferential pricing for bonus (that is, Charge Property type is set to Credit).

- The attributes behave exactly like charge but with two differences: PROPERTY.TYPE must be CREDIT. Any percentage specified results in an increase in the bonus amount rather than a decrease.
- Product Line –It is the Product Line for which bonus pricing is valid. If left blank, the definition is applicable for all Product Lines
- Product Group – It is the Product group for which bonus pricing is valid. If left blank, the definitions is applicable for all product groups
- Product – It is the Product for which bonus pricing is valid. If left blank, the definition is applicable for all products.
- Variation- Product Variation for which this bonus pricing is valid. If left blank the definition is applicable for all variations of this product. Variations should be a valid record in EB.LOOKUP of AA.PRODUCT.VARIATION .
- Property – It is a Credit Charge Property. If left blank, it indicates the definition is applicable for all Charge properties of this Product or Line. If Property is selected it should be a valid record in AA.PROPERTY and has to be a CREDIT type.
- Currency – It is the currency of the arrangement and the amount specified. It is mandatory if Bonus Amount is available.
- Bonus Uplift – Percentage increase – If specified as 0.50 the calculated bonus increases by 0.50% (mutually exclusive with Bonus Amount ). If Rate attribute is indicated it cannot exceed 100 or be less than zero.
- Amount – If an amount is specified, it replaces the amount calculated or specified on the arrangement (mutually exclusive with Bonus Uplift ). The amount specified here still follows the minimum charge, Charge waive attributes and any periodic attributes of the Charge Property Class for example, if the bonus amount falls below the minimum charge, still the customer is applied minimum charge amount.
- Exclude – It allows the user to mark a Property or Currency combination to be excluded from Preferential Pricing. This can be used in the case where there is a generic setting for preferential pricing (for example, 2% increase for all bonuses) and the user wants to exclude a specific bonus (for example, New Arrangement Rebate) or currency from the preferential pricing, exclude could be selected for that charge Property to exclude it from the Preferential pricing.

The Interest Charge Pricing attributes allow the bank to specify preferential pricing for Interest.

- The Product, Property , and Exclude attributes work in exactly the same way as it is applicable for Charge and Bonus. The Currency attribute is mandatory and refers to the currency of the arrangement. Operand and Margin attributes determine the preferential pricing that is applied to the interest rate. If interest product condition in the product is set up with multiple tiers, then the margin is applicable to all the tiers.
- Product Line – It is the Product Line for which this interest pricing is applicable. If left blank, then the definition is applicable for all Product Lines.
- Product Group – It is the Product group for which this interest pricing is valid. If left blank, then the definition is applicable for all product groups.
- Product – It is the Product for which interest pricing is valid. If left blank, then the definition is applicable for all the products.
- Variation – It is the Product variation for which this interest pricing is valid. If left blank, then the definition is applicable for all variations from this product. It should be a valid record in EB.LOOKUP of AA.PRODUCT.VARIATION type.
- Property – Interest Property for which pricing is applicable. If left blank, the definition is applicable for all the interest properties of the product/line. If specified, it should be a valid record in AA.PROPERTY.
- Currency – It is the arrangement currency (it is mandatory in all cases except when Exclude is selected)
- Operand – Operand to Add, Subtract or Multiply the standard rate with the preferential margin is available.
- Margin – Preferential margin to be given.
- Exclude – It allows the user to mark a Property or Currency combination to be excluded from Preferential Pricing. This could be used in the case where there is a generic setting for preferential pricing (for example, Subtract 0.75 from all debit interest (Principal Interest) and the user wants to exclude a specific product or Property (for example, debit interest on the Mortgage cash back product) from the preferential pricing, then Exclude can be selected.

##### Financial Product Lines

Relationship pricing arrangements created for a customer have to be applied to the financial arrangements like Loans, Deposits, and Accounts. The Pricing Rules Property Class handles the rules for selecting the appropriate relationship pricing plan, and reassesses the same.


##### Pricing Rules

- When a new financial arrangement is created for a customer, it checks all the relationship arrangements of the customer based on the options stated in the Pricing Rules Property condition. It selects the right margin and updates it in the INTEREST Property, of the financial arrangement of the customer.
- It is possible to review the margins at regular intervals based on the frequency stated in the Pricing Rules.

- This is used to select a relationship pricing arrangement to assign a financial arrangement. The methods available are: Automatic – The rules in this Property determine the pricing plan to apply. Manual – It allows users to manually override this by assigning a plan manually. Automatic Or Manual – This is same as automatic, but it allows the user to override this by assigning a plan manually. In case a manually assigned plan is no longer available during a plan reset, then the arrangement goes back to automatically choosing a plan. NO.PRICING – No plan is selected and none can be entered manually. Relationship pricing is not applied to the arrangement.

- If automatic is selected in plan selection method, this attribute denotes the type of automatic selection that is done.
- Best – It uses the best plan based on a single interest Property. If there is more than one pricing arrangement with an identical best benefit, the system chooses the one which was established most recently.

- If Best is selected as the type, it specifies which arrangement interest Property (for example, Deposit Interest) is compared across eligible arrangements to determine the plan to select (that is, the best one) among the following rules: Credit Interest – Highest rate increase Debit Interest – Highest rate decrease Currently this is available only for Interest properties. If two or more plans are equal then the system automatically chooses the most recent of the pricing arrangements.
- Frequency – Frequency on which the plan has to be reassessed to apply on the financial arrangement from the customers’ current relationship plans. This provides the option for the system to periodically check that client is still on the best plan taking in to account any changes that have been made to any of the relationship plans for which the client may be eligible.
- Reset on Activity – It specifies the Activity to trigger a re-selection of the pricing plan. For example, when a Make Due Activity happens, it has to trigger a re-selection of the pricing plan.
- Once the Preferential Pricing properties have been identified the system adds the benefit or discounts at the arrangement level and shows the differences.

An example of Interest Property Class is described here. From the Product condition only 5 percent is set as default in the Fixed rate attribute.

The attributes are populated by the Relationship Pricing Product (that is, the Pricing Plan) at the financial arrangement level, followed by the operator and margin which is applied to the arrangement rate prior to each accrual. In the above case an actual rate of 5.5% is the effective rate for this deposit.

An example of Charge Property Class is described here. From the Product condition a fixed amount of USD 100 is applied.

The attributes are populated by the Relationship Pricing Product ID that is, the Pricing Plan) at the financial arrangement level and is followed by either the discount or uplift percentage. In the above case a discount of 2.5percent is applied to the USD 100 charge.


##### Activity Class Records for Relationship Pricing

Each AA.ACTIVITY.CLASS record defines the list of Actions to be applied on the given list of Property Classes for a given process in the Activity.Temenos releases AA.ACTIVITY.CLASS for Product Lines and its Property Classes or the arrangement.

When properties are linked to the AA.PRODUCT.GROUP , the system generates AA.ACTIVITY records which are Property specific named instances of AA.ACTIVITY.CLASS .The following AA.ACTIVITY.CLASS records are released for the Relationship Pricing Product Line:

- RELATIONSHIP.PRICING-NEW-ARRANGEMENT - Creates a new arrangement for relationship pricing
- RELATIONSHIP.PRICING-CLOSE-ARRANGEMENT - Activity used for closing of the arrangement
- RELATIONSHIP.PRICING-PERIODIC.ELIGIBILITY-ARRANGEMENT - Periodic review of eligibility
- RELATIONSHIP.PRICING-STATIC.ELIGIBILITY-ARRANGEMENT - Static Review of eligibility
- RELATIONSHIP.PRICING-SWITCH.AUTOMATIC-ARRANGEMENT - Activity to switch automatic mode.
- RELATIONSHIP.PRICING-SWITCH.MANUAL-ARRANGEMENT - Activity to switch manual creation
- RELATIONSHIP.PRICING-TAKEOVER-ARRANGEMENT - Activity to takeover preferential arrangement
- RELATIONSHIP.PRICING-UPDATE-CUSTOMER - Activity to update Relationship pricing
- RELATIONSHIP.PRICING-UPDATE-PREFERENTIAL.PRICING - Activity to perform update on preferential pricing Product conditions
- RELATIONSHIP.PRICING-VIEW-ARRANGEMENT - Activity to view all the properties of the arrangement
- RELATIONSHIP.PRICING-UPDATE-ACTIVITY.PRESENTATION - Activity to update the presentation screens
- RELATIONSHIP.PRICING-UPDATE-ACTIVITY.API - Activity to update Activity API routines
- RELATIONSHIP.PRICING-UPDATE-ACTIVITY.MESSAGING - Activity to update Activity Messaging


##### Automatic Arrangement Creation

In order to cater to automatic creation of Relationship Pricing arrangements the BNK/AA.RELATIONSHIP.TRACKER TSA.SERVICE needs to be started.

There are different conditions which necessitates the possible automatic creation of new pricing arrangements. Some might require online processing while others are processed during the COB.

The following section describes the online processing during creation of new pricing arrangements.

- New Customer – Whenever a new customer is created, automatically relationship arrangements can be created based on the eligibility rules set based on the customer segment. For example, eligibility rules for creation of relationship plan is set as follows: If the customer sector is 1002 (staff) then for that customer, Staff Relationship plan has to be created. If the customer age is greater than 65(Senior citizen) then for that customer, Senior Citizen relationship plan has to be created. If the customer target is three (High net worth Individuals) and salary is greater than 100,000 then HNI product has to be created.
- Customer static change – Whenever a data is changed in the customer record (that is, a static change) and if the customer is eligible for new relationship plan, then new relationship arrangement has to be created as per the eligibility rules. For example, if the customer is presently having Silver Relationship pricing arrangement, and his salary is now changed from 100,000 to 200,000, then as per the eligibility rules, the customer is now eligible for Platinum relationship product, which is opened for the customer.

New Pricing Product - If a new relationship pricing product is made available for sale, then the BNK/AA.RELATIONSHIP.TRACKER service has to reevaluate all customers to determine if any existing customers are eligible for the new relationship pricing.

For example, a new Titanium product is available for customers whose assets are greater than USD 200,000. If an existing customer, whose asset worth more than USD 200,000 currently has a Platinum Relationship arrangement, now the customer is eligible for Titanium Relationship product.

Updated Pricing product - If an existing relationship pricing product is amended and re-proofed and published, the BNK/AA.RELATIONSHIP.TRACKER service has to reevaluate all customers to determine whether they are eligible for this pricing product now.

Updated Eligibility Rule - If the eligibility rule is amended in the existing product, then the BNK/AA.RELATIONSHIP.TRACKER service should reevaluate all customers to determine whether they are eligible for this pricing product now. For example, as per the eligibility rules (Gold product = the customer should have assets worth USD 100,000). The customer’s asset is presently USD 50000 and eligible for Silver Relationship product. The customers’ asset is now increased from USD 50,000 to USD 100,000, therefore as per the eligibility rules the customer is now eligible for Gold Relationship product.

Eligibility rules for HNI Relationship product are set. The Rules Engine condition is shown below.

After authorising the customer record, the BNK/AA.RELATIONSHIP.TRACKER service evaluates the eligibility rules and automatically creates a HNI Relationship product and a Generic (Default) product for the customer.

#### 🔧 Working With

Relationship pricing is based on various relationships that a customer maintains with the bank. It refers to both the relationship and customer characteristics (for example, customer segmentation) that the bank prefers to employ.

For example, eligibility for relationship pricing plan can be based on:

- Customer’s age (for example, minors, senior citizen)
- Customer’s salary, if the customer’s salary is greater than USD 200,000 then he is eligible for High Net worth Individual (HNI) Relationship plan.
- Loyal customer (that is, length of relationship with bank)
- Customer’s sector (If sector equals to 1002(staff) then he is eligible for a Staff Relationship pricing plan, If the sector is equal to 1001 (Individual) then he is eligible for HNI Relationship Pricing plan and so on)
- 250,000 = HNI Relationship pricing plan)

This product line is a non-financial product line, which allows for definition of multiple pricing products. It also allows preferential pricing for selected segment of customers.

### 4.13  Limit Balance


> **📇 Quick Reference Card**
> 
> **Purpose:** *The Limit Property Class can maintain the balance information of total sanctioned, utilised, unutilised and excess.*
> 
> **Sections:** 📖 Introduction


#### 📖 Introduction

The Limit Property Class can maintain the balance information of total sanctioned, utilised, unutilised and excess.

- In case of a single limit, the information is maintained on the same account that is linked with the limit.
- In case of a shared limit, the user can maintain this information in one of the accounts that is linked with the limit (or) can make use of a dedicated account.

The Limit Property Class holds the account information that maintains the limit balance information.

When a limit is defined based on a time code, it is possible to maintain balance information based on time code definition. The user can choose to maintain time code balances in addition to the summary balances.

Since limit balance information is maintained as balance types, the user can calculate fees or charges corresponding to each balance. For instance, the user can calculate

- A charge on the total limit amount
- An interest on the utilised and unutilised amount
- A penalty interest on the overdrawn limit amount.
